News.title: Funeral for gangster turned author Paul Ferris takes place in Glasgow
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Mourners have paid their final respects to author and former Glasgow gangster Paul Ferris during a funeral service in the city.

The former crime boss died earlier this month at the Queen Elizabeth University Hospital (QEUH) aged 62, following a short illness, it is understood.

Family and friends assembled for the funeral, which took place on Monday at Daldowie Crematorium on the outskirts of Glasgow.

A piper guided the cortege as the hearse drove up to the entrance, bearing a coffin decorated with floral arrangements spelling out the words Dad and Legend.

open image in gallery Paul Ferris died earlier this month ( Danny Lawson/PA )

Scottish actor Paul Brannigan and former boxing champion Alex Arthur were among those present to pay their respects.

Music played during the service celebrating the life of Mr Ferris included Wish You Were Here and Coming Back to Life by Pink Floyd, Brothers in Arms by Dire Straits, Your Song by Elton John, and I Won’t Back Down by Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers.

Mr Ferris turned his back on a life of crime following a period serving time after working as an associate of Arthur “The Godfather” Thompson Sr.

open image in gallery Scottish actor Paul Brannigan was among those present to pay his respects ( PA )

Ferris was cleared of the 1991 murder of his former boss’ son, Arthur “Fat Boy” Thompson Jr.

In 1998, he was convicted of arms trafficking offences following a trial at the Old Bailey in London.

It was while serving his sentence that he co-authored his debut book, The Ferris Conspiracy, with Reg McKay, which was published in 2001.

The autobiographical book was the inspiration for the 2013 gangster film, The Wee Man, starring Martin Compston and John Hannah.

open image in gallery The family of Mr Ferris is inviting mourners to make a donation to The Invisibles, an independent group helping homeless people in Glasgow ( PA )

After seeing the film, Mr Ferris :“It was very humbling (to see the film), I thought it was an emotional rollercoaster.

“The best way was to be up front and honest about it.”

The family of Mr Ferris is inviting mourners to make a donation to The Invisibles, an independent group helping homeless people in Glasgow, according to the Naked City Facebook page, where photographer Brian Anderson first shared the news of the death of Mr Ferris.

A post on the page ahead of the service said: “As family and friends prepare to say their final goodbyes, they are asking those who wish to pay their respects to consider a gesture of kindness that could make a real difference to the lives of others.

“The family has chosen to encourage donations to The Invisibles, also known as See The Invisibles, an independent group whose volunteers work to support some of Glasgow’s most vulnerable people.”

It added: “By inviting donations in Paul’s memory his family hopes to turn a time of sadness into an opportunity to help others.”

News.title: Brick by brick: How LEGO is hooking adults on its toys
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Business is booming at LEGO thanks to an unexpected group of buyers.

The Danish toymaker saw global revenue soar by 21 percent from June to August after posting a 12-percent gain this year overall, and the company attributes some of that growth to adults buying LEGO sets for themselves.

The secret has been sets that touch on adult nostalgia and discovery, LEGO Global Chief Product & Marketing Officer Julia Goldin told The Wall Street Journal.

“Over the past eight years, we said there was a bigger opportunity with adults - not just people who are super-high-affinity fans, but people who maybe built a long time ago or had never built with bricks before - by giving them the things they would love to build now,” she said.

LEGO now offers a wide range of adult-friendly builds, including paintings like Claude Monet’s Bridge over a Pond of Water and Van Gogh’s Sunflowers; Gen X’s popular handheld Nintendo Gameboy, houseplants and a Polaroid camera.

open image in gallery LEGO sells more than 200 building kits on its website, including paintings by artists such as Van Gogh and Monet, as well as pop culture favorites like the Nintendo Game Boy and original PlayStation ( Getty Images for ReedPop )

Adults with LEGO habits include Hollywood stars such as Anna Kendrick and Daniel Radcliffe, as well as athletes such as NBA star Victor Wembanyama and Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams.

Of the more than 2,700 sets and products on the company’s website, 225 were in its “LEGO Gifts and Collectibles for Adults” section Monday. That’s 13 more than were listed in the section in early June.

Part of what has made the company popular with adults is that it markets to people’s passions, not just age and gender, Goldin said. “You might think botanicals are women and F1 cars are men,” she told The Journal.

“Yes, botanicals have a huge following among women and teenage girls, but bonsai trees are one of the top 10 products for men and teen boys. Speed Champions F1 cars show up in the top 10 for teen girls.”

Adults’ affection for LEGO brick-building is part of a wider trend in the retail industry - grown-ups are buying toys.

open image in gallery ‘[LEGO] “It's really great for people to do things with their hands. We're all on our phones so much and it's really nice to just have something that's relaxing and creative that is tactile,” music star Olivia Rodrigo said ( Getty )

Adult-only households made up 55 percent of U.S. toy sales through the first half of the year, according to a report from retail research and analysis firm Circana. Toy sales among those aged 18 and older surged 25 percent in the first half of this year compared to the same period in 2025.

"We're seeing toys increasingly function as hobbies, fandom ecosystems, and social experiences rather than traditional children's products," Circana insights boss Kristen McLean said in the study.

This summer, LEGO announced a collaboration with pop star Olivia Rodrigo - five LEGO sets have the Grammy-winning artists branding, including a guitar, flower bouquet and record player. In a July interview with Nylon, Rodrigo explained why she thinks LEGO draws in adults.

“It's really great for people to do things with their hands,” she said. “We're all on our phones so much and it's really nice to just have something that's relaxing and creative that is tactile.”

News.title: Saints players voice safety fears for Paris NFL game amid France riots
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

New Orleans Saints players have touched down in France ahead of their game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, with the civil unrest gripping Paris dominating the questions they faced on arrival.

The team landed at Charles de Gaulle airport on Monday morning. A virtual news conference followed, in which the rioting that has filled headlines and social media was addressed.

The NFL said on Sunday that “preparations continue as scheduled for NFL events and the game” at Stade de France.

Tight end Juwan Johnson said some of his family members are “very undecided" about whether to travel to Paris for the game.

“Just being safe is obviously the biggest thing,” Johnson said. "Some guys have family here. Some guys have their parents, their kids and things like that."

Johnson said his family “may be making the trip. If they do I’m sure it’ll be great. If they don’t, obviously I completely understand. We’re very undecided right now.”

Juwan Johnson admitted his family is undecided over traveling to the game ( Reuters )

Away from the match, Paris Saint-Germain have invited Saints players to attend the soccer club's Champions League game against Barcelona on Tuesday night at Parc des Princes.

Safety Justin Reid said that beyond that, he will mostly stay closer to Versailles, where the team is being accommodated.

“Keep it low-key, keep it fun, do things as a group, do things as a team and above all else stay out of the mix and don’t find any way to be a distraction to our ultimate goal here, which is to come in and put on a performance and get a win,” he said.

The NFL's statement added: "There’s been no disruption or impact at league sites.”

The Steelers, meanwhile, plan to arrive in Paris later this week.

Safety Jaquan Brisker said “it looks crazy out there. But I guess everybody has a plan.”

France is imposing curfews in several areas following riots and looting over the weekend.

French prime minister Sebastien Lecornu had originally ruled out a blanket curfew in Paris and said it was more appropriate for now to apply partial and localised curfews, without providing details. He did not rule out declaring a state of emergency in the capital.

News.title: Italy to dispatch 500 troops to 'defend Milan' after protests and looting
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Italy's government will dispatch 500 army troops to "defend Milan" after two days of unrest that saw demonstrators clash with police, loot shops and vandalise property.

The troop deployment, announced Monday by Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini, is expected to form part of a package of security measures due to go before a cabinet meeting expected Tuesday.

Luxury stores on Milan's Via Montenapoleone cleared their windows Monday and shut early, bracing for a return of the violence that hit the city over the weekend. Brands including Chanel, Tiffany and Dior took merchandise out of their displays as a precaution as police patrolled the street, where a handful of tourists looked on.

"From words to action: 500 more troops to defend Milan," Salvini, head of the co-ruling right-wing League party, wrote on social media.

open image in gallery Workers secure a shattered shop window with wooden boards following clashes between police and protesters during demonstrations over rising living costs and poor public services, in Milan, Italy, October 19, 2026 ( REUTERS )

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, who faces a national election next year, condemned the violence. She chaired a meeting with ministers and security chiefs on Monday to discuss the situation.

"The government will respond firmly to these attacks on the state, including through measures aimed at curbing violence by minors," Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani, who also serves as deputy prime minister like Salvini, wrote on X.

Corriere della Sera newspaper said Meloni was considering extending preventive detention for minors and cracking down on youth gangs as part of the planned crackdown. The measures would bring forward some provisions contained in an existing security bill currently being examined by parliament.

open image in gallery Police officers stand inside a Decathlon sporting goods store behind shattered glass during a protest over the state of public services and the rising cost of living in Milan, Italy, October 18, 2026 ( REUTERS )

The weekend trouble began as an initially peaceful demonstration on Saturday over poor public services and rising costs. However, several hundred hooded protesters, many believed to be minors, then set bins ablaze and looted shops in the city centre.

Television footage showed the ransacked stores included sports retailers Decathlon and Arc'teryx and mobile phone operator Vodafone. Stores such as clothing brands Levi's and Under Armour, as well as Decathlon, covered their shop windows with cardboard and wooden panels.

Italian police said it had detained 271 young people during unrest in Milan on Sunday. Of those taken to police stations, 32 were arrested, including 23 minors and 13 foreign nationals, police said on Monday.

open image in gallery Pedestrians walk past boarded-up Levi's and Under Armour storefronts following weekend clashes between police and protesters in Milan, Italy, October 19, 2026 ( REUTERS )

A further 28 people were reported to judicial authorities.

The unrest followed clashes on Saturday in Milan and other northern cities including Bologna, Brescia, Bergamo and Turin, where 28 protesters were arrested, according to a police report released on Sunday.

The disturbances echoed unrest in neighbouring France, where hundreds of thousands of people angered by rising living costs and declining public services took to the streets on Saturday in some of the country's most violent protests in years.

News.title: French bond sell-off spreads across Europe
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. The cost of French government borrowing has risen at the fastest pace among G7 nations after a second night of riots.

The yield on 10-year French bonds, known as OATs, climbed from 4.80pc to 4.85pc on Monday, the steepest increase among major world economies.

Bond yields are effectively the interest rate paid by governments when they borrow money by issuing bonds to financial markets.

Emmanuel Macron is facing a crisis after shops were looted and vandalised across the country.

More than 2,300 people were arrested on Saturday after protests against the cost of living and poor school conditions.

Jim Reid, an analyst at Deutsche Bank, said: “This won’t make it easy for the international community to be totally comfortable buying OATs, so the modest recovery in French spreads over the last week or so will be tested today.

“With France already facing a difficult fiscal backdrop and the 2027 election approaching, the weekend adds another layer of political risk for markets.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Burnham seeks EU embrace over AI | UK presses for access to a scheme that will prioritise investment in sovereign technology

2) Larry Ellison’s TikTok bans ad account for Musk documentary | Social media company blocks promotion for the film because of its political content

3) Profit warnings rise ahead of Budget | Most companies blame government policy and geopolitical uncertainty for worsening outlook

4) Istanbul airport stockpiles jet fuel over shortage fears | Turkish hub can sustain flights for three weeks without topping up tanks

5) GB News to launch ‘all-British’ radio station | New broadcast venture will attempt to win market share from BBC

What happened overnight

Oil prices fell more than 1pc after Donald Trump’s decision to waive sweeping sanctions on Russia.

On Friday, the President signed an executive order that delayed a wave of fresh sanctions and tariffs as they were set to take effect.

Brent crude edged down by nearly 1pc to just under $109 a barrel, with West Texas Intermediate hovered at around $101 a barrel.

Asian shares were mixed as volatility in technology stocks persisted.

South Korea’s benchmark Kospi index was up 1.1pc to 5,729.58 on Monday, after falling sharply last week. The Kospi is down more than 18pc over the past month, and still well below the 9,000 mark it crossed in June at its peak on the global AI frenzy.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 lost 0.8pc to 64,799.03. Japanese chip equipment maker Tokyo Electron lost 2.1pc, and OpenAI investor SoftBank Group dropped 3.6pc.

Hong Kong’s stock market was closed because of a holiday. The Shanghai Composite index edged 0.2pc higher to 3,722.20, after China reported better-than-expected growth of 4.5pc for its economy in the third quarter.

CXMT, China’s leading memory chipmaker, fell more than 7pc despite the company forecasting a strong profit for the first nine months.

China’s official growth data is set to be issued on Monday, giving the markets a glimpse into how the world’s second-biggest economy is faring.

The data is expected to show that China’s economy expanded by 4.4pc in the third quarter, improving on a multi-year low in Q2 but still falling just short of its annual target.

Beijing is aiming for growth of around 4.5pc to 5pc this year, which is its lowest goal in decades.

However, experts think China is on course to miss its annual economic target, weighed down by the Iran war energy shock.

China’s economy has been under pressure from mounting energy costs and faltering domestic demand. Researchers polled by AFP suggested exports were its sole outperformer.

Taiwan’s Taiex fell 1pc. Shares of Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., or TSMC, the world’s biggest contract chipmaker, were down 0.6pc. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 was 0.3pc higher at 8,832.20. India’s Sensex edged down 0.1pc.

Indonesia’s benchmark stock index fell another 5pc to its lowest level since 2020, after it plunged over 11pc on Friday following a warning from index provider MSCI that it would downgrade the country from its “emerging market” status.

News.title: Europe records highest ever number of West Nile Virus cases
News.content:
Mainland Europe has seen the largest number of cases of a debilitating mosquito-borne illness, with Italy hardest hit by the disease.

According to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control there have been 1,715 locally acquired cases of West Nile Virus so far this year, compared to 989 cases at the same point last year. Italy has been hardest hit, with 748 cases, followed by Greece with 445 cases, France with 144 and Spain with 139.

There have been 130 deaths, with the greatest number occurring in Italy, which saw 56 deaths.

The number of cases is likely to tail off over the next few weeks as the weather across Europe becomes cooler and less favourable for the Culex mosquito which spreads the disease.

West Nile Virus is in the same family of viruses as dengue, yellow fever and Japanese encephalitis. It causes flu-like symptoms and sometimes vomiting and diarrhoea but in around one in 150 cases it can develop into a disease that affects the brain and nervous system and can be fatal. There is no vaccine or treatment.

The disease is widespread in birds, but humans can only acquire it if they are bitten by an infected mosquito. The disease does not spread from human to human. Most cases of severe disease occur in older people and those with weakened immune systems.

News.title: Arsenal late show keeps heat on Man City
News.content:
In the ordinary course of a Premier League season, you would say Manchester City have applied pressure on Arsenal by opening up a six-point lead before the champions play at Nottingham Forest this afternoon.

This is not a normal Premier League season though, and we await to discover if the top of the league table is simply a mirage.

Regardless, Mikel Arteta and his Arsenal players have their own motivations to accumulate as many points as possible before January as they seek to retain the title for the first time since the 1930s.

Arsenal have struggled at the City Ground, drawing 0-0 on their last two Premier League visits. They also lost at Forest in May 2023, a result which confirmed Manchester City as champions at Arsenal’s expense, and were knocked out of the FA Cup by Forest in January 2022.

Forest are yet to score a home league goal under Oliver Glasner, another data point suggesting this will be a low-scoring game.

That might not be the full story though, with Forest creating a hatful of chances in their defeat at Crystal Palace last week and Arsenal also playing a more inventive, technical game with the ball so far this season.

Arsenal have yet to score from a non-penalty set-piece, and their percentage of goals from open play is now the highest in the Premier League.

Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt after sustaining what Glasner described as a “minor muscle injury” at Palace and his involvement in the game will be a last-minute call. With the exception of Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie and long-term absentee William Saliba, Arsenal’s squad is in pretty good health. Bukayo Saka, Martin Odegaard, Kai Havertz, Riccardo Calafiori and Ben White could be recalled to Arteta’s starting XI after starting the Champions League win over Lille on the bench.

Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Slow and dull Man Utd are just not good enough
News.content:
Manchester United are like John Toshack’s duvet. You fix one problem – being far too vulnerable to conceding goals – only to create another – lacking the threat to score. It is all very Meh United not Man United. The indisputable fact is they are just not very entertaining to watch. They are slow and dull.

In the end it also points to another thing. The thing highlighted in midweek by Lisandro Martínez after the Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid: they do not have the strength in depth to compete.

What they do have appears to not be fit for purpose. Certainly Michael Carrick, the under-pressure manager, is struggling to get the best out of the resources he has.

“It’s like a duvet,” Toshack, the former Real Madrid and Wales manager, famously said of football. “If you pull it up, your feet get cold. If you pull it down, your shoulders get cold.”

There will have been times in the last few days, with the intense criticism and scrutiny over his future, when Carrick will have simply felt like dragging that duvet up over his head and keeping it there.

Defeat by Leeds United would have been unthinkable. It would have put Carrick under potentially intolerable pressure in what appears to be a pivotal week, with Como away in the Champions League and a home Premier League fixture against Bournemouth in the coming days.

Was this a lifeline or the tightening of the noose for Carrick? Time will soon tell. The relief of avoiding defeat was tempered by the reality of it now being just one win in their opening seven league games – at home to newly promoted Ipswich Town – and they are down in 13th place. It is six games without a win in all competitions.

News.title: Pierre Sage fears for his Crystal Palace future after Brighton humiliation
News.content:
Pierre Sage has admitted that he fears for his future at Crystal Palace, adding that he felt “shame” after his side slumped to their joint-heaviest defeat by rivals Brighton and Hove Albion.

Sage replaced Oliver Glasner as manager in June but since then Palace have won just two league matches with him in at the helm. The south London club have taken seven points from seven Premier League games and have already conceded 17 goals, the most of any team in the league.

“I don’t know,” Sage said when asked if he will get enough time to rectify Palace’s slump. He admitted that his shame was about how Palace were overwhelmed, leaking three goals within the first nine minutes of the game before eventually losing 5-0.

“We are not at the level we expected, and I’m really sorry for that,” the 47-year-old said. “I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face.”

The Frenchman said that he took full responsibility for the 5-0 defeat, and understood why hundreds of Palace fans left well before the final whistle.

News.title: Ruthless Daniel Dubois dispatches Fabio Wardley in just two rounds
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley.

When Wardley dragged himself out of the ring at Manchester’s Co-Op LIVE Arena, the physical damage was obvious, but the psychological sting was far deeper. Wardley had Dubois severely hurt early on, flooring the Londoner twice and teetering on the verge of a career-defining stoppage. Instead, he let the knockout slip away, allowed Dubois to find his rhythm, and was ultimately broken down and halted in the 11th round - surrendering his WBO heavyweight belt in a dramatic comeback victory.

Now, just five months after that gruelling night, the two heavyweights meet again at London’s O2 Arena in an immediate rematch that carries potentially massive implications for the entire division.

For Wardley (20-1-1, 19 KOs), the decision to trigger his rematch clause was instant. Dismissing concerns over the severe punishment he absorbed down the stretch, the Ipswich man is motivated entirely by redemption and the belief that his early success proved Dubois is beatable.

Dubois (23-3, 22 KOs), however, views things very differently. Entering as The Ring’s No. 1 heavyweight contender and a proven two-time world champion, Dubois has brushed off Wardley’s power, claiming his rival “punches like a baby” and insists Wardley threw away his one and only chance at glory in Manchester.

With Oleksandr Usyk approaching the final chapter of his career and the Anthony Joshua vs. Tyson Fury blockbuster looming just eight weeks away, this London clash is far more than a personal grudge match. The winner won’t just walk away with the WBO strap; they will stake an undeniable claim as the torch-bearer for the heavyweight division’s next era if they can land another title fight in short order.

News.title: Newcastle jeers tell Matthias Jaissle his ‘vertical’ football is not working
News.content:
Newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

News.title: Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card
News.content:
Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

But as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

Sports.title: Former Premier League ace who made history with Newcastle leaves role as Darlington manager after horror start to season
Sports.content:
Next

NEWCASTLE icon Steve Watson has been sacked by National League North strugglers Darlington.

The former right-back, 52, made 351 Premier League appearances during his stunning career.



But Watson has been axed after a 2-1 defeat to AFC Telford United left Darlington four points adrift of safety.

And chairman David Johnston reckons a new boss is needed to kickstart the Quakers’ season following a horrific start.



In a club statement, he said: “Darlington Football Club can confirm that Steve Watson will leave his role as first team manager with immediate effect.

“The decision was reached by mutual agreement between the Darlington FC directors and Steve following discussions over the past few days.



“Steve leaves with our gratitude for his leadership, dedication and commitment over nearly three years as first team manager.

“However, the club and Steve have agreed that now is the right time to appoint a new manager to take the club forward. We wish Steve every success for the future.

“In the meantime, Terry Mitchell will lead the team as caretaker manager while the club conducts its search for a suitably qualified replacement.”

Watson took charge of Darlington in December 2023 and managed to steer the non-league minnows clear of the dreaded drop zone.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But, despite penning a new two-year deal in March, he was been dismissed with just a point separating the Quakers from the foot of National League North.

Watson is still Newcastle’s youngest ever player after making his debut aged 16 years, seven months, and nine days old against Wolves in 1990.

The St James’ Park hero went on to make 258 appearances for his boyhood club.

He notched 14 goals along the way and narrowly missed out on FA Cup glory when he reached the final with Alan Shearer and Co in 1998.



Watson went on to have spells with Aston Villa, Everton and West Brom before hanging up his boots while on Sheffield Wednesday’s books.

And the ex-defender bossed Gateshead, York and Chester prior to heading into the Darlington dugout.

Sports.title: All the mad things Erling Haaland spends his money on from £100k book he can’t read to stuffed squirrels
Sports.content:
Next

ERLING HAALAND is the highest paid Premier League football with an estimated salary of £525,000-per-week.

His incredible wages have meant that he has been able to enjoy all the trappings of a wealthy footballer.



That includes an amazing car collection that’s worth around £10million.

And, on top of his motors, the Norwegian hotshot has built an impressive property empire, including recently adding an island pad to his portfolio.



But, for all those investments made with an eye on the future, there have been some pretty daft purchases too.

SunSport looks at the strange things Haaland, 26, has spent his mega fortune on.

A £100,000 book he never read

Haaland, himself, admitted he wasn’t much of a reader, which makes this one even more bizarre.

Back in March, the Man City striker broke the auction record for the most expensive Norwegian book ever sold.

He splashed around £100,000 on a rare 1594 edition of Snorre Sturlason’s Royal Sagas.

Haaland immediately donated the historic text to a public library in his home region, Time, where it is on display – meaning he can’t actually read it.



He said: “I’ve been lucky enough to live out my dream through football.

“I know not everyone gets that chance. Books give so many more people the chance to dream big, see new possibilities and find their own path.”

Incidentally, the book is about the history of medieval Norse kings, featuring stories of Viking kings, queens, farmers and warriors.



Cowboy get-up

It’s not the sort of look you’d rock in Alderley Edge, to be fair. Maybe a saloon bar in Austin or Dallas, mind.

But, Haaland really made a name for himself during the 2026 World Cup in the USA and Mexico.

So, he thought he would celebrate with some outlandish presents.

He dropped into Wild Bills’ Western Store in Dallas and let his credit card go wild.

He was fitted for custom cowboy hats, splashing the cash on a Stetson beaver fur felt headpiece that costs around £1,950, and three other bits of headwear.



Haaland also bought a longhorn belt buckle for around £100 and the viral “Y’all can kiss my Dallas” T-shirt for £25, as well as plenty of cowboy boots, western shirts, and hip flasks.

It was reported he dropped about £7,500 in Wild Bills, but that wasn’t all.

Stuffed animal, anyone?

Some might say more money than sense. But we commend Haaland and his outlandish spending.



During his Dallas splurge, with some items generously bought for his Norway teammates, the Golden Boot winner made his most whackiest purchases yet.

They were of the stuffed animal variety and pretty specific in design.

He purchased a taxidermy racoon holding a bottle of liquor that cost him around £564.

Perhaps fearing it might get lonely, he added two friends – a pair of stuffed squirrels costing around £677.



Inexplicably, one of those squirrels was dressed as a sheriff.

When Haaland returned home from the US, following Norway’s exit from the World Cup, he was spotted exiting a plane proudly clutching his raccoon.

Handbag collection

Now, Haaland fancies himself as a bit of a fashionista.

In the past, we’ve seen him wearing silk pyjama sets and matching lounge outfits from Dolce & Gabbana.



Haaland frequently attends high-profile D&G events, including the Alta Sartoria show in Taormina, Sicily, where he wore an ivory double-breasted silk suit with a draped scarf and jewelled frog brooch. Yes, his style is equally as out-there.

It’s his handbags, though, we’re particularly focused on.

Astonishingly, it has been reported that Haaland has a £1million luxury holdall collection.

Forget being a Viking boy, he’s a Birkin boy, spending a fortune on Hermés bags.

From the £60,000 The Endless Road HAC 50 Bag, 2024 to their Limited Edition Caban Togo Multipockets HAC Birkin 50, 2025 costing £50,000, Haaland embraces Hermés’ man bags.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Collecting dust in, we imagine, his substantially large Cheshire mansion wardrobe, are also handbags from Louis Vuitton, Goyard and Tom Ford.

All these things just have you asking one, simple question… what will he buy next?

Sports.title: Video of man kicking rugby ball from roof terrace towards pitch during Brentford vs Liverpool sparks police hunt
Sports.content:
Next

POLICE are on the hunt for the man who punted a rugby ball towards the Gtech Community Stadium from the top of a nearby roof terrace.

Video footage has emerged on social media of a guy booting the item from a significant height over a glass barrier, which then hit the roof of the East Stand during a Premier League match.



It is believed to have occurred in the second half of Brentford’s 2-1 defeat to Liverpool on Saturday.

It is not known if the ball then landed on the pitch or even struck somebody in the crowd.



Brentford condemned the behaviour as “dangerous and potentially very harmful”.

And the West Londoners said they were “supporting a police investigation” in their ongoing enquiries.

A caption that accompanied the video said “someone on a Brentford rooftop tried to join the Premier League game below”.

Individuals in the video, whose faces are obscured, can be heard laughing and screaming as the projectile was launched towards the ground.

In a statement, the Bees said: “Brentford Football Club is aware of an incident involving an item being kicked from a height towards the field of play during Saturday’s match against Liverpool.

“Such behaviour is dangerous and potentially very harmful.



“The matter has been referred to the police and the club is supporting the relevant authorities in their investigation to help identify those responsible and take appropriate action, which may result in criminal prosecution.

“The matchday safety of fans, staff, players and officials is of utmost importance, and the club will support all efforts to ensure action is taken.”

A Metropolitan Police spokesperson said: “Police are aware of an incident which occurred during the Brentford v Liverpool match on Saturday 17 October, where an item was kicked towards the pitch.

“Officers are making enquiries to establish if any offences have been committed.”

Sports.title: Man Utd legend teases ‘there’s only one job Cristiano Ronaldo would take to become a manager’
Sports.content:
Next

TEDDY SHERINGHAM reckons there’s only one job Cristiano Ronaldo would take if he is to become a manager.

With Ronaldo turning 43 in February, many people are speculating how long he has left and what he will do next.



Former Manchester United striker Sheringham thinks it unlikely he will move into management.

He told BetVictor: “I can’t see Cristiano Ronaldo being a manager, 24 hours a day, seven days a week.”



However, Sheringham believes that the Portuguese icon could be tempted by one role: “One exception could be the Portugal job”.

Ronaldo has made Portugal one of the most feared nations in football after his debut in 2003.

Before CR7 arrived on the scene, Portugal had never won a major trophy.

Since his debut in 2003, Portugal have won three – including the Euros in 2016.

Ronaldo is one of the most talked about athletes in the world and him taking over as Portugal boss one day would send shock waves through the footballing world.

The Portuguese star recently considered retirement from international football following the 2026 World Cup.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

However he decided to continue, but then had an altercation with current boss Jorge Jesus that saw him quit the latest Portugal camp.

He is currently provisionally suspended while the Portuguese FA determine his punishment for walking out after being an unused substitute.

Despite his playing career slowing down, Ronaldo is finding other ways to immerse himself in the beautiful game having invested a 25 per cent stake in UD Almeria.

Sheringham believes due to his immense popularity, being a manager could prove difficult.



The former England striker said: “Football has consumed his life and wherever he goes, its non-stop for him. Same as David Beckham.

“Most footballers or ex-footballers are allowed to switch off at certain times, but when you’re at the top of your game, like Beckham and Ronaldo, you can’t do that.”

Sports.title: Chris Kamara risks wife's fury with incredible new challenge after Great North Run collapse
Sports.content:
Chris Kamara risks wife's fury with incredible new challenge after Great North Run collapse

Sky Sports great and football fan favourite Chris Kamara has taken on another audacious charity challenge, not long after he collapsed during the Great North Run

View Image Chris Kamara has taken on another ambitious challenge despite his recent scare at the Great North Run (Image: Prostate Cancer UK/PA Wire)

Chris Kamara has announced his next great charity endeavour as part of a 500-mile run for Children In Need. That's despite his recent collapse at the Great North Run as he aims to raise money for charity in a growing list of fitness-related challenges.

‌



‌



Kamara, who was diagnosed with speech apraxia and dyspraxia in 2022, gave his wife, Anne, and two sons a scare after falling at the Great North Run. The former Sky Sports Soccer Saturday favourite ran the half marathon alongside one of his sons, Jack, as well as friend and fellow broadcaster Ben Shepherd.

‌



In the wake of his apraxia diagnosis, Kamara had to relearn how to run as the neurological condition affected his speech, balance and movement. Explaining his fall at the finish line, he said his "legs couldn't believe it...and then they collapsed below me."

‌



Barely one month after pulling off that feat, Kamara has now signed up for a Children In Need challenge before the end of the year. He and Olympian Jonny Brownlee will help children at Outwood Primary Academy Lofthouse Gate in Wakefield run 500 miles combined over four hours on November 10.

Kamara is also gearing up to run the 2027 London Marathon in another bid to raise funds for charitable causes. And he told the BBC that his spouse raised objections to the idea, as the 68-year-old plans to participate in the Run for Pudsey.

‌

"Although my wife says 'no', tell her I'm hoping to run the London Marathon," said Kamara. "She'll hate me actually revealing this, because I collapsed after the Great North Run.

"Thankfully, it was when I was over the line. If I stay fit, I could possibly do the London [Marathon] and this run with Jonny Brownlee and the kids from Outwood Primary will be another step in my fitness [journey]."

The Run for Pudsey is an initiative aimed at encouraging children to get outdoors and take part in physical activity. That's in addition to the potential fundraising benefits it will contribute towards Children In Need.

"We don't see loads and loads of kids out playing football these days," Kamara continued. "We see them on their computers and iPads...anything that encourages them to get outside and do stuff is so important."

Sports.title: Enzo Maresca confirms huge Man City injury blow and gives Erling Haaland update
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca confirms huge Man City injury blow and gives Erling Haaland update

Erling Haaland came off limping after Manchester City's 3-2 win against Ipswich, making him the latest of several injury concerns for Enzo Maresca before their Champions League clash with AEK Athens

View 2 Images Erling Haaland was in pain after Manchester City beat Ipswich (Image: Neal Simpson/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Enzo Maresca has confirmed that Erling Haaland is available to face AEK Athens - but Manchester City team-mate Antoine Semenyo will be out for around eight weeks. City striker Haaland was seen limping at the end of Saturday's dramatic 3-2 victory over Ipswich.

‌



‌



Before the win, Maresca revealed that he may be forced to take the 26-year-old out of his starting line-up to avoid injury. But Haaland wasn't the only concern from the Ipswich match. Matheus Nunes and Mateo Kovacic both came off injured during the second half, while Semenyo picked up a knock after coming on as a late substitute.

‌



Ahead of City's game at home to Athens on Tuesday, Maresca provided an update by telling a press conference: "He (Haaland) can be available. We will see.

‌



"We have a session now. We have some doubts after Saturday's game. He was quite good yesterday, better. The rest are more or less okay. The only one that will be out for probably eight weeks is Antoine.

"In the first moment we expect an even worse injury so we were more worried but after the scan we are less worried. It could be eight weeks. Now the most important thing is to recover it. When he is back, around December, we have a new player. It's not muscular."

"To lose Antoine, or any player, is not good. In terms of Erling, we said we can use Antoine as a nine but we have different players to try. We will see, at the moment it is Erling, we don't need to think about another one."

Maresca went on to explain how players like Haaland and Semenyo - who featured at the World Cup - will need to be managed. "We need to pay attention to workloads," the City boss continued.

‌

"That is why we will do some changes tomorrow. Try and keep players fit. Some things are out of our control, like Antoine.

"Antoine was one of the players we wanted to rest, he played 10-15 minutes, and then he got injured. We need to pay attention [to the World Cup players]."

Sports.title: Ezri Konsa relishing Harry Kane duel as he bids to help Arsenal end Champions League hoodoo
Sports.content:
Ezri Konsa relishing Harry Kane duel as he bids to help Arsenal end Champions League hoodoo

Ezri Konsa already looks like one of the signings of the season and is determined to help Arsenal keep up their clean sheet record

View 3 Images Konsa helped Arsenal to victory at Nottingham Forest on Sunday (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Ezri Konsa is living out his boyhood dreams with Arsenal - and is “hungry” to help them win more trophies.

‌



‌



Gunners defender Konsa grew up as an Arsenal fan, wore the shirts as a kid and jumped at the chance to join close friends at the Emirates in the summer.

‌



Konsa is already looking like one of the signings of the season after his £55m move from Aston Villa but he is also determined to help Mikel Arteta ’s men lift more silverware.

‌



England centre half Konsa won the Europa League with Villa last season and is now eyeing the Champions League ahead of Wednesday’s trip to face Bayern Munich.

When asked whether he grew up as an Arsenal fan, Konsa said: “I’ve been asked this a lot! Yes, I was. I had a lot of Arsenal kits when I was younger. It’s been posted everywhere, so … To answer that question, yes I was.”

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

You could see how much it meant to Konsa when he was filmed arriving at the Arsenal training ground after joining the club to be greeted by close pal Eberechi Eze.

Was it a dream come true? “Of course, man. You dream of playing for big clubs like this,” said Konsa.

‌



“When you’re a kid, you see the likes of Arsenal, growing up, and the amount of quality players they’ve had throughout the years and to be here, and not only to be here but to be here with close friends makes it even more special.”

That has undoubtedly helped Konsa slot straight in to be surrounded by England team mates and his outstanding performance against Nottingham Forest on Sunday - typified by a brilliant late challenge on Liam Delap - has helped him fit in straight away.

Arsenal have kept four clean sheets in their first seven Premier League games and Konsa has formed a formidable partnership with Gabriel in the absence of injured William Saliba.

‌



Konsa said: “As a centre-back, I look forward to playing against the best. In the Premier League, every striker’s got their own qualities and are really good.

“Liam Delap was good at times, held up the ball well and is a very physical striker. I relish those challenges, the last-ditch tackles, I’ve done it a few times before.

View 3 Images Living the dream: Arsenal fan Ezri Konsa with close pal Eberechi Eze (Image: Stuart MacFarlane/Arsenal FC)

‌



“Look, it’s a good tackle but sometimes you get caught out of position, and you have to recover and make that kind of tackle. In hindsight, I could be in a better position to avoid those sort of challenges but always nice when it pulls off.

“Everyone knows about Arsenal’s record last season and how good they are at keeping clean sheets. It’s something that I wanted to do, to continue. One of the reasons I joined the club was to carry on keeping clean sheets. We’re doing all right so far. So long may it continue.”

Arsenal won the title last season but lost the Champions League final in heartbreaking fashion to Paris Saint Germain in a penalty shootout. They face a major test against Harry Kane ’s Bayern on Wednesday.

‌



Konsa is determined to back up his Europa League success with Villa by helping Arsenal go one better this season as well as lifting more trophies.

He added: “That’s the plan. When I came here, I wanted to win. I was hungry to win. Last season I got my hands on the Europa League and this season I want more.

“Bayern have got a great team. We know how tough it’s going to be, going away to the Allianz but we’ll be ready.

‌



View 3 Images Konsa and Kane will go head to head on Wednesday (Image: The FA via Getty Images)

“Harry’s a striker who can drop deep, go into midfield, he can drag you around and can assist, he can score, he has all the qualities a top striker needs. We know it’s going to be a tough game.

“I played against him when he was at Bayern two seasons ago in the Champions League. We won. I don’t really look much at those kind of stats but I’m relishing the challenge.

Article continues below

"The boys went all the way last season, just couldn’t get it over the line, lost in a penalty shoot-out. As players, the standards we have, the goals we have… we want to win everything, we want to win the Champions League. The Prem.

“We want to win whatever trophies are in front of us. As players, that’s something we are going to strive towards and hopefully we can win a few titles this season.”

Sports.title: Man Utd players claim they have been banned from interviews by club after Martinez outburst
Sports.content:
Man Utd players claim they have been banned from interviews by club after Martinez outburst

It comes after Lisandro Martinez's explosive interview in the wake of United's defeat by Atletico Madrid in the Champions League last week

View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes was among the players who declined to speak to media after the Leeds game (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United players claimed they had been gagged by the club following Sunday's 1-1 draw at Leeds United. It is common for United players to speak to members of the written press in the mixed zone after games, especially after a positive performance.

‌



‌



However, after the match at Elland Road, despite being asked by reporters to stop, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha said they weren't allowed to speak.

‌



It follows Lisandro Martinez's explosive TV interview after United's 2-0 Champions League defeat to Atletico Madrid, in which he tore into the club's hierarchy, including director of football Jason Wilcox, for the club's perceived lack of summer transfer business.

‌



Martinez, who was fined for the outburst, subsequently apologised after clear-the-air talks with the club and played against Leeds. He received support from travelling United fans, who chanted "Argentina, Argentina, Argentina" from the away section, only to have to come off at half-time with an injury.

Man Utd may be rushed to appoint Michael Carrick's successor as new twist emerges READ MORE :

The silence from United players after the Leeds game suggests they have been asked by the club not to speak for fear of more Martinez-style tirades. However, it is understood that there had been no direct order from the club's media team for players to refrain from engaging with written reporters after the match.

Harry Maguire spoke to the club's official website after the game. He said: "You can't question the togetherness, the spirit and the fight. This is a tough place to come. Leeds have been flying in the league.

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"We can be better. We have to show more quality with the ball. When you come to places like this, you can't be beaten on set-plays and we conceded a set-play which got them back in the game.

"Throughout, we felt comfortable in our shape. They didn't create too many chances. To concede a set-piece after half-time is disappointing. We had to dig in. We got a foothold at about 70 minutes and probably looked the more likely to go and win it, but a draw is probably fair."

‌



View 3 Images The silence from the players followed Lisandro Martinez's explosive interview (Image: Florencia Tan Jun - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

Meanwhile, Michael Carrick claims the performance felt like a "fresh start." The United boss said: "We're not getting too carried away because we haven't won the game. I think if you keep doing the right things for the right reasons, then you get what you deserve in the end."

The draw extended United's winless Premier League run to five matches – their only win was against newly-promoted Ipswich in August – while they have won just two of their 10 games in all competitions.

Article continues below

View 3 Images Carrick was satisfied with the performance (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Not since the end of the 2018-19 season have United gone six games in all competitions without a win and it is 40 years since they won only one of their first seven top-flight games at the start of a season.

Carrick's side travel to Italy to face Cesc Fabregas's Como on Wednesday in their third Champions League game of the season before returning to Premier League action on Sunday against Bournemouth at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Sir Jim Ratcliffe 'kills' Man Utd transfer agreed by Jason Wilcox - 'It's a mess'
Sports.content:
Sir Jim Ratcliffe 'kills' Man Utd transfer agreed by Jason Wilcox - 'It's a mess'

Manchester United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe reportedly blocked one of Jason Wilcox's transfer targets at Old Trafford

View 2 Images Manchester United chiefs Jason Wilcox and Sir Jim Ratcliffe have reportedly had differences of opinion behind the scenes (Image: (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images))

Manchester United minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe reportedly 'killed' the chances of the club moving to sign one unnamed signing this summer. Sporting director, Jason Wilcox, has come under fire in recent weeks following Lisandro Martinez's bombshell interview, taking aim at the transfer chief for this summer's business.

‌



‌



United were looking to address their midfield engine room this summer, with Elliot Anderson among the potential targets. Wilcox is understood to have been a huge admirer of the England international, who joined rivals Manchester City from Nottingham Forest for £116m earlier this summer.

‌



However, the club decided against signing the former Newcastle United midfielder, bringing in Carlos Baleba for £70m, Andrey Santos for £50m and Youri Tielemans for £35m.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

According to the Daily Mail, Ratcliffe's strict budget meant a move for Anderson was not financially viable given the restraints the club are working under. United were able to bring in two midfielders for the price of Anderson, with money left over for Baleba.

‌



In the aforementioned report, one agent described Wilcox's position as 'incredibly difficult' with growing pressure on the United transfer chief following the disappointing summer transfer window.

Speaking to the Daily Mail, one agent said: "Jason is in an incredibly difficult position. Everybody would think he’s the decision-maker at the club, but he absolutely isn’t.

"Manchester United is run by the owners, Sir Jim and the Glazers. If you sack Wilcox, nothing will change. It’s a mess." Another said: "We had a deal agreed with Jason and then Jim got involved and tried to change it. He ended up killing it."

‌



View 2 Images Jason Wilcox brought Carlos Baleba to Manchester United in the summer window (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Wilcox was the target of a furious rant from Martinez after defeat to Atletico Madrid in the Champions League last week.

The Argentinian defender said: "I have to control myself a lot. But sometimes it's a reflection of how our club is at the moment, you know?

Article continues below

"We did a fantastic season last season, and now we expect more from the top, from above, you know, to bring more players to compete, because many, many teams bring many players in as well, and today also, Atletico have an amazing team, and they deserved to win today."

"I expected more from our technical director. I have to be honest, you know? And also, as players, we have to do more, but it's also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for these kinds of nights."

Sports.title: Gary Neville thinks Man Utd dressing room have 'definitely had a tear up'
Sports.content:
Gary Neville thinks Man Utd dressing room have 'definitely had a tear up'

Manchester United drew 1-1 with Leeds United and Gary Neville believes there's been a 'tear up' in the dressing room

View 2 Images Gary Neville believes Manchester United players have had a 'tear up' following Lisandro Martinez's bombshell interview (Image: Sky Sports Gary Nevillle Podcast)

Former Manchester United defender Gary Neville believes there's 'definitely' been a 'tear up' in the United dressing room after Lisandro Martinez's explosive interview following the defeat to Atletico Madrid.

‌



‌



The Argentinian defender came out swinging in his post-match interview, taking a swipe at sporting director Jason Wilcox, claiming there should have been more investment during the summer transfer window.

‌



United teammate Amad also found himself in hot water, with a cryptic social media post after the defeat to Atleti midweek, with the words "F***ing disgrace. I have no words."

‌



Head coach Michael Carrick said on Friday that it was intended as a message to back Martinez, but he called on Amad to use the passion and emotion in the right way.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Speaking on the Gary Neville podcast after the 1-1 draw with Leeds, the former United captain said: "They still have to finish fifth. Today's a stepping stone, but we can't get carried away.

"I mean, it's because of what we thought might happen before. I actually thought they'd win today, I thought there would be a response.

"I think that dressing room's definitely had a... I think they've had a tear-up and they've had a meeting, 100 per cent.

‌



"There's no way they've not dealt with that Martinez issue. If you think about Amad Diallo's Snapchat, saying 'You're an effing disgrace.'

View 2 Images Lisandro Martinez let rip after Manchester United's Tuesday night defeat (Image: Bradley Collyer/the Press Association)

‌



"Well, that's at his team-mate. So they're obviously launching each other, I think it's got a bit about him, Amad, to be fair. So has Martinez, Martinez has got something about him.

"He's gone rogue, but so has Amad. You're an effing disgrace, that's what's happening here, that's the dynamic. Well, that can only be a good thing for Michael Carrick.

"Because you're looking at it and thinking, he needs something. He needs somebody to start fighting back, he needs something to cause a moment.

Article continues below

"He needs something, he needs a rocket up it. So, yeah, maybe that's the turning point. Maybe Lisandro Martinez has done the best motivational speech that he's ever done for Manchester United on Tuesday night. Maybe he's done them a favour."

Sports.title: Kai Rooney shares update as he bounces back from Man Utd heartbreak in perfect way
Sports.content:
Kai Rooney shares update as he bounces back from Man Utd heartbreak in perfect way

The 16-year-old son of Manchester United legend Wayne made his Premier League 2 debut on Friday as part of a busy weekend

View 2 Images Kai Rooney had a busy weekend playing for Manchester United (Image: Manchester United, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Kai Rooney, the son of Manchester United legend Wayne, has posted a message after responding to his Under-21s debut in the perfect way. The 16-year-old made his bow in Premier League 2 on Friday.

‌



‌



After making his way through the youth teams at United, he was part of the squad for the match against Nottingham Forest at Loughborough University. He was given a chance to make an impression when he was brought on with 12 minutes left to play.

‌



At that time, the scoreline was 2-2, with United hoping that Rooney could help them to push for a winner. But, the game went the opposite way as Forest scored late to record a 3-2 win as he suffered late heartbreak.

‌



The loss was the United development squad's first of the campaign in Premier League 2, having clinched victories in their opening three fixtures against Ipswich Town, Leicester City and Brentford. However, Rooney, had little time to think about the setback.

Howard Webb discloses double Man Utd contact after major VAR error READ MORE :

Harry Maguire makes worrying admission about Man Utd players and Lisandro Martinez claim READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Despite featuring for the U21s on Friday, he was straight back into the starting line-up for the club's U18s the following day as they too faced Nottingham Forest. Rooney got himself on the scoresheet to hand United the advantage in the first half.

‌



He was substituted in the 66th minute, but United were unable to hold on for all three points. Forest drew level in the 78th minute, with the match finishing 1-1.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Following the double header, Rooney took to social media to respond to his goal, sharing a picture of his celebration alongside a caption reading: "back on the scoresheet.'. It's been a busy few weeks for Rooney as he made his U19s debut just last week.

‌



He came on as a second-half substitute in the UEFA Youth League clash against Atletico Madrid, a game which United lost 3-0.

He signed a two-year scholarship with the club back in July. The deal can turn into a three-year professional deal worth around £50,000 per year, plus an annual signing-on fee.

View 2 Images Kai Rooney has come up through the Manchester United youth ranks (Image: Manchester United, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



As Rooney was starting to make his own way in football, it had previously been revealed by his mum, Coleen, that he had to ban his dad from attending matches.

As Rooney began carving out his own path in football, his mum, Coleen, had previously revealed that he was forced to ban his father from watching him play. "Kai told Wayne to stop coming to football games, when he played grassroots tournaments and stuff because he used to get swarmed and he couldn't even watch the game," she said on I'm a Celebrity...Get Me Out of Here in 2024.

"How do you say to all of these kids, 'Go away, I'm watching my son?' Adults, it's different, you could speak to them. So he (Kai) just said, 'Oh, dad there's no point you coming because you don't even watch me play anyway.' Which is sad, but it can't be helped anyway. At the same time, the fans help you along the way and get you where you are."

Article continues below

Wayne has, however, since been spotted at matches, suggesting that the ban has now been lifted.

Sports.title: Ronaldo punished over Portugal walkout with fine he can pay off in 39 seconds
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days and fined £215 over his walkout from the Portugal national team following an explosive fallout with head coach Jorge Jesus.

The Portuguese FA's disciplinary council did not specify when Ronaldo's ban begins, but Sky Sports News understands it is enforced from the date he left the squad's training camp in Denmark on September 30.

It means the 41-year-old former Manchester United and Real Madrid star is available to play in Portugal's Nations League matches next month against Denmark and Wales if he is called upon by Jesus.

Ronaldo accused Jesus of broken promises and a "breach of trust" over his involvement in the team. The new head coach denied there had been any agreement.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player ICYMI: Ronaldo's extraordinary letter airing his problems with Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus explained

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner asked to be punished by the Portuguese FA when he posted a lengthy letter detailing the circumstances which led to his departure from the camp. Ronaldo said he wanted to be spared any leniency.

However, the player reported to be the highest-paid footballer in the world could pay off his fine from the Portuguese FA in 39 seconds based on his estimated wages at Saudi Pro League club Al Nassr.

Ronaldo reportedly earns £488,000 per day from his Al Nassr salary, while Forbes estimate his earnings for 2026 will reach £225m.

The captain's fall-out with Jesus began after he was an unused substitute in a 2-1 win over Norway in Oslo. Ronaldo claims he was told he would be brought on and had warmed up only for Jesus to change his mind.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Piers Morgan argues that Ronaldo is the undisputed best player of all time ahead of Lionel Messi

Ronaldo missed the game against Denmark and the home match against Norway, both of which Portugal won to leave them top of Nations League Group A4 with a perfect record from four matches.

After the second win over Norway, Jesus insisted the door remained open for Ronaldo, who subsequently apologised for his actions and admitted he deserved to be sanctioned.

The Portuguese federation's disciplinary council announced Ronaldo's punishment in a 28-page document on Monday evening, saying it was "adequate and sufficient" for the player's "serious infraction".

Ronaldo is Portugal's record goalscorer and appearance holder with 146 goals in 234 caps. He said in his near-2000-word statement last month that he hopes his international career is not over yet.

Jesus did not comment when asked for his response to Ronaldo's lengthy statement to his 679 million Instagram followers. It is up to the Portugal head coach now to decide if Ronaldo is part of his plans for the next international break.

"It's hard to watch back but also gives me that fire in the belly."

Sports.title: UEFA demands answers from FIFA over Infantino dealings in urgent letter
Sports.content:
UEFA is increasing the pressure on Gianni Infantino and has sent FIFA an urgent letter demanding answers to 42 detailed questions about his presidency.

The letter, which has been seen by Sky Sports News, was written on Monday by UEFA secretary general Theodore Theodoridis and sent to his FIFA counterpart Mattias Grafstrom.

Sky Sports News has also obtained a copy of the full list of 42 questions which cover 12 topics, including 10 alleged conflicts of interest, across eight pages.

Theodoridis gives FIFA two weeks to respond to UEFA's long list of concerns which were raised by European football leaders at the FIFA Council meeting in Zurich last Thursday.

He begins by noting that Infantino acknowledged during the meeting that mistakes had been made but the explanations provided "have not begun satisfactorily to address a number of fundamental questions".

UEFA has also asked for an immediate audio recording of the meeting in another sign it is demanding full transparency from FIFA.

"These questions require answers now," Theodoridis writes. "They cannot be deferred until the next meeting of the FIFA Council - nor can future governance reforms substitute for scrutiny of decisions already taken and accountability for them."

The 42 questions are split into 12 sections:

1. FIFA Forward Enterprise - the World Cup sell-off proposal. Why did Infantino negotiate to sell off a stake in FIFA tournaments in secret?

"Could FIFA explain why an agreement granting exclusivity to Thrive Capital was signed without prior consultation of the FIFA Council? Who authorised FIFA to enter into this agreement, and on what basis?

"Why was the FIFA Council not consulted before exclusivity was granted, irrespective of any approval that may have been envisaged at a later stage?

"Could FIFA also confirm who the members of the Management Board Bureau were at the time of the decision and how each of them voted, specifying who voted in favour, who voted against and who abstained?

"When was it intended that the FFE proposal and supporting documentation would be submitted to the FIFA Council?"

2. Will investigation into FIFA governance be independent and why is FIFA blocking release of documents?

"How does FIFA intend to establish what actually happened in relation to FFE, the Balogun case and the other matters raised by members of the Council, and to ensure appropriate accountability for any shortcomings identified?"

3. Review of funding of FIFA's member associations. On what basis did FIFA propose to sell off a stake in World Cups at a valuation of $20bn when this summer's tournament generated revenues of $15bn?

"Please explain the investment and exit assumptions underlying Thrive Capital's proposed participation".

4. Development funding and use of FIFA's financial resources. Why were member associations going to receive development funding to accept the sell-off proposal when FIFA already has $6bn cash reserves?

"The FIFA president has repeatedly stated that FIFA's money belongs to its MAs. Why, then, was substantially increased funding for MAs presented in connection with FFE and external investment, rather than being financed directly from FIFA's own resources?

"What exactly were MAs being asked to approve as part of the FFE proposal in order to access these additional funds? Following the withdrawal of FFE, FIFA has now proposed increasing funding to $25m per MA using its own reserves. Why was such an approach not considered before FFE was proposed?"

5. Remuneration and financial transparency. Why did Infantino receive a £1.3m payment in 2024 on top of his £4m FIFA salary?

"Recent media reports, referring to filings by FIFA's US World Cup organising entity (FWC2026 US), indicate that the FIFA president received substantial additional remuneration which was not disclosed in FIFA's annual report.

"Could FIFA clarify the nature, amount and basis of these payments, why they were not disclosed in FIFA's annual report, and whether they were reviewed and approved by the competent FIFA bodies?

"Could FIFA also confirm whether the additional remuneration was treated as taxable income and whether the corresponding income tax was paid?"

6. Review of disciplinary procedures and the Balogun case. Why was Balogun allowed to play when he was suspended?

"President Trump publicly acknowledged having called the FIFA president to request a review of the Balogun disciplinary case. What exactly did he ask him to do, and what was his response? Would the case have been reviewed in the absence of his intervention?

"Following that conversation, did the FIFA president or the FIFA secretary general communicate with anyone within FIFA, including members of the administration or the chair of the disciplinary committee, concerning the Balogun case? If so, could FIFA specify with whom, when and the nature of those communications?"

7. Compliance with the Laws of the Game. Why was there a 27-minute World Cup final half-time show?

"The half-time interval during the World Cup final lasted 27 minutes, without any prior request to the IFAB and consultation with the FIFA Council.

"Similarly, the introduction of mandatory so called hydration breaks at all World Cup matches, in deviation from the existing rule was not preceded, to our knowledge, by consultation or a request for authorisation from the IFAB."

8. Electoral integrity and independence of FIFA's judicial bodies. UEFA doubts about whether FIFA presidential election will be fair.

"The official electoral campaign period began on 30 April 2026, the date of the FIFA Congress in Vancouver. Which body, in addition to the FIFA Electoral Committee, is responsible for overseeing the electoral process, and what procedures and safeguards have been established to prevent the misuse of FIFA resources and ensure a fair and impartial presidential election?

"We have concerns regarding the independence and impartiality of the chair of the FIFA Electoral Committee, Mr Chiomento, given the committee's crucial role in overseeing the presidential election."

9. Presidential expenditure and financial oversight. Infantino's private jet provided by Qatar Airways.

"Numerous media reports in recent years have raised questions concerning the FIFA president's use of private aircraft and the costs of his accommodation, notably in Qatar and the United States.

"Could FIFA provide a detailed account of the relevant expenditure, including its amounts, purposes, authorisation procedures and compliance with FIFA's applicable financial and travel policies?"

10. World Cup hospitality and allocation of privileges.

"We request access to the complete list of guests seated in the VIP and VVIP sections during the World Cup final, including their names, positions and the reasons for their invitations.

"Could FIFA also explain the criteria and decision-making process governing the allocation of these places, particularly in circumstances where numerous guests were apparently given priority over presidents of MAs and secretaries general of confederations?"

11. President Trump's FIFA Peace Prize

"In the absence of any prior involvement of the FIFA Council, who decided to establish the FIFA Peace Prize, for what purpose, and who decided that the President of the United States should receive it?

"What role did the FIFA president personally play in the creation of the award and the selection of its recipient? Were any independent selection procedures or objective criteria established and applied? If so, could FIFA provide the relevant documentation?"

12. Conflicts of interest

"A series of decisions, transactions and interventions involving the FIFA president, the President of the United States and individuals associated with him raise serious questions concerning potential conflicts of interest, transparency and institutional accountability."

Those were:

The FIFA Peace Prize, which was not submitted to the FIFA Council for approval.

The reported seven-year, approximately $4m lease of office premises in Trump Tower, New York, involving Eric Trump, for premises reportedly unused for much of the year.

The proposed agreement with Thrive Capital, led by Mr Joshua Kushner, a member of the US president's family.

The US president's telephone call to the FIFA president requesting intervention in the Balogun disciplinary case.

Reported advanced discussions involving the US president and individuals associated with him concerning a FIFA cryptocurrency.

The World Cup sponsorship arrangement with Kalshi, a company reportedly advised and partly owned by Donald Trump Jr, including reports that Kalshi received extensive advertising exposure without providing financial consideration to FIFA.

The last-minute relocation of the World Cup draw, reportedly at significant additional cost to FIFA, to the JFK/Donald Trump Center in Washington, DC, instead of Las Vegas.

The involvement of the US president's daughter and grandson in the Club World Cup draw.

The announcement of a $75m investment in Palestine during the US president's Board of Peace meeting, apparently without prior information being provided to, or approval sought from, the FIFA Finance Committee or Council.

Public statements by White House representatives, including Andrew Giuliani and the US president himself, defending the FIFA president, supporting his continued presidency and criticising those questioning his leadership.

UEFA has so far failed to put forward a candidate before the November 18 deadline to challenge Infantino in next March's presidential election.

Arsene Wenger would be a popular choice to take on Infantino but FIFA's global football development chief has made no comment about a potential challenge.

FIFA has been contacted for comment.

Sports.title: Australia strike late on rain-hit second day against South Africa
Sports.content:
Scott Boland has taken four of South Africa's five wickets to fall, including that of Ryan Rickelton late on another rain-hit day in Gqeberha, as Australia reduced their hosts to 97-5 in the second Test.

After rain washed out the first two sessions of the second day, when South Africa's first innings finally resumed at 20-2 they swiftly lost a third wicket after only a couple of overs.

Boland (4-31), who had taken two wickets with consecutive deliveries on day one, added debutant Marques Ackerman caught behind for six.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from day two of the second Test between South Africa and Australia

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Boland took two wickets in two balls against South Africa on the opening day of the second Test

Mitchell Starc (1-27) then struck to remove Matthew Breetzke (4) - also nicking off, when chasing a wide drive - to have the Proteas rocking at 40-4.

Australia were shorn of one of their four-pronged front-line pace options, with Josh Hazlewood absent on day two due to illness. He is expected to be available for the remainder of the Test.

South Africa gradually grew into proceedings, their captain Temba Bavuma leading from the front with an unbeaten 41 as part of a fifty partnership for the fifth wicket with Rickelton.

Score summary - South Africa vs Australia, second Test, Gqeberha South Africa 97-5 after 43 overs in first innings: Temba Bavuma (41no), Ryan Rickelton (31); Scott Boland (4-31), Mitchell Starc (1-27)

But, just as the pair would have been preparing to put their feet up for the evening and resume battle in the morning, Rickelton - dropped on 26 by Marnus Labuschagne - became Boland's latest victim as Matt Renshaw claimed a sensational, one-handed catch low to his right at slip.

South Africa are the reigning world Test champions, having beaten current table-toppers Australia in the 2025 final, but they trail 1-0 in this three-match series after a heavy 214-run defeat in the first Test.
