Sports.title: Russell and Leclerc are the joint ‘sprint race champions’ of 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli can clinch the drivers’ championship at the next round – but three of his rivals out-scored him over the course of Formula 1’s six sprint races this year.

Singapore played host to F1’s sixth and final sprint race of 2026 last weekend. The sprint races were won by four different drivers: George Russell won three (Shanghai, Montreal and Zandvoort), while his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli triumphed at Silverstone, Lando Norris won in Miami and it was Max Verstappen’s turn in Singapore.

Russell could have beaten Verstappen last weekend, of course, having taken the lead off him at the start. But his crash at the end of lap one ended his chances of winning a fourth sprint race.

It also meant he ended the year with as many sprint race points as a driver who didn’t win any of these races. Charles Leclerc collected 34 points from sprint races, the same as Russell. This was made possible by the single-point gaps between finishing positions in sprint races, which are much closer than those used in grands prix.

After Russell’s retirement, Norris was on course to end the year as the top sprint race points-scorer. But his last-lap tangle with his team mate cost him three points and left him third.

As points are only awarded to the top eight finishers in sprint races, the drivers from the top four teams tended to monopolise them, with one exception: Isack Hadjar did not score a single point in a sprint race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Liam Lawson scored points for both Red Bull (while substituting for Hadjar at Zandvoort) and Racing Bulls in sprint races. His regular team mate Arvid Lindblad also took sprint race points, as did Alpine’s Pierre Gasly and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg.

But for almost half the grid, the sprint races offered nothing. The addition of four more sprint races next year could further increase the gap between the leading teams and the midfield.

Sports.title: Singapore victory leaves Verstappen one win away from a full set – but not for long | 2026 Singapore Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen’s 73rd career victory was surely one of the most overdue of his career. At his 10th attempt, the Red Bull driver finally won the Singapore Grand Prix.

He’d come close several times before. Verstappen had started second four times and converted three of those into second-place finishes. On the other occasion he was wiped out by the Ferrari drivers as they sprinted to turn one.

But after finally claiming his first pole position at the Marina Bay circuit, Verstappen never let go of his advantage, leading every lap of the race. However with other drivers switching to the preferred soft tyres over the final stint, Verstappen did not set the fastest lap, so he did not collect his seventh ‘grand slam’.

He has now won at 27 different circuits, a feat only bettered by Lewis Hamilton on 31. Verstappen has won on every track on the calendar with a single exception: the Madring, which held its first grand prix this year.

However in order to complete a clean sweep of victories at every track on the calendar, Verstappen will have to win at three new rounds next year. Two venues where he has raced in F1, but not previously won at, will return on the 2027 F1 calendar.

What’s more, another driver will be in the same position as Verstappen. This is Hamilton, the last driver to have achieved a clean sweep:

Hamilton last achieved a clean sweep when he won the French Grand Prix in 2018. He kept up the achievement over the next two seasons – even as the Covid-19 pandemic added new races to the schedule in 2020 – but his run ended when he failed to win at Zandvoort in 2021.

Achieving a clean sweep next year would arguably be a greater feat for either driver. There were 21 circuits on the calendar when Hamilton achieved it in 2018, but there are 24 on next year’s schedule.

Verstappen became the fifth driver to achieve 50 pole positions last weekend. He did so in his 250th race start and joins Ayrton Senna, who took 108 races to do the same, Hamilton (168), Michael Schumacher (177) and Sebastian Vettel (196).

This was the fourth year in a row the Singapore Grand Prix has been won from pole position. Verstappen led every lap on his way to victory, which is the fourth ‘lights-to-flag’ victory at the circuit in the last five years, along with Sergio Perez’s win in 2022 (from second on the grid), Carlos Sainz Jnr’s in 2023 and Lando Norris’s from 2024.

Red Bull was only one win behind Mercedes when the season began. However Mercedes has enjoyed such a strong season that Red Bull’s victories in the last two rounds means its is now 10 behind. However Red Bull did end Mercedes’ streak of leading at least one lap in every race this year.

Racing Bulls reached 100 points, which is more than they scored last year and their best score since 2021, when they competed as AlphaTauri.

But Alpine’s season has decidedly hit the skids as they failed to score for the third round in a row. It was a particularly frustrating weekend for Pierre Gasly, who finished one place outside the points in both the sprint race and grand prix.

Williams left Singapore point-less, too. Carlos Sainz Jnr got his car into the top 10 early on in his 250th appearance in a grand prix weekend, but slipped to 14th at the flag.

10 years ago today Lance Stroll scored his most recent victory to date, in his final race before he became a Formula 1 driver.

Just two weeks shy of his 18th birthday, Stroll’s promotion to F1 with Williams the following year had already been announced. He had clinched the European Formula 3 championship earlier in the season and won both of the preceding two races in the season-ending triple-header at the Hockenheimring.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Wants Melikuziev Fight Next Year
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia intends to put his ordered title defense against Bektemir Melikuziev on hold until next year, insisting he requires a dedicated training camp while gearing up to face Nikita Zon on October 31.

The WBA super middleweight champion remains focused on competing on the Canelo Alvarez vs. Christian Mbilli undercard in Riyadh. Still, wanting to delay Melikuziev until 2027 raises major concerns regarding whether sanctioning officials will let him keep the belt while taking an unapproved interim contest.

The WBA previously noted that the Munguia vs. Zon matchup had not received sanctioning approval, adding that officials would review the matter while keeping Melikuziev in position as the mandatory challenger. Munguia gave no indication during the interview that he secured an exemption or official sign-off to delay the mandatory.

Instead, the titlist pointed to the compressed schedule as the reason he cannot face Melikuziev right away.

“Proper training camp and other things. But we have a short time for that fight,” Munguia told The Ring. “I think next year it’s going to be a good fight.”

Wanting a complete camp for an opponent like Melikuziev makes sense on paper. Shifting focus from one challenger to a heavy-handed mandatory creates complications, especially on shortened notice.

Still, personal preference does not erase championship duties. Melikuziev locked in his mandatory status through official channels. Forcing him to sit on the sidelines while Munguia takes another bout requires formal sanctioning body consent, not just the champion deciding a later date suits him better.

When the interviewer floated a schedule featuring Melikuziev in May and Hamzah Sheeraz in September, Munguia welcomed the Sheeraz option. Neither date, however, represents a signed agreement.

For now, Munguia is guaranteeing an explosive finish against Zon.

“It’s going to be a good fight, and it’s going to be a knockout,” Munguia said.

A stoppage win in Riyadh could generate a highlight reel moment on a major international stage. It will not resolve the uncertainty surrounding his strap. Until the WBA formally rules on the matter, Munguia is laying out a calendar he desires rather than one he is authorized to carry out.

Sports.title: Alberto Puello Plans To Mark Up Dalton Smith
Sports.content:
Alberto Puello plans to test Dalton Smith’s accuracy and cut-prone skin on Saturday, when the WBC light welterweight champion makes his first defense at Sheffield’s Utilita Arena. Smith could have a difficult night if he cannot consistently find the skilled southpaw.

Puello (25-1, 11 KOs) brings a different style than Subriel Matias, whom Smith stopped in five rounds in January. Matias gave Smith opportunities to plant his feet and fire during their shootout. Puello is unlikely to offer the same opportunities.

“With the big head he has, I’m not going to miss a blow. It’s going to be very easy to mark him up,” Puello told The Ring.

That threat has some substance behind it. Smith has suffered cuts around his eyes during his career, including against Matias. Puello’s ability to land accurately could become an issue even without the punching power normally associated with a knockout threat.

The Eddie Hearn-promoted Smith (19-0, 14 KOs) needs to avoid spending rounds following Puello without getting his punches off. Coming through boxing in the Dominican Republic, Puello has been exposed to different styles, and he has the professional experience to change his approach when something stops working.

Against Matias, Smith was dealing with a one-track pressure fighter whose instinct is to walk in behind high earmuff defense and trade at point-blank range. That allowed Smith to tie him up on the inside, rough him up, lean on him, and time his short hooks in the clinch. Matias basically walked straight into Smith’s traps because he has zero interest in back-foot boxing.

Puello is the polar opposite. He is not going to march into Smith’s chest to give him free clinches or let Smith wrap him up. He fights behind a long, tricky southpaw jab, controls distance, and steps off to the sides the second an opponent tries to close the gap.

Hearn has matched Smith against guys who come forward, allowing him to use his heavy-handed throwback fighting style to bludgeon them. Against a pure mover with an awkward southpaw stance like Puello, that exact style can make a fighter look flat-footed, crude, and completely out of ideas over twelve rounds. Style-wise, Puello is a nightmare for him.

Puello lost his WBC 140-lb title to Matias by a controversial 12-round majority decision in July 2025. He now travels to the champion’s hometown intending to leave less room for debate.

“The way I do it is to win clearly and never deviate from that plan that I have,” Puello said.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois Targets February With Agit Kabayel Possible
Sports.content:
Daniel Dubois wants to be back in the ring this February. Frank Warren is eyeing Agit Kabayel to set up a massive heavyweight unification clash.

Dubois retained his WBO title by stopping Fabio Wardley in two rounds on Saturday at London’s O2 Arena, leaving him ready to pursue another champion without the need for a third fight with Wardley.

“He’ll fight in February, we are going to see what happens,” Warren told talkSPORT.

Warren is keeping a close eye on Kabayel’s November 28 defense against Nelson Hysa in Germany. He reported approximately 43,000 to 44,000 tickets sold for that event.

“Let’s see the outcome because that would be a fantastic unification scrap,” Warren said.

Kabayel offers a different challenge than Wardley. The German works the body with relentless pressure. He aims to drag opponents into deep waters rather than trade quick bombs. Dubois packs enough power to crack him coming forward, so it would get violent immediately.

If Kabayel drags him into rounds five, six, and seven while ripping hooks into his ribs, Dubois will be forced to answer the exact mental questions he has struggled with throughout his career.

The calendar could be tricky, though, to make a Dubois vs. Kabayel unification fight. Going from late November to February leaves barely two months to recover. If Hysa pushes Kabayel hard, that turnaround shrinks fast. Right now Warren is floating an option, not closing a contract.

Filip Hrgovic is also hovering around the picture. The IBF champ sat ringside Saturday night, looking for revenge against the only man who beat him as a pro.

“He wanted a rematch since Daniel holds a win over him,” Warren said.

Dubois holds plenty of leverage while his destruction of Wardley is fresh in everyone’s minds. Snatching another belt cements his status. Taking on Kabayel gives him a fresh face after crushing Wardley back-to-back.

Warren made it clear his fighter is chasing giant paydays, too.

“He wants big fights because he tells me he wants to make huge money,” Warren said.

February stays circled on the calendar. Once Kabayel gets past November, Dubois will know if he has a chance to make this fight happen.

Sports.title: Oscar Collazo Faces Mandatory Order After Flyweight Setback
Sports.content:
The WBO is not doing Oscar Collazo any favors. Just as the Puerto Rican minimumweight champion was preparing to walk away from 105 pounds, the sanctioning body stepped in to complicate matters, ordering him to defend his strap against interim titleholder Ryusei Matsumoto within a 15-day negotiating window.

The timing could hardly be worse for Collazo. He had already set his sights on bigger game, skipping right past light flyweight to challenge Ricardo Sandoval for two flyweight belts on October 10 in Chicago.

That two-division title run was ruined when a painful rib injury in training camp knocked him off the card. Instead of resting up and rescheduling his run at 112, Collazo now finds the WBO knocking on his door, insisting he settle business at the minimumweight limit.

WBO representative Gustavo Olivieri laid down the law on social media, making it clear that both camps have two weeks to hammer out terms or the fight goes straight to purse bids. The organization is leaning on its rule of keeping only one champion per division, which puts an end to Matsumoto’s interim status one way or another.

The order simply covers the paperwork, not a fight date. Nobody expects Collazo in the ring tomorrow, especially with bruised or broken ribs needing time to heal. The real issue is the weight. Making 105 pounds is brutal for any fighter growing into his prime, and Collazo had already mentally and physically started the transition to flyweight. Asking his body to drop back down for Matsumoto is a grueling chore that risks stalling his career.

Collazo holds the cards, but neither option is simple. Walking away from the belt leaves him empty-handed with nothing guaranteed at 112, while taking the Matsumoto fight delays his move up for several months.

Matsumoto’s team is in a great position, knowing they either get a shot at the real belt or pick it up by default. Collazo has to decide if keeping the hardware is worth the torture of making 105 one more time.

For Collazo, the risk-to-reward ratio is completely upside down. If he wins, what does he get? A small purse and the privilege of holding a belt that does not move the needle commercially. If he enters the ring drained from making weight and gets caught or looks sluggish against Matsumoto, his entire stock drops before he ever gets to cash in at flyweight.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Still Has Plenty Of Paydays Available
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley can still bag massive paydays below elite title level. Calls for him to hang up the gloves after getting stopped by Daniel Dubois completely miss that reality. Falling short against Dubois does not strip him of his ability to top domestic bills.

Derek Chisora wrote the playbook here. Chisora never had to conquer top-tier heavyweights to fill arenas or generate huge paychecks. British fans recognize him, know the entertainment they are paying for, and show up. Wardley can mirror that blueprint without wasting years fruitlessly chasing a rematch with Dubois.

Domestic dust-ups against Dave Allen, Johnny Fisher, or Chisora himself offer immediate box-office appeal. Efe Ajagba or Tony Yoka provide solid international flavor. None of those are walkovers, but none require beating a pound-for-pound monster to pack out a venue.

The draw remains unchanged. Fans know Wardley hits like a truck, and they know he can get hurt in return. Put Wardley in the ring with Fisher, and nobody cares if a world belt is on the line; they are tuning in because someone is going to sleep.

That leaves Queensberry holding plenty of cards. A routine bounce-back victory followed by a massive domestic main event puts him right back in the money without pretending he solved the Dubois riddle.

Down the line, reaching the end of his Queensberry deal might even open up a fresh bidding war. Zuffa could easily see value in an action-heavy British brawler. While nothing is on the table right now, it highlights how many avenues exist beyond this single loss.

Wardley’s physical condition must always come first. From a purely business perspective, the path is clear. Chisora proved you can remain a massive ticket seller without beating the division’s champions.

Wardley does not need another belt around his waist to get paid. Pick the right matchups, and he can laugh all the way to the bank for years to come.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Seeks Stamina Help From Team Usyk
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is working alongside Oleksandr Usyk’s conditioning team ahead of his October 31 bout against Christian Mbilli in Riyadh. The meeting will thoroughly test his gas tank across twelve rounds.

Base camp is Gandia, Spain, where Canelo brought in outside fitness specialists while Eddy Reynoso directs the boxing work. Against Mbilli, the payoff must show when fatigue sets in, especially since the younger contender never stops pressing forward.

“In strength and conditioning, I am learning new things,” Canelo told The Ring. “I appreciate them because they put all of their energy into me and are doing everything based on what [my head coach] Eddy Reynoso needs for boxing.”

Mbilli’s relentless tempo explains the sudden shift in preparation. Canelo punishes opponents who march directly into his range, yet he needs steady volume to win rounds. Landing occasional sharp counters leaves far too much clock open for an aggressive challenger throwing nonstop leather.

The main question is whether Canelo can sustain his offense once the fight pushes past the midway mark. Now 36, Canelo returns following his defeat against Terence Crawford and subsequent surgery on his left elbow, with over a year of inactivity behind him. He expects peak execution from a heavily taxed body.

A fresh training philosophy provides something new, yet genuine output down the stretch remains unproven. Cardiovascular endurance does not magically appear in the twilight of a twenty-year career. You cannot rebuild an engine with that much mileage, especially after serious elbow surgery and more than a year out of the ring.

Usyk’s training methods work for Usyk because he has spent a lifetime developing an engine built for movement, bounce, and non-stop output. Transplanting those drills onto a flat-footed counterpuncher who relies on heavy torso rotations and planted feet makes zero sense mechanically.

Mbilli is a nightmare style for an aging fighter who needs scheduled rest breaks. He throws upwards of 80 punches a round, does not care about taking shots to give three back, and smothers distance

The mental comfort of working with Usyk’s crew might give him a temporary psychological lift in camp, but once round seven arrives, and Mbilli is still in his chest, those new drills will not buy him the oxygen his legs and lungs can no longer produce.

Training in Spain softens the time shift into Saudi Arabia. Canelo described feeling “really weird” during his early morning bout with William Scull and stated he has requested that Turki Alalshikh schedule a ring walk no later than midnight or 1 a.m.

Better timing can sharpen his entrance. Once the bell rings, though, Mbilli brings intense pressure that travel logistics cannot solve. Canelo needs the work with Usyk’s camp to translate into steady output when fatigue threatens to stall him.

Sports.title: David Benavidez Drops Canelo Chase Three Years Late
Sports.content:
David Benavidez has finally conceded that a fight with Canelo Alvarez will never happen, admitting that reality years after his climb up the divisions settled the question.

Benavidez currently fights at cruiserweight, two full divisions above super middleweight, while openly discussing a future heavyweight jump against Oleksandr Usyk. He has not made 168 pounds since 2023. Any realistic window to face Canelo closed several weight classes ago.

“I think honestly I could say with confidence that that fight is never going to happen,” Benavidez told Brian Custer.

When Brian asked if he had permanently moved on, Benavidez praised Canelo, yet still claimed the Mexican star simply refused to face him.

“I don’t want to keep disrespecting somebody … not even disrespecting, but just calling somebody out that doesn’t want to fight,” he said.

That rationale ignores the massive physical gap separating them today. Critics can reasonably argue Canelo should have met Benavidez when both shared the 168-pound division. That complaint loses all weight with Benavidez now preparing for Michal Cieslak at 200 pounds.

His prospective roadmap includes Jai Opetaia, Artur Beterbiev, and eventual heavyweight tests. None of those plans lead anywhere near Canelo.

A logical alternative after Canelo fell to Terence Crawford would have been targeting Crawford directly. Crawford had talked of entering boxing’s Mount Rushmore. The public intrigue around him was at an all-time peak, and Turki Alalshikh held the purse strings to fund virtually any blockbuster Crawford wanted next.

If Benavidez truly wanted to settle the score on the belts Canelo kept out of reach, Crawford was the obvious lever to pull. Instead of shifting his crosshairs to the newly crowned undisputed champion, Benavidez let the moment disappear.

“He’s a great fighter. He’s a legend,” Benavidez said. “I would like to be a great Mexican legend like him one day.”

Calling yourself a future Mexican legend sounds nice in an interview, but looking at the actual resume tells a different story. Canelo earned that status by taking on the toughest challenges available from junior middleweight all the way to light heavyweight, facing elite operators like Floyd Mayweather Jr., Gennadiy Golovkin, Miguel Cotto, and Dmitry Bivol.

Benavidez is nowhere near that neighborhood. Instead of securing defining legacy bouts, he is lining up voluntary defenses against Michal Cieslak at 200 pounds. While Cieslak is a capable European contender, nobody outside of hard-core circles is paying to see that fight. It does nothing to elevate Benavidez to the pantheon of Mexican greats.

If Benavidez genuinely wanted to close the gap on Canelo, he needed to make real waves. Taking out Gilberto Ramirez was a solid win, but sitting on belts and scheduling low-demand opponents like Cieslak keeps him in neutral. Fighting fringe contenders at cruiserweight only proves that while he talks about chasing history, his matchmaking still trails far behind the standard Canelo set.

Sports.title: Frank Martin Wants Shakur Stevenson Or Tank Rematch
Sports.content:
Frank Martin is calling for bouts with Shakur Stevenson, Gervonta Davis, or Isaac Pitbull Cruz. Still, his recent ring activity shows he has serious ground to cover before getting those marquee fights.

The 31-year-old light welterweight contender welcomed every major challenge, targeting Davis in particular.

“Man, I love that rematch,” Martin said to Fight Hub TV. He also acknowledged that facing Cruz or Lamont Roach could build momentum toward a second Davis meeting.

Martin pointed to weight issues during his initial loss to Davis without detailing what went wrong. Vague explanations will not convince the public to buy a sequel. He must deliver clear proof inside the ropes that a second meeting would end differently.

The inactivity is killing whatever marketability he had left from the Tank pay-per-view. Since the lucrative 2024 bout with Davis, Martin has made only two ring appearances. His sole win since 2023 was a decision over veteran Rances Barthelemy, followed by a ten-round draw against Nahir Albright earlier this year.

Albright was supposed to be a routine showcase to get him winning, and instead, Martin escaped with a gift draw in a fight that many observers thought he dropped. When you look shaky against Albright, you have zero leverage to demand dates with elite champions.

Martin steps into the ring against Tarik Zaina on October 24 for a rebuilding fight. Winning is essential, yet vanishing into inactivity afterward would erase any progress.

“We ain’t chasing nobody,” Martin stated. “I just want to put on a dominant performance,” noting he is ready for whatever comes next.

Waiting for top fighters to call him rarely works. Neither Stevenson nor Davis has an incentive to pick him when Martin carries minimal buzz. Cruz offers the most practical path forward. The aggressive style Cruz brings could create an explosive contest, giving Martin a platform to secure a defining victory.

Joining Zuffa could also solve his scheduling problems if the promotion delivers active fight dates. Constant ring time will do far more for his career than calling out superstars he cannot book.

Ghana News.title: University of Ghana awaits Book and Research Allowance over documentation delay
Ghana News.content:
The University of Ghana is awaiting payment of its Book and Research Allowance following delays in the submission and validation of documents required for the disbursement, the Education Minister’s spokesperson, Hashmin Mohammed, has said.

In a Facebook post on Monday, October 19, 2026, Mr Mohammed explained that the institution’s documents had to be submitted to the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) for validation before the Controller and Accountant-General’s Department (CAGD) could process the payment.

His explanation comes as the government advances payments of the allowance to eligible tertiary institutions, with GH¢238 million reportedly disbursed to 56 institutions under the first batch.

A further GH¢198 million has been earmarked for the second batch, which includes the University of Ghana.

Mr Mohammed said the documentation and validation requirements were necessary to ensure that payments were properly processed and made to the intended institutions.

However, he did not provide a specific date for the University of Ghana’s payment.

The spokesperson said the government had mobilised approximately GH¢436 million for the allowance payments, covering the first and second batches.

The allowance supports the academic and research activities of eligible lecturers in public tertiary institutions.

The latest update provides an explanation for the delay affecting the University of Ghana, although the timing of its eventual payment remains unclear.

Attention will now be on the completion of the validation process and the release of the funds to the institution.

Delays in the payment of the allowance have periodically attracted concern from beneficiaries, making the government’s disbursement arrangements an issue of interest to tertiary education staff.

Ghana News.title: Where is the 24-hour economy? – Bawumia challenges Mahama government to show results
Ghana News.content:
John Mahama of NDC (L) and Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia of NPP (R)

The New Patriotic Party (NPP) flagbearer Dr Mahamudu Bawumia has been tearing into the government's flagship 24-hour economy, delivering a brutal verdict nearly two hours into the NDC administration.

Dr Bawumia has challenged the Mahama government to demonstrate progress on its flagship 24-hour economy policy, questioning whether the initiative has delivered the jobs and employment opportunities promised to Ghanaians.

Speaking at the NPP’s Thanksgiving service in Sunyani, Dr Bawumia criticised the government’s handling of the policy, arguing that Ghanaians were yet to see tangible results.

“We have waited for 2 years, but we cannot see the 24-hour economy. They were just campaign propaganda. They don’t understand for them to come and explain it to us. They themselves don’t understand it. Where is the 24-hour economy?” he asked.

He argued that the policy risked remaining an election promise if the government could not translate its commitments into concrete employment opportunities and benefits for the public.

Dr Bawumia also challenged the government’s economic recovery narrative, saying improvements in headline indicators such as inflation and the exchange rate would mean little if households continued to struggle financially.

“The government says inflation is down, and the dollar is down, but Ghanaians are interested in the pocket economy. They know the pocket economy,” he said.

He maintained that economic stability should be reflected in improved living conditions and relief from the financial pressures facing ordinary Ghanaians.

“I am saying stability of the economy is meaningless if it cannot be linked up with the total liberation of the suffering of our people,” he added.

The former Vice President’s comments form part of the NPP’s criticism of the government’s economic management and its implementation of campaign promises, particularly the 24-hour economy initiative.

The policy is a flagship programme of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), aimed at expanding economic activity and creating employment through round-the-clock production and service delivery.

Ghana News.title: Japan Motors donates five motorcycles to support 42nd National Farmers’ Day
Ghana News.content:
The Ministry of Food and Agriculture has announced that Japan Motors Trading Company Limited has donated five branded motorcycles towards the 42nd National Farmers’ Day celebration.

In a press release issued on Monday, October 19, 2026, the Ministry said the donation qualified the company as a silver sponsor of the annual event, which recognises the contributions of farmers and fishers to Ghana’s development.

“The Ministry remains deeply grateful to the Company for its dedicated commitment to support the celebration and the promotion of agricultural development in Ghana,” the statement, signed by the Ministry’s Public Relations Unit, said.

The Ministry described the donation as a recognition of the important role farmers and fishers play in national development and an example of private-sector support for agricultural promotion.

It called on other corporate organisations, financial institutions, development partners and individuals to contribute towards the upcoming celebration.

The Ministry said the annual event provides a national platform to recognise the hard work and achievements of farmers and fishers, whose activities are central to food security, employment and economic growth.

National Farmers’ Day is an annual celebration held to honour farmers and fishers across Ghana for their contributions to agricultural production and national food security.

The 42nd edition is expected to take place later this year, with corporate sponsors and other partners supporting its organisation.

Japan Motors’ donation adds to the support being mobilised for the celebration as the Ministry encourages more private-sector participation.

Ghana News.title: Making Ghana’s 5G investment deliver for businesses and the economy
Ghana News.content:
At a busy shop in Kumasi, a customer waits while an electronic payment stalls. In a diagnostic centre, medical images await transfer to a specialist. A guesthouse loses a booking when its internet connection drops, while an engineering firm waits for a large design file before it can finish a client’s work. For these businesses, connectivity affects income, customer confidence and the time available to serve the next person.

Now consider what more dependable connectivity could make possible: a retailer keeping stock records and online orders up to date during the afternoon rush; a student joining a practical lesson remotely without repeated interruptions; a logistics company receiving timely updates to organise deliveries; or a small professional firm serving clients elsewhere in Ghana without travelling for every meeting. These are practical opportunities through which Ghana’s 5G investment could improve everyday services and expand the reach of local businesses.

The gains depend on more than speed. A payment terminal needs a connection that remains available. A diagnostic centre needs adequate upload capacity. A hotel needs enough capacity for guests and business systems to work simultaneously. Each needs a service suited to its workload, at a price it can sustain.

Spectrum licensing opens the way for operators to provide these services. Turning that opportunity into economic value requires investment in networks, affordable access and businesses equipped to use connectivity effectively. Ghana’s progress should therefore be measured through fewer disrupted transactions, work completed sooner and customers served more reliably. Those outcomes give the country’s 5G investment a purpose that businesses and the public can recognise.

From spectrum awards to usable services

On 15 July 2026, the National Communications Authority removed the exclusive wholesale 5G rights of Next Gen Infraco Limited, commonly known as NGIC, while preserving the remainder of its licence and spectrum assignment. The amendment opens space for competing deployments while retaining NGIC in the infrastructure landscape.

MTN Ghana’s announcement on 2 October reported an award notice for spectrum in the 700 MHz and 3 GHz bands, with fees totalling US$202 million for 15-year licences. At that announcement, payment obligations and formalities were being finalised, with deployment to follow licence issuance. Graphic Online separately reported Telecel’s award of three 2.3 GHz lots, quoting company confirmation.

An award, an issued licence and an available retail service are different stages. A business still needs installed infrastructure, compatible equipment and a provider able to activate service at its premises. Public reporting should make these stages clear so that businesses can plan against verified availability.

Spectrum fees are one component of operators’ network investment. Radios, transmission infrastructure and power systems require capital expenditure, followed by recurring energy, maintenance and operating costs. Customers face separate calculations: equipment and installation charges they bear, subscription fees and usage charges. Those costs should be assessed against improvements in the customer’s work and earnings.

Coverage must translate into working connections

Coverage describes where a connection may be obtainable; capacity describes how much traffic a network can carry while users compete for it. Lower-frequency spectrum, such as 700 MHz, helps extend reach and penetrate buildings. Wider mid-band allocations provide room for greater capacity, subject to the bandwidth activated, antenna configuration, interference and user conditions.

A business can therefore lie within a coverage area and still experience slow transfers when demand rises. A hotel needs adequate service when guests return in the evening. A commercial district needs capacity when many businesses are trading simultaneously. Installation tests should reflect those conditions and the equipment’s intended location inside the premises.

The NCA’s clarified 70 per cent outdoor mobile-broadband population target for March 2027 is technology-neutral. It should not be read as a guarantee of usable 5G at every premises within that population. Coverage figures need to be accompanied by evidence of experienced performance.

This matters especially for smaller businesses and communities beyond the largest commercial centres. A connection that is nominally available but unaffordable or unreliable cannot support regular use. Deployment policy should assess both network reach and the practical conditions under which customers can participate.

Wireless broadband needs capacity and reliable installation

Fixed wireless access connects premises to a cellular network through installed receiving equipment. It can offer an alternative where fibre installation is costly or slow. Fixed customers, however, share radio capacity with mobile users. Ericsson’s planning guidance considers their combined demand during the busiest periods.

For illustration, twenty businesses simultaneously requiring 20 megabits per second need 400 megabits per second of useful download capacity before mobile traffic and operating headroom. This is a demand calculation, not a measurement of Ghanaian cell capacity. An advertised “up to 100 Mbps” subscription identifies a maximum speed; it does not establish reserved capacity or minimum performance during congestion.

Uploads deserve particular attention. Medical images, engineering files and cloud backups move towards the network. A one-gigabyte file contains approximately 8,000 megabits. At a sustained upload rate of 10 Mbps, its theoretical transfer time is about thirteen minutes; at 50 Mbps, it is under three minutes. Actual transfers take longer when overheads and interruptions are included.

Improvement has economic value when it helps complete work sooner or avoids delays elsewhere. Providers should test reception, select suitable indoor or outdoor equipment and check the customer’s local network. Poor office Wi-Fi can restrict performance even when the external connection is adequate.

Reliability also depends on power and backhaul, the transmission links connecting radio sites to the wider network. A backup subscription may share the primary connection’s mast, transmission route or power dependency. Resilience arrangements must address those shared points of failure.

International lessons for Ghana

Kenya demonstrates the importance of entry costs. In October 2023, Safaricom reduced its 5G router price from KES25,000 to KES9,999 while expanding coverage into selected towns across 35 counties. At an indicative exchange rate for the announcement date, those prices were approximately GH¢1,970 and GH¢790. These are historical comparisons, not current Ghanaian equipment prices.

The announcement shows an effort to lower the adoption barrier, not proof that cheaper equipment produced business growth. Ghanaian packages should combine affordable equipment with installation qualification and transparent usage terms. Instalments may ease cash flow without reducing total cost; allowances and fair-use restrictions can affect whether a package supports daily work.

India offers a model for application testing. Its Ministry of Communications reported 100 5G laboratories in March 2026. Ghanaian universities, operators and businesses could jointly test applications in health, education and logistics against available 4G, fibre or Wi-Fi alternatives. A logistics pilot should measure dispatch delays or completed deliveries, with an operational manager responsible for putting the application into daily use. Laboratory activity alone does not establish commercial success.

The United Kingdom illustrates why performance claims need measurement. Ofcom’s Mobile Matters 2025 found standalone 5G’s average response time about 15 per cent lower than non-standalone, but its connection success rate was also lower: 95.9 against 97.6 per cent. Standalone 5G uses a 5G core, the systems managing connections beyond the radio network; non-standalone builds on existing 4G infrastructure.

These crowdsourced observations were not a controlled technology comparison or a forecast for Ghana. They demonstrate why buyers need several measures together. Faster responses have limited value when an application cannot establish its connection. Ghana should report performance with clear sampling methods and measurement endpoints.

Make investment and accountability practical

Businesses should establish the existing connection’s performance before testing a replacement. A 90-day pilot can measure consultation interruptions, completed transfers or productive hours recovered, alongside the full additional cost of equipment, integration and service.

Consider a hypothetical business generating GH¢3,000 in additional monthly contribution and removing GH¢1,000 of avoidable costs. Contribution means revenue remaining after the variable costs of earning it. With additional operating costs of GH¢1,500, the net monthly gain is GH¢2,500. An initial outlay of GH¢10,000 would have a simple payback of four months, assuming recurring gains and excluding financing and tax. Saved staff time counts only when productively redeployed or translated into an actual saving.

Business associations can aggregate demand from smaller firms, giving providers a clearer basis for installation and capacity planning. Providers should specify minimum performance at qualified premises, restoration targets and remedies for failure. Pilot results should include unsuccessful cases so that investment decisions reflect operating conditions.

The NCA should publish clear award and licence status and independently checked deployment milestones. Coverage reporting should be supplemented with working-hour download and upload performance, responsiveness and availability. Infrastructure-sharing and wholesale access arrangements should also be monitored as competition develops.

Ghana’s service economy will gain when better connectivity enables businesses to serve customers reliably and complete more valuable work. That requires suitable networks, commercially sustainable packages and users equipped to benefit. These outcomes should guide the country’s assessment of its 5G investment.

The author, Prof. Abdul-Rahman Ahmed, is Head of the Department of Telecommunication Engineering at KNUST and founder of Stratfound Consult.

Ghana News.title: Nico Williams’ agent finally explains failed Barcelona move in 2025
Ghana News.content:
Barcelona’s inability to provide guarantees over Nico Williams’ registration derailed the proposed move in the summer of 2025, his agent, Félix Tainta, has finally revealed.

The Spanish football powerhouse had been keen to sign the Spain international, with their interest extending over two summers, following his top-class performances for both Spain and Athletic Bilbao.

Williams became one of the most sought-after players in Europe in summer 2024 after playing an integral role in Spain’s success at the 2024 European Championship and helping Athletic Bilbao end their 40-year trophy drought by winning the Copa del Rey.

According to Tainta, negotiations had taken place between Barcelona and Bilbao over a possible transfer of the enterprising attacker.

However, the move ultimately fell through over Barcelona’s inability to guarantee Williams’ registration under La Liga’s financial regulations.

“We were in talks with Barcelona and Athletic Bilbao were aware of this. They knew what was happening throughout the process, although the club was not happy with Barcelona’s actions,” he said, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo.

“As the negotiations progressed, it became clear that Nico Williams could not afford to take the risk of not playing. It’s like a Formula 1 car; if I move into your house, I shouldn’t inherit your problems. I made that perfectly clear to Barcelona,” he added.

“We decided, in the absence of specific guarantees, that we could not risk Nico going there and then ending up without playing. He is a professional and needs to practice his profession, especially with the World Cup approaching at that time,” he explained.

“If I come to your house to do my job, I should be able to continue doing it and your problems shouldn’t affect me. If you can’t ensure that doesn’t happen, maybe I should change my mind. That’s exactly what happened,” Tainta concluded.

Williams ultimately remained at Athletic Bilbao, where he has established himself as one of the club’s most important attacking players.

The trophy presentation offered the Iron Breakers an opportunity to recognise a supporter they say contributed to their journey to success, while formalising a relationship they hope will support the club’s future development.

With Mr Ahlijah accepting the role of patron, Vodza Iron Breakers will look to build on their finals victory as they pursue their ambitions in beach soccer.

Ghana News.title: Education Minister refers Obuasi SHS headmaster’s sexual misconduct allegations to CID
Ghana News.content:
Haruna Iddrisu is Education Minister

The Minister for Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has referred allegations of sexual misconduct involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, and female students to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) for investigation.

The move is intended to allow the police to investigate the criminal aspects of the allegations while education authorities conduct separate administrative inquiries.

Speaking to Accra-based Citi News, Mr Iddrisu confirmed that the headmaster had been interdicted pending investigations, stressing that the government would not tolerate sexual misconduct in schools.

“Any act of sexual misconduct involving a teacher and a student amounts to abuse of office, and government takes strong exception to it. We have forwarded it to the criminal investigation department to deal with the criminal aspects of it whilst I’ve asked for the suspension of the headmaster without prejudice whilst we look into the merits of the case,” he said on Monday, October 19.

Mr Iddrisu also disclosed that the government was considering broader measures to address indiscipline in schools, including the introduction of stronger regulations to guide the conduct of students and teachers.

He said a committee would soon be established to advise the government on the matter.

The Minister further indicated his support for making the Ghana Education Service’s (GES) code of conduct and standards legally binding under Article 11 of the 1992 Constitution.

The GES announced Mr Abdulai’s interdiction in a statement issued on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, to facilitate investigations into the allegations.

The case reportedly triggered a student rampage at the school, during which some school property was destroyed, forcing the temporary closure of the institution.

The allegations remain subject to investigation.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Indian court extends detention of ‘Cockroach’ leaders
World.content:
The extension of the custody of the CJP activists comes amid a crackdown on near daily protests against the government.

An Indian ‌‌court has extended the detention of two leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).

The extension for Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das on Monday comes amid a crackdown on near-daily protests against the government.

The two activists from the youth-led movement were arrested as they demonstrated at a historic protest venue despite a ban. Their jailing provoked a new protest in New Delhi on Friday.

The CJP is a major force behind the protests, which have demanded the resignation of India’s election chief over a controversial revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya ⁠⁠Janata Party (BJP).

Ranka and Das were ⁠⁠among 14 protesters who climbed over barricades last week to enter the Jantar Mantar observatory, the day after it was removed from a list of approved demonstration sites. A court later sent the activists to prison for five days.

Indian media reported on Monday evening that they had been detained for two more days after police requested extra time to question them. Delhi ‌‌Police did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

“This is an absolute mockery of the judicial system,” the CJP’s legal head, Ratna Singh, told reporters outside the court, adding that the party would challenge the order in a higher court.

The CJP, alongside opposition parties and left-wing student organisations, has led near-daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, after 130 million names were removed from voter lists.



The Election Commission has said that the lists included 28 million people who have died, 63 million who have relocated, and 30 million who could not be traced. It denied favouring any party and said ⁠⁠wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol.

The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.

CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, student leaders and several of their supporters were also detained on Friday as ⁠⁠hundreds poured into central Delhi for a protest in support of Das and Ranka.

However, the youth-led movement insists it will not back off. A sit-in by the CJP and its supporters earlier this year forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam paper leaks.

World.title: Ex-OpenAI employee accused of planting device has Saudi backing: Prosecutor
World.content:
US federal prosecutors allege the defendant was in frequent contact with unnamed member of royal family.

An ex-OpenAI engineer accused of planting a recording device in an executive conference room at the AI company appears to have received considerable support from the Saudi government, United States prosecutors have said in a court filing.

Federal prosecutors allege that the defendant, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, was in frequent communication with an unnamed member of the Saudi royal family and that a Saudi military official paid for a one-way plane ticket for Alfozan’s wife and young son to return to Saudi Arabia after his arrest, according to the court document, made public late on Sunday.

Prosecutors made those allegations as they asked a federal judge to keep Alfozan in US custody to await trial, arguing he is a flight risk. Alfozan, a Saudi national and lawful permanent resident in the US, is scheduled to appear in federal court in San Francisco later on Monday.

The case has highlighted security challenges around sensitive AI research as companies and governments compete fiercely for an edge in the transformational technology.

“The defendant went to significant lengths to create customized, encrypted recording devices to secretly record highly sensitive meetings involving senior OpenAI personnel and executives, high-level business counterparts, and government officials, all while communicating with individuals of significance in Saudi Arabia and pursuing opportunities in — and making plans to travel to — Saudi Arabia,” prosecutors wrote in a detention memo.

The Saudi government media office did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A lawyer for Alfozan did not immediately respond to a request for comment.



The lawyer, William Pernik, previously asked for Alfozan to be released from custody, subject to conditions including location monitoring and surrendering his passport, and said Alfozan had spent the last 15 years in the US and had applied to become a citizen.

The lawyer said a planned trip by Alfozan to Saudi Arabia this month was booked before he was under investigation and was for “family and immigration reasons”, according to a court filing.

Investigation remains active

US prosecutors charged Alfozan last week with using an electronic device to intercept oral communications. Alfozan plugged a recording device into the back of a television in an executive conference room at one of OpenAI’s San Francisco buildings, according to a criminal complaint.

Meetings involving government officials took place in the conference room around the time the device was installed, according to the prosecutors’ detention memo.

Prosecutors said the investigation remains active and additional charges could be brought against Alfozan.

A member of the Saudi royal family sought to recruit Alfozan for an AI-focused role in Saudi Arabia, writing in one message, “Saudi needs you more then [sic] the US!” Alfozan replied, “100,” according to messages cited by prosecutors.

Before his arrest, Alfozan was scheduled to fly to Riyadh during a planned two-month parental leave. His wife told investigators that she and their son planned to move permanently to Saudi Arabia and that Alfozan eventually intended to join them, according to prosecutors.

In an Arabic-language interview on the Identity Capital podcast last month, Alfozan said that he visits Saudi Arabia three or four times a year, follows developments there and advises or mentors Saudi startups.

He said meeting Prince Mohammed bin Salman, then deputy crown prince, during a 2016 gathering with young Saudi tech workers in Silicon Valley persuaded him to learn at a top tech company before bringing those skills back home.

While Alfozan was working at Facebook, he and other Saudis in Silicon Valley formed a consulting initiative that linked Saudi public- and private-sector organisations with expertise in big data, the internet of things and machine learning.

OpenAI previously said it discovered the device on September 30 and referred the matter to the FBI.

Al Jazeera has reached out to the Saudi embassy for comment.

World.title: Netanyahu’s new security doctrine: Regional strategy or election ploy?
World.content:
Experts say Netanyahu’s security doctrine and map of regional alliances serve his political ambitions ahead of elections.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has unveiled an updated national security doctrine and displayed a map of rival regional alignments, signalling a security approach that prioritises preemptive military action, the expansion of buffer zones, and the pursuit of new regional partnerships.

The document was developed with the assistance of Israel’s National Security Council and published by the Prime Minister’s Office on Sunday, just nine days before Israel’s parliamentary elections that could spell the end of Netanyahu’s time in office. It outlines a formal policy of preventing perceived threats through military action rather than containment – a policy that has already been seen in action over the past few years, as Israel pursues multiple wars and attacks on its neighbours.

Electoral survival strategy

The timing of the map’s release carries particular political significance, with Netanyahu fighting to retain power amid criticism of his conduct in power, the ongoing corruption trial he faces and his handling of the October 7, 2023, attacks, as well as the wars that followed.

As the October 27 election day draws closer, Netanyahu is attempting to bolster his credentials as Israel’s ‘Mr Security’, hoping to get the votes of Israelis who may not like some of his other policies or behaviour, but still view him as the most likely leader to defend the country.

Netanyahu, who did get the endorsement of US President Donald Trump on Sunday, said during the briefing that Israel could face the possibility of a far less supportive administration in Washington in two years, after the end of the Trump presidency.



“In two years, a president… who is extremely hostile to Israel could come to power [in the United States],” Netanyahu warned.

He therefore argued that Israel must “expand our network of alliances and develop capabilities that make us a valuable asset” to other countries as a way of protecting itself if US policy towards it changed.

The comments, according to analysts, suggest that Netanyahu is seeking to portray his leadership as essential to navigating both Israel’s regional military challenges and its diplomatic isolation, all while keeping a fearful electorate reassured.

Mohanad Hage Ali, deputy director for research at the Malcolm H Kerr Carnegie Middle East Center, explained that the strategic presentation centred on competing regional blocs and buffer zones.

That framework “incubates and nurtures existential fears, which would lead Israeli voters to feel the need for a decisive leader”, Hage Ali noted.

In his assessment, Netanyahu stands to benefit from the Israeli public’s fear of regional threats by presenting himself as a familiar leader capable of managing them, making him “the devil you know”, as the analyst put it, to voters reluctant to embrace political change at a sensitive time.

Netanyahu’s political opponents have been quick to push back against that narrative.

Gadi Eisenkot, one of the prime minister’s main challengers in the upcoming election, said that the published doctrine was “two hollow pages, full of slogans that have nothing to do with a security concept”.

Another, former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, described the document as “superficial”.

Expanding security zones

The map displayed during Netanyahu’s briefing was originally published in May by Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung, a German political foundation. It divides the Middle East and parts of Africa into competing blocs, highlighting the region’s complex network of alliances and rivalries.

Those networks include states, unrecognised entities and non-state actors.

The map identifies an Israel-United Arab Emirates alignment, described as the “Hexagon Alliance”, alongside a separate grouping of Egypt, Turkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia – the latter three of which signed the Mecca mutual defence pact in August – labelled the “Sunni Diamond Alliance”. It also depicts Iran and its regional allies as a separate axis.

The map serves to illustrate the issues outlined in the published security doctrine, presenting a region where Israel faces multiple threats, the alliance that Israel is seeking to cultivate across the wider region, and the perceived need for “buffer zones” – the occupation of territory in other countries.



Israel’s existing illegal occupation of territory in Gaza and southern Lebanon illustrates the potential consequences of expanding the buffer zone approach.

Hage Ali warned that continuing to pursue an approach built around expanding military control could lead to “more conflict and more ethnic cleansing” under the guise of security buffers.

Embracing regional factions

A striking element of the map displayed by Netanyahu is its explicit designation of non-state actors as friendly entities.

The map highlights territories controlled by the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in Sudan and Khalifa Haftar’s self-styled Libyan National Army within an alignment deemed cooperative to Israel and the United Arab Emirates.

Israel views these actors as pragmatic partners or at least cooperative entities in a broader strategic grid, Hage Ali explained. However, the public association of these groups with Israel threatens to damage their domestic standing across the Arab world.

That reflects Netanyahu’s immediate priorities, where “what Israelis think matters more than the reputation of your allies and the viability of these alliances”, Hage Ali added.

The portrayal of the Middle East as a region divided into competing alliances also carries risks for Netanyahu’s broader diplomatic ambitions.

Earlier this year, Netanyahu proposed a “hexagon of alliances”, envisaging cooperation between Israel, India, Greece, Cyprus and unnamed Arab, African and Asian partners, against what he described as “radical” regional alliances.

The proposed grouping has not been established as a formal alliance, and commentators in Israel and the international press have described the project as a branding exercise rather than a binding military pact, noting that countries like India prioritise non-alignment and pragmatic trade over ideologically rigid blocs.

For Tehran and its regional partners, the map also offers potent political leverage.

Hage Ali emphasised that the visual layout “will certainly help their propaganda machine”, providing Hezbollah and other Iranian allies with evidence to reinforce the narrative that Israel seeks to expand and dominate the region.

World.title: Benny Gantz drops out of Israel’s election race
World.content:
Decision comes after polls showed his Blue and White party below the 3.25 percent threshold needed to enter the Knesset.

Benny Gantz, a former Israeli army chief and defence minister, has withdrawn from Israel’s election race after polls showed his party falling short of the threshold for entering parliament.

The leader of the Blue and White (Kahol Lavan) party announced on Monday he will not run in the October 27 polls, saying he will “continue to work for unity”.

The 67-year-old is expected to hold a news conference later on Monday.

Opinion polls in the lead-up to next week’s vote had consistently shown Gantz’s party hovering below the 3.25 percent threshold needed to enter the 120-seat Knesset, or Israel’s parliament.

A former main opposition leader, Gantz sat in a national unity government with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from 2020 to 2021.

He also joined Netanyahu’s war cabinet that was formed to oversee Israel’s genocidal war against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip after the Hamas-led attacks in southern Israel on October 7, 2023. Gantz quit the emergency cabinet in early June 2024, saying Netanyahu “is preventing us from advancing toward true victory”.
