“The CityBoy Movement, to all of you, you have done something new in Nigeria politics. You did not just gather people; you built a structure, millions of real, verifiable members,” he said.

Tinubu highlighted the group’s claimed nationwide presence, saying its structure extended from the state level to local governments, wards and polling units.

“You have a presence in every state, every local government, every ward, down to the polling units,” he said.

The President also praised the group’s engagement with young Nigerians through its call centre and community outreach initiative, CityBoy Care.

“You drilled down; a call centre that speaks to young Nigerians every day and listens to whatever their community needs. CityBoy Care, meeting members where they live,” Tinubu said.

He described the movement’s activities as evidence of organised grassroots engagement, rather than publicity-driven mobilisation.

Tinubu said the group’s efforts in reaching communities and responding to their needs had strengthened his confidence in its political mobilisation ahead of the next election.

With the movement working at the grassroots, the President said, he could return home and “sleep soundly”.

World.title: National grid stabilised after ‘multiple trippings’ – NISO
World.content:
Stock image for illustration

The Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) says it has put in place corrective measures to stabilise the national grid following multiple trippings on Monday.

The management of NISO said this on its verified X handle in Abuja.

It said: “NISO wishes to inform the public that at approximately 12:40 p. m. on Monday, the grid experienced multiple trippings on the 330 kilovolt (kV) transmission network.”

The system operator said that following the incident, it immediately implemented appropriate corrective measures to stabilise the power system and restore normal operations.

It said that restoration efforts had been successfully completed, and the grid has returned to normal operation.

”NISO wishes to clarify that the incident affected only a section of the grid, contrary to unverified reports and claims currently circulating in the media, ” it said.

According to NISO, members of the public are. therefore, advised to disregard misleading information and rely on official communication channels for accurate and verified updates on the status of the grid.

It said that NISO remains committed to maintaining grid stability, ensuring the reliable operation of the national electricity transmission system, and providing timely and accurate information to the public. (NAN)

World.title: Subsidy removal: I’ve no regret, we can’t go back to Egypt — Tinubu
World.content:
By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

President Bola Tinubu on Monday said he had no regret over the removal of fuel subsidy, insisting that Nigeria cannot return to “Egypt.”

President Tinubu also commended his son, Seyi, who is the Patron of the City Boy Movement, a political campaign structure for his re-election.

The President spoke at a forum titled, “Together till 2027: An Evening with Original City Boy,” organised by the City Boy Movement in conjunction with the “Relax, Tinubu Is Fixing Nigeria” movement, at the Old Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja.

He said: “When I walked into this hall, I did not see a crowd. I saw Nigeria. I saw why I ran for the presidency of this country. I saw why I wake up every morning to work. I saw the reason. Now, I have no regret. I saw the future that belongs to you.

“I cannot describe the situation or the elation I felt hearing from one or two of you. The words I do not often say enough, I must say tonight: thank you very much. Thank you for standing with me. The road we have walked these past three years has not been easy.

“We took hard decisions that you heard from Kashim Shettima.”

He continued: “I could listen to my political opponents promising a return to subsidy. Most of all, sometimes I remember my scripture studies, both in the Bible and the Holy Quran. When Moses left Egypt, they faced a challenge, and the Red Sea parted and gave way.

“You cannot ask Moses to go back to Egypt. We wake up with ideas, original thoughts and deep thinking to move this country forward. With your energy and support, we will never go back to Egypt.

“No regrets. Before I left home, I saw one of the greatest Chinese economic news reports, that the economy was growing by about 4.6 per cent. We are on the right trajectory. We are in good company. The economy is growing steadily. You will have a future, a future to believe in.

“Nigeria must win this election before any candidate does. You are not campaigning for me. You are campaigning for your own future, and that future is Renewed Hope. There is nothing that will push us back.”

The President noted that when he took over the helm of affairs, there was no money to pay, and the country was owing airlines.

“They were almost cutting their flights to Nigeria. Our foreign reserves were nothing. We were printing currency as if there was no tomorrow. But rather than looking back at the flaws of the past, I took the lesson. My first lesson was that I could not avoid assuming the responsibility and liabilities of my predecessor. That was a challenge.

“We rebuilt our tax system. Many said young Nigerians would turn their backs on reform. They were wrong. You are here. I came and promised one thing: that I would stop the unending strikes by ASUU, the Academic Staff Union of Universities, so that a four-year course would be completed in four years in the universities.

“We understood that a nation cannot borrow its way to greatness. You were patient when patience was hard. You defended this administration in the markets, on the campuses, in the motor parks and on social media.

“Often, when it was not popular to do so, I saw it, I noticed it, and I will never forget it. I say thank you once again to the City Boy Movement. All of you have done something new in Nigerian politics.

“You did not just gather people. You built a structure with millions of real, verifiable members, with a presence in every state, every local government, every ward, down to the polling unit. You built a call centre that speaks to young Nigerians every day and listens to whatever their communities need. City Boy Care reaches members where they live.

“That is not noise. That is organisation. That is excellent thinking. That is the kind of seriousness this country needs from its young people, and I am very proud of you. I must say so. Relax: Tinubu is fixing Nigeria.”

President Tinubu said the movement had carried its promise to every corner of the country and had told the story of the work his administration was doing when others chose to tell only half of it.

“I say thanks to every youth support group at home and abroad — from Lagos to Maiduguri, from Karu and Akwanga to Sokoto, and from London to Houston to Toronto. You carry different names, different colours and different slogans.

“No promise can be bigger than that of a better Nigeria — one Nigeria, united for one purpose, with great vision, commitment to duty, reality and fidelity to friendship. You have made an enormous contribution. I can go back home confidently tonight and sleep soundly.”

The President assured the City Boy Movement, especially the youths who had stood with him, that they would not be left behind.

“The future of this country does not belong to me, and it does not belong to my generation. It belongs to you.

“I am very proud, once again, that when I signed the Student Loan Act, I had no regrets. Today, more than a million students have been supported through NELFUND.”

On his son, Seyi, he said: “He is running after his father. Your young colleagues would have seen that you are investing your time effectively. We are with you. Thank you. You did it humbly. You did not ask for a title or an office. You went to the young people, your age mates, your group. You listened to them and organised them.

“I am proud of all of you. But I will tell you what every father tells a son: you have only started. Do more, not less. Serve harder. Set an example that your own children, my grandchildren, will be proud to follow.”

He advised the youths to ensure that every young person they knew had a Permanent Voter Card and used it.

“Tell them what we have done, and tell them what we will do. Campaign with your ideas. I came and removed subsidy on my first day. No Nigerian will go bankrupt. Yes, there was nothing left to pay for subsidy.”

The Vice President, Kashim Shettima, said Nigeria’s economy would have collapsed had President Tinubu not taken what he described as far-reaching decisions.

He said that but for the tough decisions, critics would, by now, be writing epistles about a collapsed economy from the comfort of their homes in Dubai and New York.

The Vice President credited the President’s decisions for the economy’s recovery.

He said: “The President took those far-reaching decisions. He had the courage of conviction and the knowledge to take those far-reaching decisions that repositioned the Nigerian economy, so that now the economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the last quarter.

“Most importantly, our foreign reserves are now hovering around the level of $60 billion.

“Remember how far we have come. It is only those who have been in the deepest valley that will appreciate how magnificent it is to be on a mountain top.”

To the critics of the administration, Shettima said: “The same people who are crying wolf — if the President had not taken those far-reaching decisions, wallahi, I am not talking to you as a politician; I am talking to you as a Nigerian — our economy would have collapsed.

“These people, by now, would be writing epistles about a collapsed economy from the comfort of their homes in Dubai or New York, or in marriage with their young Moroccan wives.

“I have not mentioned anybody’s name.”

He admitted that Nigerians had endured hardship but said it could have been worse.

“Your Excellency, distinguished ladies and gentlemen, the President has to be commended, not demonised.

“Yes, Nigerians have gone through some tough times, but it could have been worse.

“Be reassured that in the coming weeks, the President will come up with robust responses to agricultural challenges, and the prices of foodstuffs will certainly come down,” he stated.

The Vice President said efforts were being made to reposition the economy, citing the Nigerian Education Loan Fund and investments in infrastructure. He then urged the youth to carry the message to the streets.

“I urge the youth of Nigeria. I beseech thee. I implore you to go out to the streets and tell the truth to other Nigerians,” he stated.

On his part, the Director-General of the City Boy Movement, Hon. Francis Shoga, said: “I stand before you today on behalf of the leadership and the entire members of the City Boy Movement.

“Mr President, we stand before you with a clear, powerful and unshakable message: the youths of Nigeria are ready. We are ready to work. We are ready to serve. We are ready to live, and we are ready to take purposeful action for the progress, unity and prosperity of our great nation.

“We are not a generation waiting helplessly on the sidelines. We are not a generation without direction, courage or purpose. We are a generation prepared to rise above every limitation, organise with discipline, confront challenges with courage and build the Nigeria of our dreams.

“Your Excellency, we are your foot soldiers, ambassadors of hope, defenders of our national unity and committed partners in the great task ahead of national transformation. Whatever young Nigerians have found, we will carry the message of Renewed Hope.

“We will inspire confidence, promote patriotism, encourage responsible participation and transform belief into action. This is our calling. This is our duty. And this is our moment to serve Nigeria.

“Your Excellency, the City Boy Movement draws its inspiration from the courage, persistence, patriotism, visionary leadership and bold decision-making that have defined your political journey and public service.

“Our mission is to inform, engage, inspire and empower Nigerian youths so that they understand the direction of government, recognise available opportunities and participate confidently and responsibly in national development.”

World.title: 2027: Amupitan assures INEC workers of improved welfare, remuneration
World.content:
INEC Chair, Joash Amupitan

The National Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan (SAN), has assured its staff members of improved welfare and remuneration ahead of the 2027 general elections.

Amupitan gave the assurance while addressing INEC Staff in the South-East on preparedness for the 2027 General Elections in Enugu on Monday.

The chairman came on a working visit to interact with traditional rulers and electoral stakeholders of the South-East.

He urged the staff to steer clear of partisan politics, adding: “You should not pick interest in any political party: be neutral and firm”.

“I am hearing that some of you are showing interest in some political parties. This is absolutely wrong.

“The commission wants you to be neutral and professional both in your words and actions.

“The commission will not take unprofessional or unethical electoral conduct from any staff.

“We have instituted a reward and sanction mechanism at local government area, state and to even national level,” he said.

The chairman said that the commission was working relentlessly to improve the welfare of its staff across all cadres and levels.

He claimed that the commission had worked hard to remove its staff from the normal civil service salary structure to a special salary structure.

“This new special salary structure will take effect from Jan. 1, 2027 and it is for the benefit of staff across all cadres and levels.

“We want the new salary structure so that you will not be easily induced by anybody before, during and after the elections.

“We are working with other relevant governmental agencies and commissions to make the cash backing for the new salary structure possible,” he said

He urged all staff to ensure that they returned the trust of the people to the commission’s programmes and activities.

“As an unbiased umpire, we need to up the confidence and trust the people repose on us by being disciplined and diligent to our duties at all times,” he said.

Amupitan also said the commission was making provisions for logistics and had already given INEC Enugu office 10 new pick-up vans.

“More logistics are coming as we ensure adequate preparation for the general elections.

“We have got our non-sensitive materials ready; while we are awarding contracts for other materials needed in the election as well as sensitive materials as well.

“Massive training and retraining will commence soon and the retraining is imperative given new guidelines and regulations introduced into the Amended Electoral Act,” he added.

Over 600 staff from INEC offices within the South-East attended the event.

(NAN)

World.title: Saudi Arabia executes Bangladeshi newlyweds over mosque kiss
World.content:
By Efe Onodjae

Two Bangladeshi nationals, identified as Nazrul Islam Abdul Basir and Siri Akhtar, have reportedly been executed in Saudi Arabia following their conviction over an alleged immoral act inside a mosque in Mecca.

Reports circulating on social media and seen by Vanguard showed that Bangladesh claimed the couple, who had travelled to Mecca for their honeymoon, were accused of kissing on the forehead inside the mosque.

The gesture was reportedly an expression of gratitude to Allah for their marriage.

The reports further claimed that the couple’s bodies had been returned to Bangladesh in two coffins for burial.

World.title: NAF airstrike kills ISWAP leaders in Lake Chad
World.content:
By Kingsley Omonobi

Precision strikes by the Nigerian Air Force (NAF), operating under Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), have neutralised scores of ISWAP terrorists in the Lake Chad region following the interdiction of an identified terrorist hideout on Monday.

Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, Director of NAF Public Relations, said the operation underscores the NAF’s sustained commitment to degrading terrorist networks, disrupting their logistics and enhancing security across Nigeria’s North-East.

According to him, “Preliminary post-strike assessments indicate that several prominent Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters were neutralised.

“They include individuals identified as key figures within the group’s security structure and leadership Council, like Jindullah, reportedly the Chief Security Guard and confidant of Abu Saleem as well as Abul KissaI, a member of ISWAP Shura Council.

“The strike also destroyed logistical assets, including boat engines and motorcycles, believed to support the group’s movement and operational activities.

“The operation demonstrates the NAF’s intense effort to conduct intelligence-led precision strikes against terrorist enclaves concealed within difficult terrain.

“By neutralising key operatives and destroying critical logistical resources, the strike delivers a significant setback to ISWAP’s operational capability, further constraining its ability to coordinate activities and threaten vulnerable communities.

“Commenting on the success, the Chief of the Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, reaffirmed the NAF’s resolve to sustain decisive air operations against terrorist networks in support of ongoing efforts to restore peace and stability across the country.

“The Nigerian Air Force remains committed to working closely with sister Services and other security agencies to consolidate operational gains, protect vulnerable communities and advance efforts towards lasting peace and security in the North-East.”

World.title: ‘I’m very proud of you’  —  Tinubu showers praise on CityBoy Movement
World.content:
By Bayo Wahab

President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday praised the City Boy Movement for what he described as a new model of political organisation in Nigeria, telling its members he was “very proud” of them.

The President spoke at the State House during a ceremonial meeting with the group and the Relax Tinubu is Fixing Nigeria (RTIFN) support group.

Addressing members of the movement, Tinubu said the group had introduced something new to the country’s politics by going beyond mobilising crowds.

“The CityBoy Movement, to all of you, you have done something new in Nigeria politics. You did not just gather people; you built a structure, millions of real, verifiable members,” the President said.

He highlighted the group’s national spread, noting that it has “a presence in every state, every local government, every ward, down to the polling units.”

The President also commended the movement’s engagement with young people, citing its call centre and its community outreach programme, CityBoy Care.

“You drilled down; a call center that speaks to young Nigerians every day and listen to whatever their community needs. CityBoy Care, meeting members where they live,” he said.

Tinubu described the group’s approach as organised and purposeful, rather than the product of mere publicity.

“That is not noise. That is organisation. That is excellent thinking. That is the kind of seriousness this country needs from its young people, and I’m very proud of you. I must say so,” he said.

The President also thanked members for defending his administration publicly, including at moments when doing so carried a political cost.

“You were patient when patience was hard. You defended this administration in the market, on the campuses, at the motorparks and on social media even when it was not popular to do so,” Tinubu said.

He added that their loyalty had not gone unnoticed.

“I saw it, I noticed, and I will never forget it. I say thank you once again,” the President said.

The City Boy Movement was founded by the President’s son, Seyi Tinubu, who is also its patron.

World.title: Nigeria Showcases Renewed Hope Housing PPP Model at Continental Forum, Attracts Replication Interest from Afrcian Countries
World.content:
The Federal Government has showcased its Renewed Hope Housing Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model at a continental forum in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, attracting interest from African countries seeking to replicate the initiative in their housing programmes.

The presentation was made by the Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC), Dr Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh, at the Second Forum for Public-Private Partnership Units in Africa, held at Africa Hall, United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA), with delegations from 36 countries in attendance.

According to a press release issued by Ifeanyi Nwoko, ICRC Acting Head, Media and Publicity, on Monday, the forum was co-organised by the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa, the African Development Bank (AfDB) and the African Legal Support Facility under the theme, “Making Social Sector PPPs Work: From Policy Ambition to Effective Service Delivery”.

The forum focused on how public-private partnerships could support the delivery of affordable housing, healthcare, education, sanitation and water services across the continent.

Nigeria was among five countries that presented projects at the forum’s project clinic, alongside Malawi, Kenya, Djibouti and Côte d’Ivoire.

Speaking on Nigeria’s housing initiative, Ewalefoh explained that the Renewed Hope Cities programme would deliver 100,000 housing units across selected cities in the country through a joint venture concession involving the private sector.

“The beauty of this PPP structure is that it is not the conventional PPP. In this case, the private party owns the land, has the design, is financing it and is doing the construction,” he said.

He explained that under President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, the government’s responsibility was to reduce the risks that could discourage private investment in housing.

“The PPP here is that government agreed to de-risk the project,” Ewalefoh said.



The ICRC director-general noted that commercial lending rates in Nigeria, which exceed 23 per cent, had made housing finance expensive for developers and prospective homeowners.

To address the challenge, the government introduced measures to reduce investment risks and improve affordability. These include designating middle-income federal civil servants as off-takers, committing to the construction of access roads to semi-urban project sites, and providing access to concessionary financing.

The Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria unlocked about $19 million in single-digit interest funding, while the Family Homes Fund provided a further $20 million in concessionary loans.

Additionally, buyers benefit from lower mortgage rates through an approximately $112 million MOFI Real Estate Investment Fund. The government also negotiated sale prices with the developer to keep the houses affordable and imposed a limit of one housing unit per buyer to discourage speculation.

According to the statement, the measures reduced the effective cost of the project by about 30 per cent.

The financing arrangement enables the government to facilitate housing delivery without directly financing the construction costs. About $39 million in concessionary funding is helping to unlock a project with construction costs of approximately $125 million in private-sector investment.

“Government does not need to finance housing capital projects. It can crowd in private capital through policy, land availability and off-taker facilitation to create a replicable, scalable model for housing delivery,” Ewalefoh told delegates.

The model generated considerable interest during the question-and-answer session, with delegates seeking to understand how Nigeria’s risk-reduction mechanisms, particularly the off-taker guarantee and access to concessionary finance, could be adapted to their respective countries.

The forum also provided an opportunity for participating countries to exchange experiences on social-sector PPP projects, including their successes, challenges, risk allocation and implementation strategies.

The ICRC said the discussions would also benefit Nigeria, as the country’s delegation drew lessons from other countries’ projects to inform the development of its own social-sector PPP pipeline.

The forum builds on its inaugural edition in 2024, which brought together more than 30 African PPP units to discuss climate-resilient infrastructure. This year’s edition featured heads of PPP units, development finance institutions, private operators and transaction advisers examining ways to make social infrastructure projects financially sustainable and affordable for citizens.

World.title: Bauchi NDC Gubernatorial Candidate Dumps Party
World.content:
Segun Awofadeji in Bauchi

The National Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in Bauchi State for the 2027 general elections, Barrister Ibrahim Muhammad Kashim, has resigned his membership of the party with immediate effect.

Kashim announced his resignation in a letter dated October 16, 2026, addressed to the chairman of the NDC in Bauchi local government area of Bauchi State which was made available to Journalists on Monday.

In the letter, he said his decision followed careful consideration and was based on personal reasons.

“I hereby formally tender my resignation from the National Democratic Congress (NDC), effective from the date of this letter,” he stated.

Kashim expressed appreciation to the party’s leadership and members for the opportunity to be associated with the NDC.

According to him, “This decision has been taken after careful consideration and is a matter of personal choice. I wish to express my appreciation to the party leadership and members for the opportunity to have been associated with the NDC.

“I respectfully request that my resignation be acknowledged and that the necessary records be updated accordingly. Please accept the assurances of my highest regards,” he concluded.

Kashim, a former Secretary to the Bauchi State Government (SSG) under Governor Bala Abdukadir Mohammed’s administration, was among the 15 governorship candidates recently listed by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the 2027 general elections in the state.

Recall that the NDC had presented Ibrahim Muhammad Kashim as its governorship candidate, with Tata Alhaji as his running mate, for the 2027 governorship election in Bauchi State.

As at press time, the party leadership was yet to react to the resignation.

Meanwhile, in a message to his supporters, Kashim said his exit from the NDC does not diminish his commitment to the struggle for a better Bauchi State.

According to him, the state deserves purposeful leadership, a stronger economy, greater opportunities for youths and women, improved security and a future where every citizen can live with dignity.

The former SSG assured that his political journey is far from over and his commitment to the rescue and development of the state remains unwavering.

He said he would continue to engage with well-meaning individuals and groups who share his vision of a peaceful, prosperous and economically vibrant Bauchi.

He said the next phase of his political movement would be communicated in due course and urged his supporters to remain calm, steadfast and united.

World.title: Kwara Doctors Among Least Paid in Nigeria, Says NMA
World.content:
The Nigeria Medical Association (NMA), Kwara Chapter, has expressed concern that Kwara doctors are among the least paid in the country.

The Chairman, Dr Suleiman Rotimi stated this on Monday in Ilorin while speaking at a news conference organised as part of the activities for the 2026 Physician’s Week.

The theme of the week is entitled: “Securing The Future of Medicine in Nigeria.”

Rotimi raised concerns over manpower shortages, poor welfare, excessive workload and alleged unauthorised salary deductions affecting doctors in the state.

According to him, some general hospitals have only a few doctors, forcing them to work long hours and increasing the risk of burnout.

“The doctors are underpaid, overworked and over-deducted.

“Some doctors have between N30,000 and N50,000 deducted from their monthly salaries, despite unpaid allowances and poor remuneration,” he lamented.

The NMA-Kwara chairman appealed to the state government to address the issues urgently, stating that “Nigeria’s doctor-to-patient ratio is about one doctor to more than 9,000 patients, with the situation worse in some parts of Kwara.”

“The recommendations from World Health Organisation is one doctor to 600 patients,” he said.

On the ongoing industrial dispute involving doctors in Kwara, Rotimi said the association had engaged the state government and other stakeholders but remains open to dialogue.

“When two elephants fight, it is the grass that suffers. The patients are the ones suffering from this,” he said.

He also called for improved mental health support, confidential medical services, safer workplaces, and protection against violence, adding that doctors should be allowed to seek help without stigma.

Similarly, he advocated that doctors should explore the use of telemedicine, artificial intelligence and robotics, while observing that these innovations will complement and help professionals in the medical field.

He noted that technology could help specialists reach underserved communities while maintaining clinical oversight.

The NMA chairman also urged the government to improve doctors’ pay, working conditions, training, research opportunities, and infrastructure to reduce the migration of Nigerian doctors abroad.

He called for collective action to build a healthcare system where doctors work in safe and dignified conditions and patients receive quality care.

The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that some of the activities organised for the physician week include scientific conferences and NMA Charity Day. (NAN)

World.title: Uduaghan Was a Detribalised Leader, Says Oborevwori
World.content:
Gov. Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta has expressed sadness over the death of former Gov. Emmanuel Uduaghan.

Oborevwori in a condolence statement on Monday by his Chief Press Secretary, Mr Festus Ahon, described the former governor as a “detribalised” leader whose contributions to the development of the state would not be forgotten.

He sympathised with the late governor’s wife, Roli, his children, the entire Uduaghan family, Itsekiri people and Delta residents over the painful loss.

The governor recalled Uduaghan’s years in office, noting that he made significant contributions to infrastructure development in the state.

Oborevwori described the former governor as a leader who looked beyond ethnic differences and worked for the overall development of Delta.

He said that Uduaghan’s years in public service had left a good mark on the state, and his death was a loss to Delta and the country at large.

He prayed for the peaceful repose of the former governor’s sou.

Recall that Uduaghan served as Commissioner for Health beetween 1999 and 2003, Secretary to the State Government from 2003 to 2007 before serving as governor of the state between 2007 and 2015.

According to a statement earlier issued on Monday by the family, Uduaghan died on Oct.19, at the age of 71(NAN)

World.title: Ochei Mourns Former Gov Uduaghan
World.content:
Mr Victor Ochei, Former Speaker of the Delta House of Assembly, and the the Delta North Senatorial candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has mourned former Gov. Emmanuel Uduaghan, describing his death as a loss to Delta and Nigeria.

The former speaker in a tribute made available to the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) on Monday in Asaba, said Uduaghan’s contributions to governance, institutional development, peace and infrastructure remained significant in the state’s history.

Ochei who served as speaker during Uduaghan’s administration between 2011 and 2014, recalled their working relationship and shared commitment to democratic governance and the development of the state.

He described the former governor as a calm and purposeful leader who combined political experience with an understanding of governance challenges.

He said Uduaghan’s Delta Beyond Oil initiative reflected his commitment to economic diversification and sustainable development.

He also highlighted the late former governor’s contributions to peace and security in the Niger Delta, particularly his efforts to promote stability in the region.

According to him, Uduaghan’s administration expanded free maternal and under-five healthcare services and invested in education through model schools and scholarship programmes.

Ochei listed the development of the Asaba International Airport and road networks among the infrastructure projects associated with Uduaghan’s administration.

He said the late former governor also valued dialogue, consensus-building and institutional cooperation in the pursuit of good governance.

Ochei described his death as a painful loss to his immediate family, Delta and Nigeria, adding that his public service contributions would remain part of the state’s history.

He extended his condolences to the wife of the deceased, children, the Uduaghan family, the Itsekiri nation and the people of Delta.

He prayed God to grant the deceased eternal rest and comfort his family and others mourning him.(NAN)

World.title: Q3 2026: Transcorp Hotels Widens Margins, Grows Profit Before Tax to ₦22.5bn
World.content:
Transcorp Hotels Plc (NGX: TRANSCOHOT), the hospitality subsidiary of Transnational Corporation Plc (Transcorp Group), has announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026, reporting a profit before tax (PBT) of ₦22.5 billion, up 1 per cent from ₦22.4 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

Profit after tax (PAT) grew by 5 per cent to ₦15.5 billion, compared with ₦14.8 billion in the previous year.

Revenue stood at ₦69.5 billion, representing a 3 per cent year-on-year decline from ₦71.3 billion recorded in the corresponding period of 2025.

Administrative expenses fell by 2 per cent to ₦29.3 billion from ₦29.9 billion, reflecting continued cost optimisation, while net finance cost declined by 35 per cent to ₦1.5 billion from ₦2.3 billion.

Total assets rose by 29 per cent to ₦206.8 billion from ₦159.9 billion as of December 2025, while shareholders’ funds grew to ₦97.5 billion.

The company said the results reflected its ability to sustain profitability and strengthen its financial position through disciplined execution, effective resource management and a continued commitment to delivering hospitality services.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Transcorp Hotels Plc, Uzoamaka Oshogwe, said the third-quarter performance demonstrated the company’s earnings discipline, noting that it grew profit after tax by 5 per cent despite a 3 per cent decline in revenue.

“Despite a 3% year-on-year decline in revenue, we grew profit after tax by 5% and expanded our net profit margin to 22.3%. We are converting revenue into stronger profits, protecting margins, and building a more resilient business,” she said.

Oshogwe said the company was directing capital towards opportunities across its hospitality, events and lifestyle businesses, with investments assessed against financial and return benchmarks.

“As we close the year, our priorities remain clear: sustain margin growth, deepen guest and client engagement, and position the business to maximise returns as demand strengthens. We remain focused on profitable growth, disciplined execution, and long-term value creation,” she added.

The Chief Finance Officer of Transcorp Hotels Plc, Oluwatobiloba Ojediran, said the quality of the company’s earnings improved during the period, supported by lower finance costs and controlled administrative expenses.

He said net finance cost declined by 35 per cent to ₦1.5 billion, representing about 2 per cent of revenue, compared with more than 3 per cent a year earlier, while administrative expenses remained below the previous year’s level.

Ojediran added that the growth in total assets to ₦206.8 billion and shareholders’ funds of ₦97.5 billion reflected the company’s expanding balance sheet.

He said the company was managing its liabilities and funding costs while maintaining a prudent capital structure to ensure that future growth was supported by sustainable financing and clear investment-return thresholds.

Transcorp Hotels said it continued to strengthen its hospitality and lifestyle portfolio, with Transcorp Hilton Abuja serving business and leisure travellers.

Transcorp Centre, the company’s 5,000-seat event and conference venue, also continues to support Abuja’s position as a destination for major corporate, cultural and social events.

World.title: COAS: Rwandan Genocide Offers Profound Lessons for Nigeria
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Army Staff (COAS), Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu has said that the Rwandan genocide offers profound lessons for Nigeria on the importance of national unity, tolerance, peaceful coexistence and conflict prevention.

Lieutenant General Shaibu, stated this on Monday during a visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial in Rwanda as part of his ongoing official working visit to the country.

According to a statement by the Acting Director of Army Public Relations, Colonel Appolonia Anele, the visit underscored the devastating consequences of ethnic hatred, religious intolerance, divisive rhetoric and violent extremism.

She said the memorial, which houses the remains of approximately 250,000 victims of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, serves as a solemn reminder of the dangers of unchecked hatred, political manipulation and national disunity.

“Rwanda’s tragic history reinforces the need for Nigerians to rise above ethnic, religious and political differences, reject hate speech, and embrace tolerance, patriotism and collective responsibility for national peace and stability,” the COAS said.

The visit further highlighted the importance of responsible leadership, early conflict prevention and sustained civil-military cooperation, reaffirming that national unity remains the foundation of lasting peace, security and development.

Similarly, the COAS also visited Rwanda’s Campaign Against Genocide Museum in Kigali as part of his official working visit to Rwanda.

Colonel Anele said the visit highlighted the importance of civilian protection, decisive military action and collective responsibility in combating genocide and other forms of criminality.

“The museum chronicles the role of the Rwandan Patriotic Army in ending the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, offering valuable lessons on safeguarding innocent lives, upholding human rights and fostering national unity.

“The experience reinforces the imperative for Nigerians to rise above ethnic, religious and political differences and unite with security agencies against threats to national peace and stability,” the statement said.

The Army spokesperson concluded that the visit further underscored the Nigerian Army’s commitment to civilian protection and solidarity with the people of Rwanda and the Rwanda Defence Force.

World.title: Alleged Wiretapping: El-Rufai Loses N120m Right Enforcement Suit against DSS, Others
World.content:
Alex Enumah in Abuja

A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Monday, dismissed the fundamental rights suit filed by the immediate past governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai against the Department of the State Service (DSS) and three others.

Justice Sylvanus Oriji in a judgment dismissed the suit for being incompetent and lacking in merit.

Meanwhile, the court has awarded N200, 000 cost of litigation in favour of each of the respondents.

Recall that the ex governor and chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), had sued the DSS, Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Independent Corrupt Practices and other related offences Commission (ICPC) and the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) to court, over alleged breach of his fundamental rights.

Recall that el-Rufai has been in custody of the security agencies since his arrest in February this year, for allegedly tapping the phone lines of the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu.

Delivering judgment in the suit on Monday, trial judge, Justice Oriji however dismissed the suit on the grounds among others, that the letters of invitation by the two federal government agencies to El-Rufai to appear for investigation over allegations against him met constitutional requirement and did not in anyway constitute infringement on his fundamental rights.

According to the judge, both the EFCC and ICPC did not violate the applicant’s rights with the letters inviting him to shed light on issues raised against him.

On whether the attempt to arrest the applicant at Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport, Abuja by the DSS (3rd respondent) violated his rights, the court upheld the DSS submission that it had statutory mandate to maintain watchlist action and arrest persons of interest.

The ourt further held El-Rufai cannot use the court to stop the agencies from performing their duties.

Justice Oriji discountenanced El-Rufai’s argument that there was no warrant for his attempted arrest and ruled that DSS had inherent powers of the police pursuant to SSS instrument and NSA Act.

On whether the seizure of the applicant’s international passport by the DSS was a violation of his rights, the court held that it was satisfied that the seizure was lawful and pursuant to the powers of the DSS and thus the applicant had failed to adduce evidence showing that the seizure was continuous, permanent and unlawful.

While dismissing the entire suit for lacking in merit the Court awarded N200, 000 to each of the four respondents.

World.title: IEC promises glitch-free 2026 local government elections
World.content:
2026 local government elections are just two weeks away, along with the additional public holiday given to South Africans. For those who’ve been living under a rock, 2026 local government elections take place on Wednesday 4 November 2026.

Better still, the Electoral Commission (IEC) insists everything will go off without a hitch, so you won’t be wasting too much time in queues on your bonus day off. Nevertheless, there are still a few things you can do to make the process as timeous as possible …

2026 LOCAL GOVERNMENT ELECTIONS

At a recent event in Midrand, all participating parties committed to the electoral code of conduct. IEC chairperson Mosotho Moepya said the commission had worked on its voter management devices after being made ‘painfully aware of the technical challenges in 2024.’ Contrary to the massive delays two years ago, both voter registration weekends ahead of 2026 local government elections went ‘exceptionally well,’ said Moepya.



As such, the IEC confirms that:

The results system has completed end-to-end testing.

Parties verified this with independent experts between 5 and 12 October .

. Voting station layouts have been improved to speed up queues.

More than 60 000 staff have been trained.

MIDRAND OPERATIONS CENTRE FAILURE

There are a few precautions you can take before voting that could save you time on the day. Image: File

Back In 2024, the results leaderboards at the Midrand operations centre failed for about two hours. The IEC insisted the results weren’t affected, but it did lead to a number of parties challenging the validity of the election. Furthermore, the embattled ANC claims technical glitches on its online platform stopped it from submitting its full councillor list recently.

This accusation was disproved in the Electoral Court. However, the ANC is escalating the matter to the Constitutional Court. Separately, the IEC has approved 2.6 million special-vote applications have been approved. It also warns of fake voting information and bogus announcements online, so stick to official IEC channels only.

HOW TO VOTE IN 2026 LOCAL GOVERNMENT ELECTIONS

Before you cast your vote in the 2026 local government election, check your nearest station. In this iteration, you can only vote at the station where you’re registered, even if you’ve moved. SMS your ID number to 32810, or WhatsApp ‘Hi’ to 060 088 0000. If you’re not on the voters’ roll, it’s too late, you can’t vote.

On the day, a fortnight from now, bring your valid identify document: A smart ID card, a green barcoded ID book or a valid temporary ID certificate will all be accepted.

Note that driver’s licences, passports, student cards and photocopies of IDs will not be.

Voting stations are open from 7am to 9pm on 4 November , but may stay open longer if necessary.

, but may stay open longer if necessary. Approved special voters can do so on 2 and 3 November , 8am to 5pm.

, 8am to 5pm. At the station. An official will check your ID against the roll, you receive your ballots, and your indelible thumbnail ink mark.

Finally, SASSA beneficiaries should note that payment dates were moved to 30 October, 2 November and 3 November, so grants no longer land on voting day for 2026 local government elections.



But what do you think? Do you think voting will be glitch free like the IEC promises? Did you have a good experience during the 2024 national elections? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Beachgoers and anglers: Here’s what Tuesday’s tides look like
World.content:
Beachgoers and anglers can check Tuesday’s high and low tide times before planning activities along South Africa’s coastline. Image: Unsplash

If you’re heading to the coast on Tuesday, check the tide times before planning your activities.

Water levels change throughout the day, while wind, waves, swell and the shape of the seabed also affect conditions along the shore and at sea.

Damaging winds and waves along the KZN coast

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for damaging winds and waves along the KwaZulu-Natal coastline



These conditions could temporarily disrupt beachfront activities and operations at small harbours and ports until Tuesday morning.

Beachgoers, anglers and others planning coastal activities should follow the latest weather warnings and check local sea conditions before heading out.

When to expect the next spring tide

Spring tides are important to watch out for because they bring higher high tides and lower low tides than usual.



The next spring tide is expected around the full moon on Monday, 26 October 2026.

These changes can affect swimming, surfing and fishing. High tides may cover rocks and reefs, while low tides expose more of the shoreline.

Check the tide times and the latest weather and marine warnings before you head to the coast.

World.title: ‘Half a loaf is better than nothing’: Why some SASSA recipients are saying thank you
World.content:
Not every SASSA grant recipient met festive season payment news with anger. A number of South Africans used the moment to express gratitude for the support they receive.

The comments, posted on The South African’s Facebook page, offer a different side to a conversation dominated by frustration over grant amounts.

‘At least we are receiving something’

Mpho Joyce put it simply. “Half a loaf is better than nothing thank you,” she wrote, adding a smiling and praying emoji.



Zandile Macu shared a more personal reason for her thanks, pointing to the role grants play in single-parent households.

“I just want to appreciate and thank you, SASSA, for helping us when there is no father at home, at least we are receiving something rather than nothing. “keep it up guys” Keep it up, guys, with good work,” she wrote.

Macu’s comment highlights how the Child Support Grant often serves as a lifeline for mothers raising children alone.

Faith and perspective from the SASSA recipients

Some commenters turned to faith. Christelle Van Biljon wrote in Afrikaans: “SE Liewers dnk Vir GOD wat one help,” which loosely translates to a call to rather thank God for the help received.

Olivia Hossell focused on older recipients, writing: “This can help the elderly.” Francina Radebe kept it short with a simple “Thanks.”

The December bonus question

Not everyone was fully satisfied. Nokuthula Bhanana raised a question many recipients ask every year.



“Sassa suppose to give an extra money in December, is that too much?” she wrote.

The idea of a December bonus or “13th cheque” for grant recipients circulates widely each year, but SASSA has repeatedly dismissed such claims. Recipients should rely only on official SASSA channels for information about payments and be wary of social media posts promising extra money.

Bhanana’s question shows how even grateful recipients feel the pressure of the festive season.

The mixed reactions reveal a divided community. While some recipients feel the grants fall far short of what they need, others see them as essential support that keeps their households going, especially in homes with no other income.

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.

Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: Four Springboks in doubt for the end-of-year tour
World.content:
Four Tests for the Springboks in November will form part of the conclusion to the Nations Championship tournament, which will see Rassie Erasmus’ team face Italy, France and Ireland as well as one final opponent at the end of November.

It will be interesting to see what selection options Erasmus opts for when it comes to these fixtures, while the medical staff will need to weigh up a few concerning injuries.

Recently, the Sharks confirmed that Eben Etzebeth had “lower limb injury” and that they were now “awaiting a further medical examination to determine the extent of the injury”.



Although there have been no further updates since then, it does seem that Etzebeth could be set for another spell on the sidelines, and could quite possibly be in doubt for the end-of-year tour.

The Springboks have also missed the services of RG Snyman and Kwagga Smith throughout this season due to serious knee injuries, and neither player is expected to be fit in time to return as soon as November.

Adding to this, it’s also likely that Cheslin Kolbe could be in doubt for the tour after he broke his jaw during Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series.



The Springboks are set to regroup at the end of October before heading abroad for their first of four Tests to conclude the Nations Championship.

Springboks’ end-of-year fixtures

Saturday 7 November: Italy v Boks Venue: Allianz Stadium, Turin Kick off: 16:00

Italy v Boks Friday 13 November: France v Boks Venue: Stade de France, Paris Kick off: 22:00

France v Boks Saturday 21 November: Ireland v Boks Venue: Aviva Stadium, Dublin Kick off: 19:30

Ireland v Boks 27–29 November: Finals Weekend Venue: Twickenham Stadium, London Kick off: TBC

Finals Weekend

How does the finals weekend work?

For the Nations Championship, across remaining pool matches in November, teams from the southern and northern hemisphere will continue to compete against each other. Points earned from those matches determine a final one to six ranking for each hemisphere’s table, and the finals weekend pairs each team against their direct equivalent rank from the opposite conference.

So, during the finals weekend, teams play a seventh and final match against their exact equivalent seed from the opposite hemisphere (e.g. sixth vs sixth, fifth vs fifth, down to the first vs first Grand Final).

World.title: Two shoebills, one canoe: Isak Pretorius wins at Wildlife Photographer of the Year, again
World.content:
South African wildlife photographer Isak Pretorius has won the Behaviour: Birds category at Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026. Image: The African Photographer

South African photographer Isak Pretorius has done it again.

He was exploring a swamp in a narrow canoe when he spotted something remarkable.

Not one, but two of Africa’s most elusive birds.



That moment has now won him one of the world’s most prestigious wildlife photography awards.

Pretorius won the Behaviour: Birds category at the Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026 competition, run by the Natural History Museum in London.

The winners were announced on 13 October.

THE WINNING IMAGE

Pretorius’s image, Scenes from the Swamp, shows two shoebill storks among wetland vegetation.

He was exploring the swamp in a narrow canoe with a guide, and felt exceptionally lucky to see two of the elusive birds at once.

In winning entries of wildlife photographer for the year 2026,Isak Pretorius captures two shoebill storks collecting nesting materials in Mabamba swamp,Uganda, highlighting the beauty of rare wildlife.#RongoPhotojournalism2026 pic.twitter.com/Mk8fYaNmQh  October 15, 2026

WHY SHOEBILLS ARE SO SPECIAL

Shoebills are among Africa’s most sought-after birds for wildlife lovers and photographers.

They’re known for their huge, shoe-shaped bills, which they use to catch prey such as catfish and lungfish in the swamps where they live.

They’re also hard to find, and face threats including fires, disturbance and the illegal live bird trade, according to research by the University of Cape Town’s FitzPatrick Institute of African Ornithology.

A SECOND WIN FOR ISAK PRETORIUS

It’s not Pretorius’s first time on the winners’ list.

In 2013, he became the first South African to win the bird behaviour category, with an image of a noddy bird trapped in a spider web.

Pretorius is a specialist wildlife photography guide. He says he uses his images to raise awareness about conservation.

“In showing people the beauty of wildlife, they will care more about it,” he has said. “That’s our best chance of protecting it.”

A STRONG YEAR FOR SOUTHERN AFRICA

Southern Africa featured strongly in this year’s awards.

The overall winner, Italian photographer Federico Veronesi, won with The Aftermath, a black-and-white image of an elephant carrying a dead calf in Namibia.

The Young Wildlife Photographer of the Year title went to Oscar Whitfield, a British photographer living in Zimbabwe, for Labour of Love, an eye-level image of a dung beetle pushing its cargo through the sand.

SOUTH AFRICA’S WINNING STREAK

It’s another proud moment for South African wildlife photography.

Last year, South Africa’s Wim van den Heever was named the overall Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2025, for a ghostly image of a rare brown hyena in a deserted diamond mining town.

THE COMPETITION IN NUMBERS

This year’s competition attracted 65,403 entries.

An international panel judged the images anonymously, looking for originality, technical excellence, ethical practice and creativity.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs’ worrying CAF away record as Da Cruz makes excuses
World.content:
After Kaizer Chiefs suffered a 1-0 defeat to Red Arrows in Zambia, their struggles away from home in the CAF Confederation Cup appear to be far from over.

Amakhosi lost three away matches in the competition last season. Defeats to Egyptian sides Al Masry and Zamalek ultimately contributed to their group-stage exit.

Their latest setback means Kaizer Chiefs have now lost four of their last five away matches in the CAF Confederation Cup, raising concerns about their ability to compete consistently on the continental stage.



Head coach Fernando Da Cruz admitted that his team lacked aggression in the first half against Red Arrows, which made it difficult for them to compete effectively.

“We played a tough first half with no aggression. We were not there inside the duels,” Da Cruz said as per KickOff.

Kaizer Chiefs CAF struggles continue

The French coach acknowledged that his side improved after the break but conceded that they struggled to create enough scoring opportunities.

“In the second half, it was better. We didn’t create a lot of chances, but we made a better second half,” he added.

Da Cruz also pointed to the playing surface as one of the challenges his team faced in Zambia, arguing that the pitch made it difficult for Chiefs to implement their preferred style of play.

“About the field, it was not a field for our advantage. It was not a very good field for us to develop our model game,” he said.



The Amakhosi coach, however, acknowledged that his team needed to adapt to the conditions rather than use them as an excuse for the defeat.

“But we must adapt, we must play with the conditions and the players adapted very well to the conditions,” Da Cruz added.

Kaizer Chiefs must now overturn the 1-0 deficit in the return leg in South Africa if they are to secure a place in the CAF Confederation Cup group stages.

Amakhosi will need to win by at least two clear goals to qualify directly. A one-goal victory would level the aggregate score and send the tie to a penalty shootout if the score remains level after extra time, where applicable.

Can Chiefs make it to the next round?

Reutlwile is a public no-fee school, while Regina Mundi is one of Soweto’s most prominent churches.

Emergency teams are assessing structural damage and any risk to nearby residents.

World.title: World Athletics puts ASA on notice
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - World Athletics has put Athletics South Africa (ASA) on notice, giving them six months to adopt a revised Constitution and hold fresh elections.

In a letter to Athletics South Africa leaked to eNCA, World Athletics has appointed Zakhele Dlamini, President of the Southern African Confederation of Athletics, to oversee its directives.

This follows findings earlier this month by ASA's disciplinary panel, which found suspended President James Moloi guilty of the misuse of funds and recommended Moloi's removal.

READ | Cape Town Marathon becomes Africa's first Abbott world major race

No action has yet been taken against Moloi by ASA.

The letter goes on to say that failure to adopt a revised ASA Constitution within the prescribed six-month period would have far-reaching consequences.

This may include the suspension of ASA, a measure which would impact South African athletes on the world stage.

World.title: Bronkhorstspruit Water Crisis: Tshwane deploys 36 water tankers
World.content:
PRETORIA - Strict measures have been issued to the City of Tshwane (CoT) after it failed to warn residents of Bronkhorstspruit, Pretoria East, that their water was unsafe.

More than 400 cases of gastrointestinal illness have been reported in the area since early this month.

Most of those affected are under the age of four.

Now the city is working on increasing the supply of clean drinking water to affected communities. This includes the deployment of a total of 36 water tankers.

Water and Sanitation Minister, Pemmy Majodina, revealed this at a meeting on Monday.

READ |Over 400 ill after Tshwane failed to chlorinate Bronkhorstspruit's water

She said an investigation found that water from the Bronkhorstspruit Water Treatment Works (BWTW) was unchlorinated from 24 September to 14 October after the city experienced issues with its chlorine supplier.

She said water quality tests found extremely high levels of E. coli and total coliforms in the water emanating from the treatment plant.

“Since 14 October, CoT has been distributing drinking water to residents using water tankers. The water tankers obtain water from the Cullinan WTW, and CoT and the Department of Water and Sanitation have conducted laboratory tests on the water from the Cullinan WTW, which indicate that the water is safe to drink.”

Other measures in place include further tests being conducted to confirm whether any other harmful contaminants are present in the water.

Additionally, more specimens have been collected by the National Institute for Communicable Diseases.

This, according to Majodina, will strengthen the epidemiological evidence and help determine whether a formal outbreak declaration is required.

READ |DA promises R10bn in eThekwini water restoration

She said the city is in the process of appointing Rand Water as an implementing agent to address these issues after an investigation also found that various components of the BWTW were not working, such as pumps, sand filters, and other mechanical equipment.

World.title: Solontsi takes over Bok women captaincy
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Sizophila Solontsi will take over captaincy duties for the Springbok Women.

The former sevens rugby player will lead South Africa in the final two Global Series tests against Ireland in Cape Town later this month.

Solontsi resumes the leadership role after regular skipper Babalwa Latsha was ruled out of the series due to an ankle injury.

READ | Dominant Australia wary of Pacific threat at Rugby League World Cup

The experienced Solontsi has already co-captained the side with Unam Tose against Italy last month.

Meanwhile Nombuyekezo Mdliki also failed to recover from her rib injury sustained against Spain earlier this month.

World.title: Masemola's return puts police leadership in focus
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Independent policing Union of South Africa says all eyes will be on National Police Commissioner Fannie Masemola as he returns back to work.

This comes as questions remain about police leadership and the decisions needed to improve command and control.

The union's general secretary, Mpho Kwinika, said that whether or not Masemola drew lessons from his suspension, it would only be he who would be able to answer that question through his actions.

“He might have learned a lot. We don't know, but we will see him. I think these six months should have taught him a lot: That when a decision is supposed to be made, he need to make it. He does not have to wait for someone to advise. "These were not complex matters. These are command and control decisions which he has to make. And unfortunately, we saw what happened, from January 2025 up until he was suspended…”

After 6 months on the sidelines, charged with violating the PFMA, Masemola is now back at work.

READ | SAPS renewal tops agenda as Masemola returns to office

But he returns to a police service ravaged by allegations of corruption and infiltration by underworld figures and faces a tough task of restoring public confidence in the SAPS.

Masemola says unity is paramount within police

“I return to office determined to unite the organisation, strengthen its institutional integrity and advance our constitutional responsibility to serve and protect the people of South Africa. It's not about an individual; it's about the responsibility entrusted to the office for leadership continuity which the organisation SAPS is central to our democracy in the country."

As he returns to duty, Masemola says his first priority is preparing for the upcoming local government elections

World.title: Expectations of credit rating upgrade grow ahead of Medium-Term Budget
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Investors are hoping that this week's Medium-Term budget will make the case for a credit rating upgrade.

There are growing expectations that South Africa is on track for a credit rating boost.

By 2020, all major agencies had downgraded South Africa to below investment grade or so-called junk status.

But since late last year South Africa has started to crawl its way back up again.

READ | Key takeaways from the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement

S&P lifted its rating late last year, and Fitch followed suit in June.

Moody's said earlier that it could upgrade South Africa's rating if fiscal performance continues to improve.

World.title: Mbeki denies meddling in prosecution of TRC cases
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - After a failed legal bid to have Commission Chairperson Justice Sisi Khampepe recuse herself for allegations of bias.

Former president Thabo Mbeki finally took the stand at the Khampepe Commission of Inquiry in Johannesburg on Monday.

Mbeki claimed that it is a lie that he interfered in the prosecution of some TRC cases.

READ | WATCH | Mbeki testifies before TRC cases inquiry

He also denied that there were secret meetings to discuss an amnesty deal for apartheid generals responsible for atrocities.

Families known as the Calata group, unhappy with the slow pace in prosecuting matters emanating from the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, want answers on allegations of political interference.

World.title: Kenya confirms third Ebola case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenya has confirmed a third case of Ebola involving a 65-year-old woman who is a close relative of the first two patients.

The Ministry of Health, in a statement, said the woman developed a fever, sore throat and malaise while in quarantine, prompting her isolation and testing.

Her samples tested positive for Ebola at both the National Virology Reference Laboratory and the Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI).

According to the Health Director-General Patrick Amoth, the patient has been transferred to an infectious disease unit, where she is receiving supportive care and being monitored.

“Having been in quarantine, she was diagnosed early and is currently receiving supportive care, improving her chances of recovery while limiting the risk of further spread of the disease,” the statement read.

The second patient, on the other hand, is in stable condition and responding well to supportive care.

The latest case brings the number of confirmed Ebola infections in Kenya to three.

According to the Ministry, of the 130 contacts identified so far, 127 had been traced and placed in quarantine, with efforts ongoing to trace the remaining three.

World.title: Motorists, households face fresh fuel price hikes
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

EPRA attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East. [FIle, Standard]

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) has increased fuel prices, raising the cost of super petrol by Sh12.93 per litre, diesel by Sh9.90, and kerosene by Sh28.49.

The new prices, effective from October 15 to November 14, 2026, will see motorists in Nairobi pay up to Sh226.96 per litre for super petrol, Sh227.76 for diesel, and Sh219.85 for kerosene.

EPRA Director-General Edward Mwirigi Kinyua attributed the price increases to the escalating conflict in the Middle East, which has disrupted petroleum supply chains and driven up the cost of importing fuel.

The rise in kerosene prices is likely to hit low-income households that rely on the fuel for cooking and lighting.

Meanwhile, higher diesel prices could raise the cost of transporting goods and operating public service vehicles, potentially driving up fares and commodity prices.

Diesel is a key fuel for the country's freight transport sector and a significant portion of public service vehicle operations, meaning the increase could have a ripple effect across the economy.

The latest review comes after EPRA maintained pump prices during the September 15 to October 14 pricing period, despite a decline in the cost of importing petrol.

World.title: Oburu Oginga to leave hospital soon - ODM
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

ODM SG Catherine Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician.

ODM Secretary General Catherine Omanyo has dismissed social media reports about the health of party leader Oburu Oginga, saying he is recovering well and is expected to be discharged from hospital either today or tomorrow.

Omanyo criticised bloggers spreading unverified information about the veteran politician, accusing them of exploiting his health condition to attract online attention and increase engagement.

“It's unfortunate what I've been reading on social media. Those people who are seeking to have more likes or viewers, they will be disappointed because he's up, he's well, he's fine. In fact, he's headed home either today or tomorrow,” she said.

Omanyo insisted that the reports had exaggerated his situation, dismissing claims of his death and assuring the public that he was doing well.

She noted that health conditions could fluctuate, saying Oburu's position as ODM party leader had made his well-being a subject of heightened public interest.

“Everybody, everybody, including you and me, our health is not static. You can be under the weather any time. It's just that he's a party leader, and it makes breaking news,” Omanyo said.

She urged social media users to exercise restraint when discussing the health of public figures, warning against spreading unverified reports, particularly claims of death, before confirmation from credible sources.

Her remarks come amid growing speculation on social media about Oburu's health, with some users circulating unverified claims about his condition.

World.title: Kenya declares Ebola a formidable epidemic disease, sets new rules
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale, who declared Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus a formidable epidemic disease under the Public Health Act. [File,Standard]

Kenya has declared Ebola virus a formidable epidemic disease, introducing new rules governing screening, isolation, quarantine, contact tracing and the handling of bodies.

Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale issued the declaration through a legal notice published in the Kenya Gazette on Monday, October 12, under Section 35 of the Public Health Act.

The declaration follows Kenya’s confirmation of its first imported case of Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease on October 6, after a Kenyan citizen who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo travelled through Uganda to Nairobi. The patient died despite receiving supportive treatment.

The case prompted health authorities to trace people who may have come into contact with the patient and strengthen screening at points of entry.

In an update on October 12, the World Health Organization (WHO) said Kenya had listed 127 contacts, with 94 in quarantine, and screened more than 665,000 travellers at points of entry.

WHO also supplied protective equipment and testing materials worth about US$70,000 to support the response.

The government published two legal notices on October 12. Legal Notice No. 203 declares the disease a formidable epidemic, while Legal Notice No. 204 establishes the Public Health (Ebola Disease) Rules, 2026.

The regulations provide for screening at points of entry, medical assessment, isolation, referral, quarantine and monitoring.

They also assign responsibilities to transport operators, health facilities, medical practitioners and laboratories.

Health authorities will conduct investigations and contact tracing, while designated health facilities will manage suspected and confirmed cases. The rules also provide for the inspection and decontamination of premises.

The regulations cover the safe and dignified disposal of bodies, burial procedures, record-keeping, transportation and repatriation. They also address public communication, media houses’ responsibilities in public sensitisation and assistance from enforcement agencies.

The rules provide for offences and penalties, although the Gazette extract does not specify the penalties for individual violations.

What the declaration means

Bundibugyo virus disease is a form of Ebola that spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person or contaminated materials.

Contact with the body of someone who has died from the disease can also expose people to infection during unsafe burial practices.

Symptoms can include fever, fatigue, muscle pain, headache and sore throat, followed by vomiting and diarrhoea. The incubation period ranges from two to 21 days.

WHO says no approved vaccine or specific treatment currently exists for the Bundibugyo strain, making early detection, isolation, supportive care and contact tracing central to controlling its spread.

The health agency has advised against travel or trade restrictions on Kenya, Uganda and the Democratic Republic of Congo based on the information available.

The new rules establish a legal framework for managing the disease, from identifying suspected infections and monitoring contacts to caring for patients and preventing exposure during burials.
