SUDAN · WAR

Key Facts — The country Sudan is a north-east African country at war since April 2023, with its army fighting the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces.

— What happened On Sunday 18 October 2026, a drone strike hit Al-Dabab in West Kordofan, and local groups say more than 100 people died.

— The numbers Relatives gave preliminary figures of over 100 dead and 120 injured, while three local bodies counted about 150 civilians killed.

— Who is blamed The Tasis alliance, which backs the Rapid Support Forces, blames the army; Radio Dabanga’s headline also names the armed forces.

— Monday in Khartoum On Monday 19 October, drones launched by the Rapid Support Forces killed four people in Khartoum, three of them children, Radio Dabanga reported.

— Prediction markets Polymarket bets give a Sudan ceasefire by 31 December 2026 an 8.5% chance, with about US$120,000 traded on the event (19 October, 3:05 p.m. ET).

— Still open The exact death toll, who flew the aircraft, and whether either side will accept an independent inquiry.

A Sudan drone strike on Al-Dabab, a town in West Kordofan, killed more than 100 people on Sunday 18 October, local groups told Radio Dabanga. Radio Dabanga is a Sudanese news service that reports on the war in Arabic and English.

For US readers, the Sudan drone strike lands as Congress weighs a bill that ties a minerals and trade partnership to civilian protection. It also adds to calls to widen the UN arms embargo, which covers only Darfur.

What Happened in Al-Dabab

Radio Dabanga reported on Monday 19 October that an air strike hit Al-Dabab, in West Kordofan state, on Sunday 18 October. Relatives told the outlet that the Sudan drone strike hit a crowded market, with preliminary figures above 100 dead and 120 injured.

The Tasis alliance gave a different account of the first blow, saying it hit a truck carrying people home from a condolence gathering. It added that a drone struck again when people gathered to help the wounded, and it counts 80 dead.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How Many People Died

Three local bodies put the toll at about 150 civilians killed and more than 120 injured. They are the Supreme Council for Dar Hamar Affairs, the civil group Qimam and the Al-Dabab emergency room.

Radio Dabanga’s own summary spoke of more than 200 people killed and injured, and its headline said dozens. All of these counts come from relatives and local groups, so the Sudan drone strike toll may change.

Who Is Blamed

Radio Dabanga’s headline attributes the strikes on Al-Dabab and nearby Al-Majlad to the armed forces, the Sudanese army led by General Abdel Fattah al-Burhan. The Tasis alliance, a political bloc that backs the Rapid Support Forces, said it suspected a Turkish-made Bayraktar Akinci drone belonging to the army.

The Rapid Support Forces, a paramilitary force led by Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, fight the army for control of Darfur and Kordofan. A Tasis spokesperson called the attack a war crime and a crime against humanity.

Drones Over Khartoum on Monday

On Monday morning 19 October, drones attacked Khartoum, the capital, and tried to hit its airport, Radio Dabanga reported. Military sources told the outlet that the army shot down two drones, which it attributed to the Rapid Support Forces.

Falling drones killed three children, including two brothers, and a man at two sites east of the airport and in the Nasser extension district. Sudan Tribune, an independent news site, had earlier reported air defences downing two drones over the Burri and Nasir districts.

A Pattern of Strikes on Markets

On Friday 16 October, a strike hit a livestock market in Nyala, capital of South Darfur, and Tasis said 30 civilians died, Sudan Tribune reported. On Saturday 17 October, a drone hit a lorry near Ankush in West Kordofan, killing four, the Kordofan Observatory said.

On Sunday 18 October, drones also targeted the Atbara and Setit dam complex and the town of Gedaref in eastern Sudan, Radio Dabanga reported. Air defences reportedly intercepted them, and no casualties were reported.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket, a crypto-based betting platform, priced a Sudan ceasefire by 31 December 2026 at 8.5% on Monday 19 October at 3:05 p.m. ET. The price fell 2.5 points in 24 hours, and about US$120,000 has been traded on the event.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for US Readers

The Sudan IMPACT Act, introduced in the US House on Wednesday 14 October, would open a minerals and trade partnership only under a civilian-led authority. The bill by Congressman Jim Baird also requires the Secretary of State to confirm a clear fall in violence against civilians first, Sudan Tribune reported.

Radio Dabanga reports growing international calls to extend the arms embargo from Darfur to all of Sudan. Background is in Sudan’s war and its backers and the Sudan minerals bill.

What Is Not Known

The final Sudan drone strike toll is open, and the counts of 100, 150 and over 200 killed and injured come from local groups. Neither the army nor the Rapid Support Forces has published its own account of the Al-Dabab strike.

It is also unclear whether the target was a market, a truck or both, and who was flying the aircraft. No independent body has yet announced an investigation.

More: Sudan news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Where did the Sudan drone strike happen?

The Sudan drone strike hit Al-Dabab, a town in West Kordofan state, on Sunday 18 October 2026. A second, smaller drone strike hit nearby Al-Majlad and injured at least two people.

How many people died in the Al-Dabab strike?

Relatives put the toll at more than 100 dead, and three local bodies counted about 150 civilians killed and over 120 injured. These counts come from relatives and local groups, and the toll may change.

Who carried out the Sudan drone strike?

Radio Dabanga’s headline attributes it to the Sudanese army, and the Tasis alliance, which backs the Rapid Support Forces, blames the army. The army has not published a statement.

What happened in Khartoum on Monday?

Drones launched by the Rapid Support Forces targeted Khartoum airport and other sites on Monday 19 October, Radio Dabanga reported. Falling drones killed three children and a man, and the army says it shot down two.

Why does the Sudan drone strike matter to the United States?

Congress is weighing a bill that ties a partnership on Sudan’s minerals and trade to protecting civilians. Calls are also growing to widen the UN arms embargo, which covers only Darfur.

MALI · SECURITY

Key Facts — The country Mali is a landlocked West African nation run since coups in 2020 and 2021 by a military junta led by General Assimi Goïta.

— What happened On Monday 19 October, Human Rights Watch said Mali’s army and Russian-controlled Africa Corps killed and wounded dozens of civilians since July.

— The numbers From April to August, Malian forces and Africa Corps flew 49 air strikes that killed 89 civilians, against 22 strikes and 44 deaths a year earlier.

— Two strikes A drone bomb killed six men at the Tombonkore cattle market on 19 August, and a drone hit the Talhandak health centre on 29 July.

— The other side Al-Qaeda-linked fighters and separatists tortured and executed at least 19 captured soldiers at Tabrichat on 18 July.

— For US readers The State Department tells Americans not to travel to Mali for any reason, and Russia’s Africa Corps and Turkish drones shape the war.

— Still open Mali’s defence ministry did not answer the rights group’s letter of 5 August, and the full civilian toll is unknown.

Mali air strikes by the army and its Russian-controlled partner force, Africa Corps, have killed civilians, Human Rights Watch said on Monday 19 October. The rights group, which investigates abuses worldwide, says the two forces have killed and wounded dozens of civilians since July.

For US readers, the report shows how Russia and cheap armed drones shape a war in a country where Americans are told not to travel. It also accuses jihadist and separatist fighters of executing captured soldiers, so the findings cut against every side.

What Human Rights Watch Found

The group interviewed 30 people between 30 July and 20 September, including 16 witnesses, community leaders, journalists and a Malian soldier. It also verified two videos of a drone strike and studied 12 photographs of drone debris.

Human Rights Watch wrote to Mali’s defence minister on 5 August and received no reply. It asks the African Union Peace and Security Council, the bloc’s security body, to hold a special session on civilian protection.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Cattle Market Strike at Tombonkore

A drone dropped a munition on the cattle market in Tombonkore, in the central Bandiagara region, on the morning of 19 August. It killed six men and wounded at least 20 people in one of the Mali air strikes the group documented.

Five witnesses said fighters of the jihadist group JNIM controlled the surroundings, but none were at the market that morning. The army chief of staff said on 20 August that forces hit a “terrorist refuge” in the Kilimpo area and “neutralised” about 20 “terrorists”.

A Health Centre Hit at Talhandak

At 4 a.m. on 29 July, a one-way attack drone struck a health centre in Talhandak, in the northern Kidal region near Algeria. A 45-year-old health worker said no fighters were nearby and the clinic held only medicine and equipment.

Photographs of the wreckage showed parts matching a Shahed-type drone, according to the rights group. Bellingcat and Jeune Afrique, two investigative outlets, reported on 24 July that Shahed-136 drones had been deployed in Mali.

The Numbers Behind Mali Air Strikes

ACLED, a monitor of political violence worldwide, counted 49 Mali air strikes from April to August, the rights group says. The strikes by Malian forces and Africa Corps killed 89 civilians, against 22 strikes and 44 deaths a year earlier.

ACLED also counts 268 civilians killed by Malian armed forces in those five months, and 134 killed by JNIM. Mali has flown Turkish Bayraktar TB2 drones since 2022 and Akinci drones since 2024, while Russia has supplied drones and combat aircraft since 2022.

Insurgents Also Broke the Laws of War

On 18 July, fighters of JNIM, an al-Qaeda-linked group, and of the Azawad Liberation Front, a northern separatist movement, attacked an army convoy at Tabrichat. Videos studied by the rights group and Amnesty International show at least 19 captured soldiers tortured and executed.

JNIM’s religious committee told the rights group the killings happened but were not ordered, and that they did not breach its reading of Islamic law. The separatist front denied executing soldiers, and a Malian prosecutor opened an inquiry on 1 August.

What It Means for US Readers

Mali air strikes are happening in a country the State Department rates Level 4, “Do not travel,” warning that armed groups kidnap foreigners for ransom. Insecurity has also grown inside Bamako, the capital.

Africa Corps is the Russian-controlled successor to the Wagner mercenary group, which Amnesty International accused of killing and torturing civilians in Mali. The drones in the report come from Turkey, a NATO ally of the United States, and from Russia.

What Is Not Known

The rights group could not identify the drone used at Tombonkore, though only the army and Africa Corps are known to own such large drones. The full civilian toll of Mali air strikes since April is unknown.

More than 50 soldiers were missing after Tabrichat, and the army had not contacted their families by mid-September. The report covers only incidents the group could document by remote interviews.

More: Mali news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Human Rights Watch say about Mali on 19 October?

It said Mali air strikes and other attacks by the army and Africa Corps killed and wounded dozens of civilians since July. It also said Islamist and separatist fighters executed captured soldiers.

What is Africa Corps in Mali?

Africa Corps is a Russian-controlled force that replaced the Wagner group. It backs the junta led by General Assimi Goïta.

How many civilians did Mali air strikes kill?

ACLED counted 49 strikes by Malian forces and Africa Corps from April to August, killing 89 civilians. That is more than double the 44 deaths in the same months of 2025.

Is it safe for Americans to travel to Mali?

No. The State Department has a Level 4 advisory telling Americans not to travel to Mali for any reason.

What has Mali’s army said about the strikes?

The army chief of staff said the 19 August strike in Kilimpo hit a terrorist refuge and killed about 20 terrorists. The defence ministry did not answer the rights group’s letter.

Sources: Human Rights Watch (French), 19 October 2026; AllAfrica (French), 19 October 2026; US State Department, 2026.

BOTSWANA · GREAT POWERS

Key Facts — The country Botswana is a landlocked southern African democracy and a leading diamond producer. It has recognised Beijing, not Taipei, since 1975.

— What happened On Tuesday 13 October, Botswana backs China on Taiwan: President Duma Boko told Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Beijing that Botswana opposes Taiwan independence.

— The upgrade The two leaders raised ties to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership and signed a joint statement plus papers on security, mining, health and training.

— The visit The presidency said the state visit to China began on Monday 12 October.

— Mining Xi offered four principles for mining cooperation, led by the line that African resources belong to Africa, and pointed to zero-tariff access.

— US angle Washington has long courted Botswana as a partner, and Chinese camera makers banned in the US run parts of its police and bank networks.

— Still open Whether the security paper involves military work, and how Washington answers, is not public.

Botswana backs China on Taiwan, after President Duma Boko told Chinese leader Xi Jinping on Tuesday 13 October that his country opposes Taiwan independence. The pledge came in Beijing, on the day the two countries lifted relations to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership.

For US readers, the visit shows a diamond-producing democracy and long-time Western partner moving closer to Beijing on security, mining and politics at once. The signed texts touch ground where American influence has been strong.

What Boko Told Xi in Beijing

China’s foreign ministry said the talks took place on the afternoon of Tuesday 13 October at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. A welcome banquet for Boko followed that evening.

Boko said Botswana will stay committed to the one-China principle, Beijing’s position that Taiwan is part of China. He added that Botswana opposes separatist attempts to seek Taiwan independence and any interference in China’s internal affairs.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Botswana Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

A Strategic Partnership With Papers Attached

The two presidents announced the upgrade to a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership, a label China gives to its closest partners. They also signed a joint statement on the new partnership.

China’s foreign ministry said further papers cover the Global Security Initiative, Belt and Road cooperation, green mining, health and human resources. The Global Security Initiative is Xi’s 2022 proposal for a security order that Beijing presents as an alternative to US-led alliances.

Mining Principles and Zero Tariffs

Xi proposed four principles for mining cooperation with Botswana and with Africa, starting with the idea that African resources belong to Africa. He also said African resources should not be used for geopolitical rivalry.

Xi offered cooperation on the digital economy, farming, livestock and a smart education project. He also pointed to China’s zero-tariff treatment for African countries that have diplomatic relations with China.

Health, Schools and Parliament

Mmegi, Botswana’s independent daily, reported that the joint statement commits China to send medical teams and supplies to Botswana. It also promises hospital partnerships, government scholarships for Batswana students and links between universities.

On Wednesday 14 October, Boko met Zhao Leji, who chairs the Standing Committee of China’s National People’s Congress, the country’s legislature. The state Botswana Press Agency reported that both sides want closer ties between their parliaments.

Gaborone Defends the Trip

Lucas Modimana, director of governance in the Office of the President, defended the size of Boko’s delegation, Mmegi reported on Friday 16 October. He called the visit a coordinated mission to attract investment, create jobs and speed up Botswana’s economic recovery.

Modimana tied the trip to efforts to reduce Botswana’s dependence on diamonds. Botswana’s foreign reserves stood at about US$4.4 billion in mid-October, a cushion that makes new investment more urgent.

What It Means for US Readers

Botswana has long been a steady US partner in southern Africa, and a one-China pledge alone is no break with Washington. Yet Botswana backs China on a security paper at the heart of Beijing’s rival vision of global security.

The Sunday Standard, a Gaborone weekly, reported on 12 October that US-banned camera makers Hikvision and Dahua are in police and bank networks. Investors in Botswana’s diamond and mining sector should watch how the new mining principles shape licences and Chinese financing.

What Is Not Known

The texts of the security, Belt and Road and green mining papers have not been published in full. Whether they involve training, equipment or military work is open.

No US government reaction to the visit has been made public. Botswana has also not said how the pledge fits its ties with Taiwan’s remaining African partner, Eswatini, or its other Western partners.

More: Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Botswana agree with China on Taiwan?

Botswana backs China on the one-China principle, President Duma Boko told Xi Jinping on 13 October. He said Botswana opposes any attempt to seek Taiwan independence.

What is a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership?

It is the label Beijing uses for its closest diplomatic relationships. For Botswana and China it came with a joint statement and papers on security, mining, health and training.

Does Botswana recognise Taiwan after the visit?

No, Botswana has recognised the government in Beijing since 1975. In Africa, only Eswatini keeps full diplomatic ties with Taiwan.

When did Boko’s state visit to China begin?

The Office of the President said the state visit began on Monday 12 October. The talks with Xi Jinping took place the next day, Tuesday 13 October.

Why does it matter that Botswana backs China?

Botswana depends on diamonds, and new mining principles agreed with Beijing could shape licences and financing. It also adds Chinese security cooperation in a country that already works with the United States. Botswana backs China, yet keeps open its Western ties.

World.title: Senate Delays Security Bill Past Runoff
World.content:
The Senate chamber during a plenary session. File photo, 2019. (Photo: Senado Federal, CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Monday, 19 October, 3:06 p.m. ET · Source: Estadão, Broadcast Político

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What happened On Monday 19 October, Senate President Davi Alcolumbre signalled that he tends not to put the public security amendment to a vote before the runoff.

Why Lula’s Workers’ Party (PT) is split over amendments that would lower the age of criminal responsibility.

What is at stake The amendment, PEC 18/2025, would widen federal powers over public security, a top campaign theme.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.8% chance of winning the runoff and Lula 23.5% (19 October, 3:04 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 77% and Kalshi at 78% (Lula: 24% and 21% ), as of 19 October, 3:20 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open Alcolumbre was still discussing the decision with senators on Monday, so no formal announcement had been made.

Brazil’s Senate is likely to push its vote on a flagship public security bill until after the Brazil election 2026, Senate President Davi Alcolumbre signalled on Monday 19 October. Sources told Estadão’s Broadcast Político that he met senators and tends not to schedule the proposal before the 25 October runoff.

The delay matters because public security is one of the sharpest themes of the campaign between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, and Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro. For readers in the United States, it shows how a fight over crime policy is shaping Brazil’s political calendar a week before the vote.

What Alcolumbre Signalled on Monday

The government’s allies in the Senate were told there would be no voting session on the amendment this week, because Alcolumbre prefers to take it up after the election period, Estadão reported. He was still debating with senators from the morning whether any session would be held at all.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The decision therefore remains open until the Senate announces its agenda. Estadão said Alcolumbre had not yet made a final call.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Criminal Age Split the Government

The amendment, known as PEC 18/2025, was drafted by Lula’s government to widen federal powers over public security, which now sits mainly with state governors, Estadão reported. The Chamber of Deputies approved it in March 2026, and the Senate’s constitutional committee finished its vote on Wednesday 14 October, Congresso em Foco reported.

Senator Rogério Marinho of Flávio Bolsonaro’s Liberal Party (PL) filed an amendment to lower the age of criminal responsibility, now 18, to 16, with 14 for some grave crimes. PT Senate leader Camilo Santana countered with a narrower version for heinous crimes only, while Teresa Leítão, the government’s leader in the Senate, is against lowering the age, Estadão said.

Lula said in a TV Globo interview on Thursday 15 October that he favours 16 for heinous crimes, but not inside this amendment, Correio da Manhã reported. Camilo’s wing argues that rejecting a cut now could cost Lula votes, Estadão said.

The Earlier Withdrawal on 15 October

Alcolumbre had already pulled the proposal from the Senate agenda on Thursday 15 October, after the government base failed to agree on the amendments, Correio da Manhã reported. He said he would await an understanding among senators.

Any change to the text approved by the Chamber must go back to the Chamber of Deputies for a new vote, according to Congresso em Foco.

What It Means for US Readers

A stalled security bill keeps crime policy at the centre of a campaign that investors and Washington follow closely. Our Brazil election polls tracker shows how tight the race is.

Markets price a Flávio Bolsonaro win more likely than not, per the Brazil election odds page. Prediction markets are bets, not polls, and they can move fast on new surveys.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, traders give Flávio Bolsonaro a 76.8% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 23.5% (19 October, 3:04 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has about US$188.2 million in total trading volume.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What Is Not Known

It is not confirmed whether Alcolumbre will formally announce a postponement or call a session before 25 October. The outcome of the amendments on criminal age is also open.

No poll or source we reviewed shows whether the delay will move any voters. The dispute may change after the runoff, whoever wins.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did the Brazilian Senate delay the security amendment?

Senate President Davi Alcolumbre signalled on Monday 19 October that he tends not to schedule it before the 25 October runoff. Lula’s allies are split over amendments that would lower the age of criminal responsibility.

What is the PEC da Segurança Pública?

It is a proposed constitutional amendment, known as PEC 18/2025, drafted by President Lula’s government to widen federal powers over public security. The Chamber of Deputies approved it in March 2026.

What happens if the Senate changes the text?

Any changed passages must go back to the Chamber of Deputies for another vote. That extra step is why amendments on criminal age threaten the schedule.

When is Brazil’s runoff?

Brazilians vote on Sunday 25 October. The two candidates are President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

Is the delay final?

No. Estadão reported that Alcolumbre was still discussing the decision with senators on Monday, and Senate leaders could still call a session.

EGYPT · GREAT POWERS

Key Facts — The country Egypt is the Arab world’s most populous country and runs the Suez Canal, the shortcut for ships between Europe and Asia.

— What happened On Monday 19 October, President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi received Maxim Oreshkin, Russia’s special envoy for BRICS financial and economic cooperation, in Cairo.

— The zone The Russian Suez zone is a planned park for Russian factories in Egypt’s Suez Canal Economic Zone; a developer was chosen on 15 July.

— The talks Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and Oreshkin discussed speeding up the project, heavy industry, car manufacturing, digital services and artificial intelligence.

— The group BRICS is a bloc of large emerging economies that began with Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, and Egypt joined in January 2024.

— For US readers Russian factories on a key shipping route and a Russian-built nuclear plant show Moscow gaining ground in a long-time US partner.

— Still open The developer has not been named, and no investment figure, opening date or first factory has been announced.

Egypt pushed ahead with the Russian Suez zone on Monday 19 October, when President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi received Russia’s BRICS envoy in Cairo. The envoy, Maxim Oreshkin, also met Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty to speed up a planned park for Russian factories beside the Suez Canal.

For US readers, the visit shows Russia building an industrial base in a country that Washington has long counted as a security partner. It also puts a Russian project next to the canal, one of the busiest trade routes in the world.

What Happened in Cairo on Monday

President El-Sisi received Maxim Oreshkin, deputy head of the Russian presidential administration and President Vladimir Putin’s BRICS envoy, the presidency said. Its spokesman, Ambassador Mohamed El-Shennawy, said El-Sisi asked him to pass his greetings to Putin and stressed Egypt’s commitment to coordinating on joint projects.

Oreshkin passed on Putin’s greetings and said Russia wants to deepen cooperation and advance strategic projects, according to the presidency. The two sides also discussed recent BRICS developments and regional issues, with Egypt’s intelligence chief Hassan Rashad present.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What the Russian Suez Zone Is

The Russian Suez zone is a planned park for Russian factories inside the Suez Canal Economic Zone, Egypt’s state-run area of ports and factory sites. It was first agreed in 2018 under a 50-year framework, with an early plan of US$7 billion and about 35,000 jobs, Ahram Online reported.

In September 2025, Egypt and Russia signed a long-term usufruct agreement, which gives Russia the right to operate the site. On 15 July 2026, Egypt’s foreign ministry said a Russian developer had been selected, after a call between Abdelatty and Russian industry minister Anton Alikhanov.

What Abdelatty and Oreshkin Discussed

Abdelatty welcomed Oreshkin on his first visit to Egypt and said Egypt is proud of its comprehensive strategic partnership with Russia, the foreign ministry reported. They reviewed how to speed up the Russian Suez zone after the developer announcement and raise industrial and commercial investment.

They also looked at cooperation in heavy industry, car manufacturing, digital transformation and artificial intelligence, including the transfer and local production of technology. Al Bayan reported in July that Egypt had set aside 300,000 square metres for the first phase.

Why Russia Targets the Suez Canal Economic Zone

The Suez Canal Economic Zone offers tax and customs incentives, port access and a base for selling to Europe, the Gulf and Africa. Its authority reported US$7.26 billion of contracted investment across 117 projects in the year to 30 June, as the Rio Times reported on 1 September.

Russia’s other big project in Egypt is the El-Dabaa nuclear plant, which the Rio Times covered on 29 August. It is planned with four reactors and 4,800 megawatts of capacity in total.

Who Is Maxim Oreshkin and What Is BRICS

Oreshkin is deputy head of the Russian presidential administration, and this was his first trip to Egypt. His special title covers financial and economic cooperation with BRICS countries.

BRICS is a bloc of large emerging economies that began with Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Egypt joined in January 2024, and Russia chaired the bloc in 2024.

What It Means for US Readers

Egypt has long been a close US security partner and a major recipient of US military aid. A Russian industrial park on its canal therefore draws attention in Washington.

US shipping lines, manufacturers and lenders that use the Suez route or the economic zone will watch which companies the Russian side brings. Western sanctions on Russia since 2022 limit what Russian firms can buy, and the financing of the Russian Suez zone has not been set out.

What Is Not Known

Neither government has named the Russian developer or given an investment figure, an opening date or the first factories. The 2018 estimate of US$7 billion and 35,000 jobs has not been updated in the official statements.

It is also unclear whether the talks produced any signed agreement, since the presidency and the foreign ministry reported discussions only. The statements do not say when the Russian Suez zone will receive its first factory.

More: Egypt news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Russian Industrial Zone in Egypt?

It is a planned industrial park for Russian companies inside Egypt’s Suez Canal Economic Zone. Egypt and Russia agreed the idea in 2018, and a Russian developer was selected on 15 July 2026.

Who met President El-Sisi on 19 October?

President El-Sisi received Maxim Oreshkin, Russia’s special representative for BRICS financial and economic cooperation. Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and intelligence chief Hassan Rashad attended for Egypt.

What is BRICS and is Egypt a member?

BRICS is a bloc of large emerging economies that began with Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. Egypt joined in January 2024.

Has the Russian Suez zone started operating?

No factory has been announced yet. Egypt’s foreign ministry only said that talks on speeding up the project continue after the developer was selected.

Why does the Russian Suez zone matter to Americans?

The Russian Suez zone sits beside one of the world’s busiest shipping routes in a long-time US security partner. It shows Russia deepening economic ties there despite Western sanctions.

World.content:

DR CONGO · EBOLA

Key Facts — The country DR Congo is Africa’s second-largest country, with more than 100 million people, and North Kivu is its eastern border province.

— What happened On Monday 19 October, North Kivu banned mass events, capped taxi loads and burials, and held a Stop Ebola day.

— The new rules No concerts, parades or political rallies; two people per motorbike; burials limited to 20 relatives; one month of minimum service in public offices.

— The toll The governor said North Kivu had 1,252 Ebola deaths by Saturday 17 October, a death rate of about 60% among cases.

— The wider outbreak The DR Congo Ebola outbreak stood at 9,455 confirmed cases and 4,561 deaths on Sunday 18 October, the CDC said.

— What it means for you The US bars flights for anyone in DR Congo in the past 21 days and rates North Kivu Level 4, avoid all travel.

— Still open How long the rules last, and whether a Stop Ebola day can win over communities that still resist the response.

New DR Congo Ebola restrictions were announced on Monday 19 October in North Kivu, an eastern province. Authorities banned mass gatherings, limited taxi passengers and capped burials at 20 relatives.

The province’s governor says Ebola has killed 1,252 people there, and Washington already bars flights to the United States for anyone recently in the country. Actualite.cd and Radio Okapi, two Congolese outlets, reported the DR Congo Ebola measures.

What the Provincial Government Ordered

The provincial government, based in Beni, suspended mass sports events, concerts, karaoke, parades, political demonstrations and nightclub entertainment, Actualite.cd reported. Offices of the public administration must run a minimum service for one month.

Checkpoints must offer handwashing, disinfection and temperature checks. People held in police cells and prisons must be screened for Ebola before they are moved between facilities.

The provincial sports and leisure division, the national police and the provincial security committee must enforce the rules. No end date was given for the bans, only the one-month limit for public offices.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on DR Congo Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Taxi Loads and Burials Capped

Motorbikes may carry no more than two people, including the rider, and cars no more than four passengers plus the driver. Jeeps are limited to six passengers plus the driver.

Burials are limited to 20 members of the family. Ebola spreads through the blood and fluids of the sick and the dead, so crowded funerals are a known danger.

Motorbikes are a cheap way to get around towns such as Beni and Butembo, so the two-person cap changes daily life for many commuters. The DR Congo Ebola rules also reach prisons, where inmates must be screened before transfers.

A Stop Ebola Day Shuts the Towns

Governor Evariste Somo Kakule, an army general, declared Monday a Stop Ebola day to raise awareness as cases climb, Radio Okapi reported. Economic and school activity stopped in Beni, Butembo, Oicha, Lubero-centre and Kasindi-Lubiriha.

Schools, markets, small shops and petrol stations stayed closed, few motorbike taxis ran, and police set up checkpoints, Radio Okapi said. In Beni, police turned back some vehicles in the Mulekera area and on Nyamwesi Boulevard.

Actualite.cd noted that a motorised caravan drove along Beni’s main boulevard as part of the anti-Ebola campaign, which cut against the call to stay home. Radio Okapi said the day was agreed with civil society groups and that community resistance persists in some health zones.

Why North Kivu Is Acting Now

The governor said North Kivu counted 1,252 deaths as of Saturday 17 October and put the death rate among cases at about 60%. The World Health Organization (WHO), the United Nations health agency, counted 1,755 confirmed cases and 1,013 deaths there by 6 October.

That report, issued on Thursday 8 October, gave North Kivu the highest death rate of any province at 57.7%. It named Beni and Katwa among the worst-hit of the 17 affected health zones.

Nationwide, the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) counted 9,455 confirmed cases and 4,561 deaths by 18 October. The outbreak began in May and involves the Bundibugyo strain, which has no approved vaccine or treatment, as the Rio Times explained in August.

Vaccination Starts With Front-Line Workers

A vaccination campaign began in Beni on Friday 16 October under Dr Steven Ahuka, the national Ebola response coordinator, the Congolese Press Agency (ACP) reported. It uses a vaccine called Ervebo and starts with health workers, burial teams, laboratory staff and body carriers.

Ahuka called vaccination an extra tool that does not replace prevention measures. The WHO has said Ervebo, licensed against a different Ebola species, should be used against this strain only within trials that test it.

What It Means for US Readers

The CDC bars anyone who was in DR Congo in the past 21 days from boarding a flight to the United States, including US citizens. It lists Ituri and North Kivu at Level 4, avoid all travel.

Aid groups and donors face a harder DR Congo Ebola operating environment where shut towns slow supply runs. The Rio Times reported that more than US$700 million of response money is unreported to national authorities, which raises pressure for tighter accounts.

What Is Not Known

The provincial government has not said how long the bans on events and taxi loads will last. It is also unclear whether one Stop Ebola day will change behaviour in this DR Congo Ebola zone, where some communities resist the response.

The WHO has not yet published a North Kivu toll for 17 October. Nor is it known whether the vaccination campaign will widen beyond front-line workers, or how fast new cases are rising in the province.

More: DR Congo news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the new Ebola rules in North Kivu?

North Kivu’s provincial government suspended mass sports events, concerts, parades and political demonstrations on Monday 19 October. It also capped burials at 20 relatives and limited taxis, cars and jeeps to set passenger numbers.

Where is North Kivu?

North Kivu is a province in eastern DR Congo that borders Uganda and Rwanda. Its main towns include Goma, Beni and Butembo.

How many people have died of Ebola in North Kivu?

Governor Evariste Somo Kakule said North Kivu had 1,252 Ebola deaths as of Saturday 17 October. The WHO counted 1,013 deaths there by 6 October.

Can Americans travel to DR Congo?

Because of the DR Congo Ebola outbreak, the CDC bars anyone who was in the country within 21 days from US-bound flights. It rates North Kivu and Ituri at Level 4, avoid all travel.

Is there a vaccine for the DR Congo Ebola outbreak?

No vaccine or treatment is approved for the Bundibugyo strain behind this outbreak, according to the WHO. A campaign with Ervebo, a vaccine licensed for a different species, began in Beni on 16 October for front-line workers.

World.title: Kenya Convicts 29 in Shakahola Cult Murders
World.content:
RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. Ask Answers are generated from Rio Times reporting only — every claim links to its source article. Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesCost of living, safety, visas across Latin America › RT Ask Rio Times 17 years of Latin America reporting, on demand. × Best for expats Cost of living Safest places Easy visas Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. KENYA · COURTS

Key Facts — The country Kenya is a major East African economy, a mostly Christian country and a popular safari and beach destination for Americans.

— What happened On Monday 19 October 2026, the High Court in Mombasa convicted preacher Paul Mackenzie and 28 others in the Shakahola cult murders.

— The victims 190 of the 191 victims were children, all under 16. Kenyan outlets put the bodies recovered from Shakahola forest at 429.

— The Bible The judge ruled that verses used to ban school and hospitals were misread, and that scripture gives no basis for fasting to death.

— The warning signs Mackenzie was charged in 2017 and a court forum raised alarm in 2019, yet followers kept moving into the forest.

— What comes next Probation reports are due on Friday 30 October, and sentencing is set for Friday 6 November.

— Still open The sentences, any appeal, and whether Kenya will tighten rules for religious groups.

A Kenyan court on Monday 19 October convicted preacher Paul Mackenzie and 28 followers of the Shakahola cult murders. Justice Diana Kavedza found all 29 guilty on 191 counts of murder, and 190 of the victims were children who starved in a coastal forest.

For US readers the case tests where religious freedom ends and criminal liability begins, in a country that welcomes American tourists and investors. The judge read the ruling for more than nine hours in Mombasa, and sentencing is set for Friday 6 November.

What the Court Decided

Justice Kavedza of the High Court, which hears murder trials in Kenya, ruled that the accused acted together to run a fasting regime. She rejected the defence that the victims of the Shakahola cult murders, all under 16, had fasted to death by choice.

Religious explanations for the fast were “legally immaterial to the determination of mens rea”, the legal term for a guilty mind, the Nation reported. The court looked at what the accused intended, not at what they believed.

The judge found that children aged six to 10 could not grasp that death is permanent, so they could not consent to starving themselves. She said some may have believed that death could be reversed.

Witnesses testified that followers who resisted the fast were beaten, and that branches and thorns blocked access to homesteads. The judge also noted an attack on a witness who entered the forest with journalists on 23 March 2023.

Justice Kavedza stressed that church membership alone does not prove murder, and that each accused must have shared the intent. She found that the 29 now convicted met that test, while two of the 31 first charged died during the trial.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Kenya Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Bible Verses the Judge Took Apart

The Nation reported that the judge gave an in-depth analysis of the Bible chapters Mackenzie used to win over his followers. She ruled that Ecclesiastes 12 and Timothy 6, which he cited against schooling, do not condemn education.

The court noted that Mackenzie told followers that doctors were witches and that medicine was made by Satan. He cited Jeremiah 17:5 and James 5:14 to say that believers should rely on prayer and anointing, not hospitals.

To justify fasting to death, the group pointed to Romans 12:1, which urges believers to offer their bodies as a living sacrifice. The judge held that Bible fasting is a spiritual discipline and called the practice “inconsistent with the biblical accounts upon which it purports to rely”.

Mackenzie called his followers the Wateule, or chosen ones, and cast everyone else as the Mataifa, outsiders he portrayed as agents of the Antichrist. That split let him cut family ties and move believers into the forest.

Warning Signs Authorities Missed

The Shakahola cult murders had roots in Good News International Ministries, which Mackenzie founded in 2003 and the Registrar of Societies registered in 2010. The church ran a television station, Times TV, in the coastal town of Malindi that spread his end-of-the-world message.

In May 2017, 43 children aged one to 13 were rescued from church premises at Mayungu, and Mackenzie was first charged that October. He was acquitted in the radicalisation case in October 2021.

In November 2019 a court users committee in Kilifi County, a local forum chaired by the presiding judge, discussed complaints about Mackenzie. The Judicial Service Commission, which oversees Kenya’s judges, has said it received no feedback on a proposal to deregister the church.

Followers began moving into Shakahola forest in 2019, and bodies were found in shallow graves from 20 March 2023. Kenyan court reporting puts the bodies recovered at 429, while the national human rights commission counted 448 deaths in a March 2024 report.

What Comes Next in Court

The judge ordered each convict to be assigned a probation officer, with reports due in court on Friday 30 October. The defence will then plead for leniency, and sentencing in the Shakahola cult murders case is set for Friday 6 November.

The state prosecutor, the Director of Public Prosecutions Renson Ingonga, attended the reading in person. Prosecutors argued that the accused acted on a common plan, and the court agreed.

Mackenzie also faces a terrorism trial at the Shanzu Law Courts, which opened on Tuesday 4 August with seven co-accused. That case concerns 52 deaths at a second site, Kwa Binzaro, and prosecutors plan to call about 60 witnesses.

What It Means for US Readers

Shakahola lies in Kilifi County near Malindi on the Indian Ocean coast, a region many Americans visit. The Rio Times guide to safety in Kenya explains which areas carry travel warnings, and its explainer on religion in Kenya sets the context.

The Shakahola cult murders ruling draws a line US courts know: belief is protected, but directing followers to die can bring murder charges. The closest American parallel is the 1978 Jonestown deaths in Guyana, where more than 900 people died.

What Is Not Known

The court has not said what sentence the 29 convicts will receive, which the judge will decide on Friday 6 November. It is also open whether any of them will appeal.

Many victims of the Shakahola cult murders are still unidentified, and counts of the dead range from 429 to 448. Whether Kenya will pass new rules for religious groups, or review the officials who missed the warnings, has not been announced.

More: Kenya news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Paul Mackenzie?

Paul Nthenge Mackenzie is a Kenyan preacher who founded Good News International Ministries in 2003. On 19 October 2026 the High Court convicted him of murder on 191 counts.

What happened at Shakahola?

Hundreds of followers, many of them children, starved in Shakahola forest after being told that fasting would bring them to Jesus. Bodies were found in shallow graves from 20 March 2023.

How many people were convicted of the Shakahola cult murders?

The High Court convicted 29 people, including Mackenzie, of the Shakahola cult murders on all 191 counts. Two of the 31 people first charged died during the trial.

When will the convicts be sentenced?

Sentencing is set for Friday 6 November 2026, after probation reports are presented on Friday 30 October. The court has not said what the sentences will be.

Does the verdict make religious belief a crime in Kenya?

No. The judge ruled that religious explanations are legally immaterial to whether a person intended to cause death.

World.title: BELTRAIDE hosts Entrepreneurship training in Stann Creek and Toledo
World.content:
BELTRAIDE hosts Entrepreneurship training in Stann Creek and Toledo

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Trade and Investment Development Service (BELTRAIDE) is hosting two entrepreneurship training workshops in Hopkins Village, Stann Creek District, and San Pedro Columbia Village, Toledo District, under the PROSPER Project.

The workshops aim to strengthen business skills, encourage entrepreneurship and create economic opportunities for rural and Indigenous communities, particularly women and young people.

In San Pedro Columbia, 20 participants have begun the first day of the five-day Gender and Entrepreneurship Together (GET Ahead) training.

The program is designed to strengthen entrepreneurial skills, build business knowledge and help participants start or expand their enterprises. Through practical activities and guided learning, participants will gain tools to develop their business ideas and improve their prospects for success.

Meanwhile, participants in Hopkins Village are taking part in the “My Green Entrepreneurship: Starting My Green Enterprise” course. The training focuses on helping aspiring entrepreneurs develop environmentally friendly business ideas and turn them into practical, sustainable business plans. Participants are being introduced to opportunities for establishing green enterprises while building the knowledge and confidence needed to pursue their business goals.

BELTRAIDE says the workshops seek to promote entrepreneurship, advance gender equality and support sustainable livelihoods.

By providing practical business skills and guidance, the initiative can help participants turn their ideas into income-generating opportunities, strengthen local economies and contribute to more resilient communities. The training also encourages environmentally responsible business practices that can support long-term development.

The PROSPER Project, which stands for Participation, Ownership, and Sustainable Progress for Economic Resilience, is funded by the European Union and implemented by the International Labour Organization in partnership with the Government of Belize.

World.title: International News: Search continues for 4 Salvadoran soldiers missing after gang ambush in Haiti
World.content:
International News: Search continues for 4 Salvadoran soldiers missing after gang ambush in Haiti

By Zoila Palma: Four Salvadoran soldiers serving with Haiti’s Gang Suppression Force (GSF) remain missing after armed groups ambushed their armored vehicle in the Santo area of Croix-des-Bouquets on Sunday.

The Fuerza Armada de El Salvador said that the soldiers were returning to their camp when attackers used firearms and explosives against their vehicle, causing it to catch fire. The military said the four soldiers managed to escape the burning vehicle, but their whereabouts remain unknown.

El Salvador’s military said its Libertad II Task Force is working with the GSF command and international forces to locate the missing soldiers.

Helicopters were deployed to support the search, forcing armed groups to retreat, although the aircraft also came under gunfire.

Efforts to reach the soldiers by land and air have been hindered by intense clashes and dangerous security conditions.

Following the ambush, the GSF urged residents of Santo to remain indoors until further notice and avoid the affected area while security operations continued.

The incident has prompted concerns and calls for authorities to clarify what happened to the missing personnel. The force said operations were ongoing to disrupt armed groups and maintain security, as residents reported hearing gunfire and helicopters following the attack.

The ambush comes amid continued efforts to combat gang violence in Haiti, where armed groups have expanded their influence and forced large numbers of people from their homes.
