El alcalde de Pego (Alicante), Enrique Moll, ha informado de que en la parte baja del término municipal, en la zona del parque natural del Marjal de Pego-Oliva, había personas en los tejados que aguardan su rescate por medios aéreos. En declaraciones a À Punt Ràdio, Moll ha señalado que los accesos a la localidad estaban cortados y que se ha activado a la UME, bomberos forestales y de la Diputación de Alicante, “pero incluso los vehículos pesados están quedándose estancados porque el acceso a la población es complicado” y están a la espera de que se activen los medios aéreos. El alcalde ha indicado, además, que están recibiendo “infinidad de llamadas” de vecinos con los bajos y garajes inundados y con agua por las escaleras en el interior de las viviendas.

La Generalitat Valenciana ha enviado a primera hora de la mañana de este lunes, sobre las 7.00 horas, un nuevo ES-Alert a los habitantes de las comarcas de La Marina Alta (al norte de Alicante, comprende municipios como Dénia, Pego o Xàbia) y La Safor (al sur de Valencia, integrada por Gandia o Barx) ante “la reactivación de las precipitaciones persistentes e intensas y las inundaciones producidas por desbordamientos y acumulaciones de agua”. El texto pedía “no cruzar zonas inundables, alejarse de ríos, barrancos, cauces, paseos marítimos y zonas de costa”; no subir a zonas elevadas, “no bajar a sótanos ni garajes” ni usar los ascensores.

Además, la Generalitat activó a las seis de la mañana la situación 2 de emergencia en las citadas comarcas. La situación 2 se activa cuando una emergencia no puede ser controlada con los medios locales o autonómicos y requiere la incorporación de recursos extraordinarios y estatales (como la UME). Las lluvias torrenciales entre Pego, Real de Gandia, Villalonga y Barx han superado los 500 litros por metro cuadrado en las últimas 48 horas.

A las siete de la mañana de este lunes, el consejero de Emergencias insistía en que no se podía circular y se debía permanecer en casa. “Está habiendo lluvias intensas y continuadas que están produciendo inundaciones importantes en diversos municipios, como son Pego, Oliva, Piles, Miramar, Els Poblets, L’Atzúbia. Tenemos muchas personas que están atrapadas y tampoco los camiones pueden alcanzar a esas zonas por la cantidad de agua y porque se están desbordando ríos. En concreto, el río Girona se ha desbordado, el Benissa también, y también pueden desbordarse otros barrancos y otros ríos. Por favor, confinamiento, no circulen por las carreteras y no atraviesen el litoral sur y el litoral norte, el litoral sur de la provincia de Valencia y el litoral norte de la provincia de Alicante”, ha detallado Juan Carlos Valderrama.

El río Girona se ha desbordado a su paso por el municipio alicantino de Els Poblets (2.750 habitantes), en la comarca de la Marina Alta, y ha provocado inundaciones en las zonas próximas al cauce, según ha informado el Ayuntamiento de esta localidad a través de redes sociales. La zona se encontraba en alerta roja por fuertes lluvias y tormentas desde el domingo, por lo que desde el Consistorio piden a toda la ciudadanía extremar las precauciones, evitar cualquier desplazamiento innecesario y no acercarse al río ni a las zonas inundadas. “No intentéis cruzar calles ni caminos inundados, ni a pie ni en vehículo”, advierten desde el Ayuntamiento, que insta a quienes se encuentren en una zona afectada a subir a las plantas superiores y seguir las indicaciones de los servicios de emergencia.

La lluvia ha obligado a Emergencias de la Generalitat a solicitar el helicóptero del Consorcio de Bomberos para operaciones de rescate en Oliva. Se han cortado varias carreteras comarcales. A lo largo del día han intervenido en los rescates 15 medios aéreos.

La delegada del Gobierno en la Comunitat Valenciana, Pilar Bernané, alertaba en las primeras horas del día a través de un mensaje en la red social X de que el peligro era “extraordinario” en los ríos y barrancos de la Safor y la Marina. Bernabé ha recordado que efectivos del III batallón de la UME se dirigían a Oliva para actuar junto a los servicios de emergencias en los avisos de inundaciones en este municipio y en el cercano de Pego. “No os desplacéis, subid a las partes altas y seguid todas las recomendaciones de Emergencias”, ha advertido en su mensaje.

World.title: Todos los ojos se vuelven al norte: lo que pasa cuando se empuja a los creadores
World.content:
Faro Santander, el nuevo espacio cultural y museístico del norte de España, lanza la II convocatoria de Ayudas a la Creación para artistas cántabros de cualquier disciplina, un programa que, además de ayuda económica, provee de asesorías especializadas y garantiza una muestra pública en el museo. Los ganadores de la primera convocatoria cuentan su experiencia

Suelen identificarse solo a toro pasado: aquel momento me cambió la vida. Hay oportunidades, sin embargo, cuyo brillo se deja ver desde el principio. Esta es una de esas. Faro Santander lanza su II Convocatoria de Ayudas a la Creación, un programa que ofrece a los proyectos seleccionados una dotación económica de 10.000 euros, seminarios y mentorías con profesionales, la ocasión de compartir proceso creativo con otros artistas y, como remate, una muestra pública en un espacio tan espectacular como el Edificio Pereda, convertido desde su reciente rehabilitación y apertura en Santander en uno de los grandes focos culturales de todo el norte de España.

Hasta el 15 de febrero de 2027 puede disfrutarse gratuitamente, comisariado por Ane Rodríguez, del resultado de los cuatro proyectos becados en la primera edición. Talento cántabro que, a partir de distintas manifestaciones culturales ligadas a esa verde tierra, ha generado un trabajo variado, muy contemporáneo y de vocación universal. En Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas, Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva recuperan materiales de un archivo de educación sexual de hace décadas; una obra, la que proponen, que cultiva la sensibilidad, que induce a la reflexión sobre gestos cotidianos como el abrazo. En Una forma minúscula, de Salón de belleza, nombre del colectivo formado por Manuela Gutiérrez y Cristina Somavilla, el cine de arte y ensayo sirve como pretexto para encontrarse y hablar, para crear comunidad y traer a la conversación la olvidada contracultura santanderina. La pintora Amaia Bregel, por primera vez en su carrera en piezas de gran escala, en Ludarquías muestra instalaciones y dispositivos impregnados de todo su saber pictórico (“Casi todo el arte contemporáneo es hijo de la pintura”, cuenta). El dúo Casapalma —Irene Atienza y Yoel Molina—, cuya música bucea en el folclore cántabro, ha logrado terminar el rodaje de un documental titulado La Suite de los Riconchos que se estrena el próximo 22 de octubre y nos trae ese ancestral conocimiento que se esconde en las danzas tradicionales y la etnografía.

Entre todos los aspirantes, el jurado escogió proyectos en los que, además de formatos convencionales, cupieran investigaciones artísticas y apuestas valientes: se valora documentación, proceso, método y pensamiento tanto como pieza final. Una característica de este programa de ayudas que los cuatro beneficiarios destacan, por inusual en el panorama nacional: “Ojalá mantengan este espíritu”, indica Germán de la Riva. La visibilidad que les ha otorgado este reconocimiento, sobre todo al verse expuestos en Marisma, en la primera planta de Faro, vecinos a una colección permanente que abarca obra desde El Greco a Frida Kahlo, es el otro gran privilegio que los artistas unánimemente señalan: “Para mí supuso un punto de inflexión”, confiesa Amaia Bregel; para ella, esta ha sido la puerta hacia otras becas o ferias de enorme prestigio, como la de Casa Velázquez o Estampa.

“Animaos a participar, sea cual sea vuestra idea”, ese es el mensaje común de los primeros beneficiarios para quienes les sigan.

Segunda convocatoria Ayudas Plazo de admisión 2026 15 octubre -

09 de noviembre Dotación económica 10.000 euros Beneficiarios Cuatro artistas (o colectivos de artistas) de cualquier disciplina, residentes o nacidos en Cantabria Así funciona el programa de acompañamiento: El proyecto debe desarrollarse en Cantabria, entre enero y junio de 2027

Se priorizarán aquellos que fomenten la generación de tejido artístico en el territorio

Se realizará un encuentro inicial entre comisarios, coordinadores y beneficiarios

Los beneficiarios dispondrán de cuatro seminarios y talleres con profesionales invitados, uno a la semana durante el primer mes de trabajo

Estos encuentros colectivos periódicos que estarán abiertos a otros artistas que deseen inscribirse

Los beneficiarios podrán solicitar tutorías personalizadas y seguimiento continuo

Al final del programa, se organizará una muestra pública en Faro Santander, a partir de septiembre de 2027

Amaia Bregel y

Ludarquías

Cuando Amaia Bregel volvió a Santander en marzo de 2020, con la pandemia, no tenía intención de quedarse. Se había graduado en Bellas Artes en Valencia, donde continuó con un máster de Producción de Arte y Pensamiento Contemporáneo y donde, sin aquel terremoto mundial, seguramente se habría imaginado residiendo todavía. Hoy, sin embargo, reivindica las posibilidades halladas en su ciudad: “Mucha gente de mi generación volvió y entre todos hemos creado una red. Soy la que más defiende Santander ahora mismo”, reclama entre risas.

05:15 Amaia Bregel | Fundación Santander

Al borde de la treintena, la ayuda de Faro ha supuesto para ella un cambio de escala, literal y profesional. Su proyecto, Ludarquías, le ha permitido abordar una producción que no habría podido llevar a cabo en las condiciones con las que venía trabajando. La artista lo resume sin rodeos: «Para mí a nivel profesional es un antes y un después». Ha podido tomar por primera vez decisiones plásticas sin ver constreñida su ambición por cuestiones estrictamente económicas y, además, ha contado, cuando la duda más quemaba, con el consejo de la consagrada artista limeña Andrea Canepa. “Fue un regalazo”, cuenta. Fruto de toda esa meticulosa labor es el objeto pictórico titulado Escalera de Jacob. Uno de los imperdibles de la muestra.

Amaia Bregel y

Ludarquías Las ayudas supusieron la oportunidad para Amaia Bregel de llevar sus objetos pictóricos a unas dimensiones nunca antes experimentadas. En la imagen, parte del trabajo de montaje final de la instalación móvil. (Crédito: Jabata Films) Antes de llegar al objeto pictórico grande, Bregel trabaja con maquetas. La propia escala presenta problemas que ha de ir afrontando en el proceso plástico y que necesitan de ingenio. En este proyecto, contó con la asesoría de la artista peruana Andrea Canepa. (Crédito: Jabata Films) Su obra parte de lo pictórico y lo deriva hacia objetos donde el color y sus vibraciones son habitables. Amaia Bregel sigue considerándose, ante todo, pintora, aunque se maneje en muchos lenguajes y métodos. Esta pieza expuesta en Marisma, en Faro Santander, lleva por título ‘Escalera de Jacob’ y puede contemplarse así, como un cubo completo, o abierta. (Crédito: Jabata Films).

Casapalma y

La Suite de los Riconchos

Su álbum debut, Montañesas (2023), mezclaba canción tradicional con sonidos electrónicos; con JOTAS (2025) profundizan en la importancia de la pandereta y de una música que, sobre todo, estaba hecha para bailar. Y ahí, en todo ese universo —de los ritmos de percusión y los pasos de danza a la alfayatería y los trajes tradicionales— encuentran el germen del documental La Suite de los Riconchos que ahora estrenan en la Filmoteca de Cantabria y que esperan que tenga un gran recorrido por festivales y salas. Música y patrimonio, arte y sociología.

08:08 Casapalma | Fundación Santander

Las ayudas, además del crucial aporte económico para completar el rodaje que finalizaron en agosto (“¡Hacer una película es muy caro!”, exclama Atienza), le han procurado otra experiencia de esas difícilmente olvidables. Tocaron en la inauguración de Faro Santander, pudieron, gracias a la celebración de ese concierto, “subir a un escenario enorme el folclore de Cantabria para que lo viera toda la ciudad”.

Casapalma y

La Suite de los Riconchos Fotograma de ‘La Suite de los Riconchos’, con Yoel Molina (izquierda) a la guitarra e Irene Atienza a la pandereta. Molina se formó en Musikene (País Vasco) y en el Conservatorio Superior de Ámsterdam. Atienza, que vivió varios años en Brasil, regresó a su ciudad, Santander, tras la pandemia. Para la grabación del documental han llevado a cabo una importante investigación musicológica y etnográfica. El baile estaba en el centro del propósito de estas músicas, y esa misma relevancia tiene en la película. Los trajes tradicionales de montañesa suelen componerse de camisa de manca ancha, saya larga de colores con detalles de terciopelo y detalles como pañoleta o faltriquera. La película documental musical, que contó con la asesoría de grandes profesionales coreográficos y estudiosos de la etnografía de la región, se estrenó en la Filmoteca de Cantabria el 22 de octubre y está pendiente de su distribución en festivales y salas.

Para una formación que trabaja con el patrimonio inmaterial, con buena reputación ya bien ganada y una trayectoria importante en el campo de la música, compartir el proceso de su película con otros artistas con métodos y objetivos más abstractos, inmersos en proyectos de lenguajes variopintos, ha sido otro de los aprendizajes más enriquecedores. Cuenta Irene que, tras esta experiencia en común, Aurelio Vélez, vinculado al colectivo etnográfico Brañaflor y asesor fundamental del filme, tomó la determinación de presentar una propuesta sobre costura y cuadros de la colección permanente a la convocatoria que ahora se abre. “Él no se imaginaba que pudiera ser candidato a unas ayudas de arte, pero programas como este son una forma de abrir la mente”.

Salón de Belleza y

Una forma minúscula

Una conversación entre dos amigas, Manuela Gutiérrez y Cristina Somavilla, que eclosiona al abrirla al resto: así podría definirse qué es Salón de Belleza, el colectivo artístico que ambas fundaron y para el que ver películas, discutirlas y cuestionar ideas anquilosadas sobre el gusto o la cultura es la razón última de ser. Una forma minúscula parte de un hallazgo accidental: se toparon con el largometraje de Jesús Garay Manderley (1981) sobre la figura del artista y activista LGTBIQ+ José Pérez Ocaña y se obsesionaron con la peli: “Le pregunté por ella a mi padre”, cuenta Somavilla, “y me contó que él había conocido aquí a Ocaña”. Ahí comienza su investigación, ¿qué relatos de aquella Cantabria habían quedado fuera de la historia oficial? “Hemos abierto fisuras en lo que se supone que es Santander: hay mucho más”, explican.

06:42 Salón de Belleza | Fundación Santander

La ayuda les ha permitido poner en marcha un grupo de investigación intergeneracional en el que la memoria oral y el intercambio de pareceres ha ido hilando una conversación inacabada e inacabable (“¡seguiremos con estos encuentros y clubes en el futuro!”), siempre dispuesta a fluir fuera de cauce y al vaivén de las sorpresas, una investigación recogida parcialmente en textos y materiales de archivo disponibles en la muestra. “Nos gustaría ahora que la gente se acercara al espacio museístico, que Faro Santander se convirtiera en ese lugar de participación y encuentro que ha sido para nosotras”.

Salón de Belleza y

Una forma minúscula Sesión de trabajo del proyecto ‘Una forma minúscula’, en la que, a partir del visionado de una película y de ciertos materiales de archivo, se abre una conversación. Fotograma del drama dirigido por Jesús Garay ‘Manderley’, estrenado en 1981. La trama acompaña a tres jóvenes homosexuales que, en un mal momento personal, deciden pasar un verano juntos en Cantabria. Entre los protagonistas, destaca el ‘performer’ José Pérez Ocaña. Además de la película, las sesiones del proyecto utilizan material que reconstruye el contexto cultural en que surgió el filme para indagar más allá del relato oficial. En la imagen, el informe de calificación por edades de ‘Manderley’ (Archivo General de la Administración). Otro de esos materiales empleados fue el libro del artista e historiador Adolfo Fernández-Punsola ‘Nuestras vidas’, editado en 1996, que recoge fotografías y documentos de las décadas que retrata la película.

Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva y

Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas

Nunca sabe uno adónde le va a llevar abrir unas cajas viejas. Germán de la Riva recordaba vagamente el contenido de las que sus padres habían acumulado en la consulta. Psicólogos, fueron pioneros en materia de educación sexual en Santander en los años 80 y 90, con métodos traídos de su experiencia en Latinoamérica y EE UU. Dentro de las solapas de cartón, películas con imágenes artísticas pero explícitamente sexuales convivían con artículos y tesis científicas, un archivo que resultó idóneo para la labor investigadora que De la Riva lleva tiempo desarrollando junto a la también doctora en Bellas Artes y bailarina de danza contemporánea Itsaso Iribarren. Para ellos, toda su obra empieza en el cuerpo.

06:28 Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva | Fundación Santander

Memoria, sexualidad o cómo nos relacionamos físicamente son cuestiones que se pueden abordar apelando a los sentidos y la intuición. El arte tiene su propio camino hacia el conocimiento y, para Iribarren y De la Riva, mostrar ese proceso junto a la obra puede ser la mejor manera de hacer pedagogía: “El público entiende más o menos lo que ocurrió en las artes hasta las Vanguardias, pero existe un vacío, una desconexión, con las artes vivas y el presente de la creación”. Justo por ello, valoran y agradecen el compromiso de Faro Santander al generar un espacio que puede proveer al espectador de las piezas de puzle que le faltan.

Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva y

Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas Itsaso Iribarren y Germán de la Riva, doctores en Bellas Artes y practicantes de danza contemporánea y artes vivas, inician todas sus investigaciones plásticas a partir del cuerpo: el movimiento, el tacto, los sentidos. Es otro de los caminos de conocimiento que permite el arte y que merece exploración. Para documentar el proceso del proyecto ‘Flesh & Films / Pieles y pantallas’ y generar un resultado expositivo, han empleado, entre otros métodos y lenguaje, la filmación analógica en 16 milímetros. Las artes vivas son una disciplina contemporánea en la que las fronteras genéricas se borran, donde conviven ‘performance’, danza, teatro físico, música, texto y artes visuales. De la Riva y Iribarren aplauden la apuesta de Faro Santander por proyectos así, donde mostrar el proceso creativo es casi más importante que alcanzar un resultado final.

Son cuatro historias, cuatro pulsos creativos distintos que, sin embargo, pintan un mapa justo de los derroteros del arte español de hoy, siempre vivo y siempre a punto del naufragio, sin tablas de salvación como la que ofrece esta convocatoria de Faro Santander. Hay oportunidades que de verdad cambian vidas, instituciones que verdaderamente tienen la capacidad de generar un tejido cultural que cosa todo el norte de España y enseñe el tapiz con lo mejor de nuestra creación fuera.

Para presentarse a la nueva convocatoria no hace falta tener respuestas, tan solo ganas de pelearse con el runrún que provocan esas preguntas que merece la pena hacerse.

World.title: Abel Ferrara, el director maldito que dejó las drogas a los 61: “Mi rehabilitación se basa en dejar de decir mentiras”
World.content:
Es un clásico de Brian de Palma, pero hubo un tiempo en que Atrapado por su pasado (1993), el thriller criminal protagonizado por Al Pacino, pudo ser un éxito de Abel Ferrara (Bronx, Nueva York, 75 años). A principios de los noventa el legendario director llevaba un año ensayando con Al Pacino cuando apareció un guionista nuevo. Semanas después, Tom Pollock, jefe de Universal, le llamó aparte durante una cena en un restaurante de Cannes para hablarle de otra nueva versión del guion, lo cual a Ferrara le pareció una tomadura de pelo. Dejó su botella de vino blanco en la mesa de Pollock antes de ir a hablar con él, y al volver la cogió y se la metió dentro de la chaqueta, por esa costumbre neoyorquina de esconder el alcohol al salir a la calle. A los pocos días, le despidieron: alguien fue contando que le había robado una botella a Pollock.

Es una anécdota que encaja muy bien con la imagen errática de Abel Ferrara, la del director indomable, pasado de vueltas, casi siempre al borde del desastre y que ha alimentado su propio mito por encima de su obra. El legendario cineasta lleva más de cinco décadas haciendo películas bellísimas sobre culpa, deseo, violencia y fe, muchas de ellas en un Nueva York de camellos, gánsteres, cuestionables agentes del orden y vampiros existenciales: desde el policía de Teniente corrupto (1992) al espía industrial de New Rose Hotel (1998). Personajes, como él, con apetito por la autodestrucción.

Abel Ferrara, durante el rodaje de su película 'El funeral' (1996). TCD/Prod.DB, TCD/Prod.DB (Alamy/Cordon Press)

Pero Ferrara ha sabido romper con esa losa en su autobiografía Scene: A Memoir, publicada el año pasado. Entre semblanzas de las mujeres de su vida, rodajes y adicciones, el libro avanza a saltos hasta su desintoxicación en Italia. Contraviniendo el rimbombante título con el que se conoció en España a Carlito’s Way, es la historia de un hombre, al fin, liberado de su pasado. Cuenta, por ejemplo, cómo su amigo Salvatore Ruocco, actor y exboxeador, lo llevó a una clínica cerca de Nápoles y se ofreció a pagarle el tratamiento. Tony Palma, responsable del centro, rechazó el dinero de Ruocco porque cuidar de los adictos era para él una responsabilidad. El cineasta dejó las drogas allí a los 61 años, rodeado de chicos más jóvenes. “A la compasión de los italianos le debo la vida”, escribe en el libro. El cineasta había coincidido con Ruocco por primera vez en Napoli, Napoli, Napoli (2009).

La duda es si el mito de los excesos y la autodestrucción le sigue siendo útil ahora, en su tranquila veteranía de budista practicante en Italia, o si escribe sus memorias para desprenderse de él. “Tradicionalmente, un mito es una historia de dioses, héroes o cosas sobrenaturales para explicar lo inexplicable. Hoy se usa para describir una creencia falsa. Mi mundo es el de los seres humanos, no los dioses, y busco la verdad en lo que me rodea para escapar del autoengaño”, afirma, en conversación desde Roma. La historiadora de cine Nicole Brenez lo comparó con Joe Strummer, el líder de The Clash: un poeta que justifica la existencia de las formas populares. Abel Ferrara lamenta que su trabajo se simplifique en las definiciones que suelen acompañarlo. “Las películas, buenas y malas, revelan toda la vida, no solo el caos, el pecado y la violencia que pueden resultar obvios en algunas de mis obras. He rodado 35 películas, pero cuando la gente habla de mí, dudo que lo hagan desde la experiencia de haberlas visto todas”, observa. “Los actores que ves delante son también un reflejo de la gente que no ves, el equipo técnico. En eso que estás viendo está presente la vida de toda esa gente”.

Abel Ferrara y Madonna, en la presentación de la película 'The Addiction', en 1995. El dúo pudo reconstruir su amistad tras haber salido tarifando por 'Juego peligroso' (1993), la película que hicieron juntos. Jan Jarecki (WWD via Getty Images)

Su convivencia con los actores no siempre ha sido sencilla. Durante el rodaje de El funeral (1996), Chris Penn improvisó una escena y agarró a Vincent Gallo de la camisa, amenazando con pegarle, mientras Ferrara lo alentaba tras la cámara. En el libro Scene, recuerda que la toma por fin estaba funcionando, pero Isabella Rossellini, la coprotagonista, les dijo que estaban destrozando el guion y acudía al plató con miedo. Penn acabó llorando y pidiendo perdón. Otras de sus páginas más conmovedoras se las dedica a Zoë Lund, protagonista de Ángel de venganza (1981) y coguionista de Teniente corrupto, que falleció a causa de una sobredosis en 1999, a los 37 años.

El director puede parecer incancelable, a pesar de su caracter explosivo y, como mínimo, poco ortodoxo. No son muchos los realizadores que han expuesto tanto de sí mismos y por eso sorprende que en sus memorias no aparezcan ni Juego peligroso (1993), uno de sus trabajos más incómodos, ni Madonna, su estrella. En aquel largo, Harvey Keitel interpreta a un director que humilla a una actriz, encarnada por la cantante, para conseguir la interpretación que busca. Madonna criticó la película, se negó a ir al estreno y Ferrara la culpó de haberla hundido. Sin embargo, cuando se le pregunta si en el libro hubo alguien sobre quien le costara ser del todo sincero, responde: “No me habría sentado a escribir un libro si no fuera para confrontar la totalidad de mi pasado. ¿Es difícil ser sincero? Esa no es la cuestión. Mi rehabilitación se basa en ser rigurosamente honesto, en dejar de decir mentiras. Lo que está o no está en el libro no se debió a mi miedo a afrontar el pasado”.

Abel Ferrara, a las órdenes del director Josh Safdie durante el rodaje en Nueva York de 'Marty Supreme' (2025). Jose Perez/Bauer-Griffin (GC Images)

Recientemente, ha aparecido como actor en Marty Supreme (2025), la última película de Josh Safdie. Al hablar de ese supuesto cool neoyorquino que asociamos a los hermanos Safdie y a cineastas como él o Larry Cohen, reacciona: “Me hace gracia que reduzcas en Larry Cohen a todos los directores de Nueva York. Tienes que responder tú cuál es tu fascinación con Larry, no yo”. Reformulamos entonces para hablar de cómo se construyen esas grandes genealogías geográficas desde fuera. “Hay una larga lista de directores de Nueva York: John Cassavetes, Elia Kazan, Martin Scorsese... La lista es interminable, pero Woody Allen está tan lejos de Stanley Kubrick como de Oliver Stone. Cada ciudad moldea una visión del mundo”, dice.

En Roma, donde vive desde hace años, rodó durante la pandemia Zeros and Ones (2021), quizá la mejor película de su última etapa. Desde allí observa y da su veredicto sobre Estados Unidos: “No veo que esté en muy buen estado, igual que el resto del mundo. Creo en la bondad básica de la gente, pero la violencia que presenciamos nace de un entorno que da la espalda a lo espiritual y persigue la autosatisfacción. Somos ocho mil millones de personas en un solo planeta, lo que nos conecta es mucho mayor que lo que nos separa, pero hemos llegado al punto del asesinato industrial y la muerte llovida del cielo. La empatía y el amor ni siquiera entran en la conversación de quienes ocupan posiciones de poder. La ambición no es incompatible con una vida espiritual”.

World.title: POW campaigners keep up fight after cabinet limits compensation
World.content:
Campaigners for the widows of former Japanese prisoners of war have said they will keep fighting for compensation after the Dutch government said only surviving partners would be entitled to receive their spouses’ unpaid wages.

Long-term care minister Mirjam Sterk announced last Friday that the partners of civil servants and servicemen who were held captive following the invasion of Indonesia in 1942 would receive 42 months’ back pay, covering the period until the liberation in May 1945.

But Sterk said only widows who are still alive when the compensation scheme is launched on February 1 next year, all of whom are well into their nineties or older, would receive the payouts because a more extensive ruling would be “too complicated”.

The government has also cut the total size of the fund from the €50 mln announced in its last spring budget statement to €11.5 mln, on the basis that only a few hundred widows of the 40,000 men who were captured by the Japanese still survive.

The decision follows decades of campaigning for victims of the camps to be given the same treatment as Dutch government employees who were forced to work in Germany during World War II.

Moluccans

They include Moluccans who later fought on the side of the Dutch during the Indonesian liberation war and were subsequently persecuted by the independent government, prompting them to flee to the Netherlands.

Earlier this year prime minister Rob Jetten apologised to the Moluccan community for the way they were treated when they arrived in the 1950s.

Peggy Stein, of campaign group Indisch Platform 2.0, called for the ruling to be backdated to include widows who were alive when parliament approved a motion by farmers’ party leader Caroline van der Plas on the issue last April.

“That was when these people heard they were going to get their wages, but some of them have died in the meantime,” she told Dutch News.

Stein added that the cabinet appeared to have pushed through the ruling without waiting for parliament to debate the extent of the compensation scheme first.

“We still had to talk to MPs and had asked for a committee debate, but never had a reply,” she said.

“This isn’t about care or morality, it’s purely and solely about the technical settling of a case for the lowest possible cost.”

No official records

Sterk said it was “practically impossible” to compensate relatives of former camp inmates who had died because the government had no central records, but Stein said her campaign group had compiled its own list of detainees and could provide documentation showing they worked for the colonial administration.

“I have a list, but they say the SVB [Dutch social security bank] is legally not allowed to use it,” she said. “But if they have €50 million to spend, why can’t they find other parties to distribute the money who are able to work with us?”

Stein said she was not calling for the regulation to be scrapped, but it should be backdated to 2025 or 2015, when the government first acknowledged that the POWs were in its service. Prior to that it had argued that the colonial government in Indonesia was a separate entity.

Stein said the campaigners would continue to press the cabinet to compensate all victims of the Japanese occupation, including those who were no longer alive. “We have made a promise to these elderly people, we have signed a petition, and we are going to keep fighting for it,” she said.

World.title: Body of missing woman from Amsterdam found in suitcase
World.content:
The body of a woman who went missing after taking a lift on a bike with an unknown man has been found in a suitcase in Amsterdam.

Police said the remains were discovered last Friday in the Amstel river and identified as a woman named as Hajar, who was last seen two weeks ago near the Rai conference centre.

She left in the direction of Buitenveldert on October 4 on a black ladies’ bike with a man whom police are now trying to trace.

Police would not confirm reports on AT5 that a passer-by found the suitcase containing the body on Saturday morning, or that messages were sent to local neighbourhood app groups later that day asking if people had noticed anybody acting suspiciously with a suitcase.

She is described as between 1.65m and 1.70m tall with dark curly hair and dark eyes. The day before she was last seen alive she was wearing a tiger print dress and white New Balance shoes.

Anyone who saw Hajar between October 4 and October 17 or has any information can contact police on 0900 8844, via www.politie.nl, or anonymously via 0800 7000 or at Meld Misdaad Anoniem.

World.title: How expats tackle Dutch language issues without giving away data
World.content:
A letter from the Belastingdienst has landed on the doormat, and it might as well be written in code. At work, the team meeting that began in English has drifted into Dutch, and you’re nodding along while hoping nobody asks for your opinion. Sound familiar? We spoke with OmniForge, a tech company helping expats tackle the language barrier online.

Why the usual AI tools fall short

AI assistants promise to help with both of these challenges, but they have their limits. Firstly, many recording and transcription tools only support a handful of major languages, which leaves plenty of expats working in English by default, says Daniel G. Ríos, co-founder and CEO of OmniForge. Secondly, most of them process everything in the cloud, which is less than ideal when it comes to an employment contract, payslip or document with your BSN on it.

The risk is not theoretical. When hackers posted Odido’s customer data online, millions of people were reminded how far personal data can travel. “In the best case scenario, your data might be used to profile you for ads,” Daniel says, “but in the case of data exfiltration from cloud providers, your data might also be used for nefarious purposes.”

A local alternative, built by expats

OmniForge is a privacy-first AI desktop app for macOS and Windows that transcribes meetings and answers questions about your documents, all on your own computer. It was built by a team of expats in the Netherlands who, as Daniel puts it, “experience the exact same bilingual friction our users do.”

https://omniforge.online/dutchnews

“People should not have to compromise on their personal information in order to benefit from a service,” he says. In practice, the AI engine lives on your machine rather than in a data centre. “You could disconnect your WiFi entirely, and it will still securely transcribe your meetings and analyse your documents.” Only account login and subscription management are online.

There’s an environmental upside too, Daniel argues: running AI on your own computer’s spare processing power, what he calls “Green AI at the Edge,” can avoid the electricity and cooling water that big cloud models require from data centres.

When the meeting switches language

Language is where OmniForge stands out. It transcribes audio in 25 languages, including Dutch, English, German, French, Spanish and Polish, and can write summaries and answers in around 200 languages. In other words, a meeting held in Dutch can be summarised in whichever language you read most comfortably.

Then there’s the meeting that starts in English and slides into Dutch. Other tools make you pick a language in advance, Daniel says, whereas OmniForge listens for mid-sentence switches. He admits the transcript does not always get the spoken language right, but because the summary can be generated in any supported language regardless of the input, the gist still comes through.

A typical user, he says, is an international professional in a technical project meeting where half the team defaults to Dutch. Instead of stopping the flow to ask for translations, they record locally, having the assurance that a full English summary will be waiting the moment the meeting ends.

Decoding the paperwork

The same tool works on documents, not just audio. You can drop a Dutch PDF into OmniForge, whether it’s a letter from your landlord or your VvE, a payslip or a notice from the Belastingdienst, then ask questions and get an explanation in English.

Phone calls are covered, too. If you’re talking to the gemeente, put the phone on speaker and record the conversation: even if you feel lost during the call, OmniForge transcribes it so you have a comprehensive summary to review the moment you hang up. “It takes the stress out of local administration,” is how Daniel puts it.

Built for international teams

For employers, the same features make onboarding and internal meetings more inclusive: colleagues who are not fully fluent can follow along through a summary in their preferred language. And because OmniForge records locally, there’s no bot joining your video calls. A project manager juggling several projects can also keep a workspace for each, store meetings and documents together, and ask the assistant for recaps or highlights.

Moreover, local processing represents a win for compliance: HR handles sensitive employee data, and client confidentiality is non-negotiable. Companies are increasingly wary of staff feeding sensitive information to AI chatbots, Daniel explains. “Keeping everything in-house means GDPR compliance by default.” Many cloud tools go to great lengths to get certified, he notes, “but that just means they took steps to secure their customers’ data. With OmniForge, each customer is the sole owner of their data.”

Limitations and next steps

Daniel is upfront about OmniForge’s limits. Because everything runs on your device, transcription speed depends on your hardware: a brand-new machine will get through an hour-long meeting much faster than an older laptop. The assistant is above-average at summaries, highlights and finding information in your documents, “but it cannot compete with the likes of ChatGPT or Claude in terms of raw intelligence,” Daniel concedes, since it has a fraction of the resources.

OmniForge’s next steps will focus on speeding up the models on older hardware and adding more regional dialects. A mobile version is also planned, depending on how many people adopt the app.

Try it on your next confusing letter

The best first step, Daniel says, is to try OmniForge on your next meeting or baffling Dutch letter. Paid tiers start at €9.99 per month for unlimited quotas for individual users. But there’s a generous free tier so you can try before you buy: 40 complimentary minutes per recording and 50 indexed files. All you need to do is download OmniForge for Mac or Windows for free and register.

World.title: PM Jetten and partner expecting a baby in 2027
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Prime minister Rob Jetten is going to become a father next year, he announced on social media on Monday.

He and his partner, Argentinian professional hockey player Nicolás Keenan, wrote on Instagram: “Someone very special is on the way. See you in 2027, little one.”

The couple posted the message with a photo of themselves holding an ultrasound scan.

The pair also posted a picture with the baby’s surrogate mother, named as Lisa.

“There are no words big enough to thank our egg donor, our surrogate mum Lisa and both their families,” they wrote. “None of this would be possible without you.”

The message was written in Dutch, Spanish and English. A statement on the website of Jetten’s party, D66, says the surrogacy is not commercial and that Lisa and the donor, who are both Dutch, are acquaintances of Jetten and Keenan.

“I grew up in a warm and loving environment and now have a fantastic family of my own,” Lisa said in the statement. “With the unconditional support of our loved ones, surrogacy feels like a very special way to contribute to making our dear friends’ dream come true.”

World.title: England’s Dutch coach Sarina Wiegman extends contract until 2029
World.content:
Dutch football coach Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract with the England women’s team by two years, taking her up to the 2029 European Championships.

Wiegman, 56, led the team to two European titles in 2022 and 2025, as well as their first World Cup final in 2023, when they lost to Spain.

Prior to that she won the European Championships with the Dutch national team in 2017 and reached the World Cup final two years later, losing 2-0 to the United States.

“I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football,” she said in a statement released by the English Football Association (FA).

“Working for a world-class organisation like the FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day.”

FA chief executive Mark Bullingham described Wiegman as “an incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments”. He added: “There is no one better to lead the Lionesses into the next two tournaments.”

Commentators had widely expected the Dutchwoman to leave her post after next year’s World Cup, after England failed to qualify automatically for the tournament.

A 4-0 loss to Spain in June, the team’s heaviest defeat since Wiegman took charge, means they will have to come through a play-off tournament with Greece, Ukraine and Slovakia to reach the finals in Brazil.

Wiegman said: “Anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come.

“We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year.”

World.title: Border police won’t publish Schiphol e-gate investigation
World.content:
Hundreds of people missed their flights and thousands more faced long delays at Schiphol on Sunday after all 78 of the airport’s automatic passport gates went down at around 6am.

The Royal Marechaussee, the military police force responsible for border checks, said the outage was caused by an IT malfunction and that there was “no indication whatsoever” of a cyberattack.

The exact cause is still being investigated, but the results will not be made public, Marechaussee head of press, Major Mike Hofman, told Dutch News.

“For operational reasons, we do not comment regarding the further configuration, operation and technical details of our systems,” he said.

With the e-gates down, everyone flying to or from a country outside the Schengen area had to be checked manually by hand, including passengers in transit. The Marechaussee opened every desk and carried out less thorough checks to keep the queues moving.

Passengers waited an hour on average, and some waited up to an hour and a half, Schiphol officials said. The gates were working again by around 3pm.

KLM held departures where possible, and Transavia said it would be flexible with rebookings. A claims specialist told the Telegraaf the number of people affected in some way could run into the tens of thousands.

Few are likely to receive compensation, experts told the paper, because the outage will probably count as force majeure since the e-gates are run by the Marechaussee, not the airlines. The Marechaussee said travellers who missed their flights should contact their airline.

The outage happened during one of the busiest weekends of the autumn, as the one-week October school holiday began in the middle and south of the country and ended in the north. The Amsterdam marathon on Sunday also attracted thousands of runners to the city from all over the world.

World.title: Police investigate Grolsch beer tasting contamination
World.content:
Eleven people fell ill on Saturday afternoon after tasting water during a tour of the Grolsch brewery in Enschede. The water may have been contaminated with caustic soda, according to local broadcaster RTV Oost.

The group of nine visitors and two guides had been given shot glasses of the spring water used to brew the beer, a tasting that has been part of the tour for years.

One of the victims told RTV Oost that several people noticed a strange, sour taste and a burning feeling in their stomach after drinking it. Members of the group became nauseous and vomited, and the broadcaster said they may have suffered internal burns to the throat, oesophagus and stomach.

Several ambulances went to the brewery, and a German trauma team was called out but turned out not to be needed. All 11 were out of hospital on Sunday, and one spent the night in hospital, Grolsch told public broadcaster NOS.

Police have started a forensic investigation, and the labour inspectorate is also investigating. A police spokesperson told NOS it could have been an accident, “or something else could be going on”.

Grolsch said the tap the group drank from is separate from the rest of the production process, and that the quality and safety of its beer “are not and have not been at risk”. The company said it would not comment on possible causes while the investigation is ongoing.

World.title: Feyenoord stretch lead ahead of Eredivisie top clash against PSV
World.content:
Feyenoord have opened up a three-point lead at the top of the Eredivisie ahead of next weekend’s clash with PSV, following the defending champions’ shock defeat at ADO Den Haag.

The Rotterdammers were made to work for their points in a seven-goal thriller at Telstar.

They took the lead after just 25 seconds when Gaoussou Diarra finished off a sweeping move and were 3-1 up after 32 minutes when Sem Steijn profited from good combination work by Gjivai Zechiël and Givairo Read.

Patrick Brouwer reduced the deficit five minutes later, but a second-half penalty by Steijn proved to be enough despite Noach Shenkman scoring a third for Telstar on 69 minutes.

Peter Bosz refused to blame the last-minute defeat at ADO on his injury crisis as he looks ahead to a testing week, with a trip to Porto in the Champions League on Tuesday followed by the visit of Feyenoord on Sunday.

PSV looked to be on course for a routine win when Sven Mijnans put them ahead in the 21st minute. But the midfielder’s dismissal just before half-time triggered a second-half collapse that culminated in Matej Sin’s headed winner for ADO in the 93rd minute.

Mijnans, who played as a makeshift striker, will be suspended for the game against Feyenoord, while Guus Til also went off after complaining of blurred vision after landing hard on his neck in the first half and is doubtful for the next week.

But Bosz said he did not fear his team was sliding into a “tricky situation” in the absence of other senior players such as Jerdy Schouten, Ricardo Pepi and new signing Sami Ouaissa.

“This is another chance to win a game,” he said. “Stick our chests out and not think in fear.”

AZ drop points

AZ Alkmaar also dropped points against a newly promoted club as they could only draw 2-2 with Cambuur Leeuwarden even after the Friesland club lost Devid Bouah to a second yellow card early in the second half.

Twente Enschede missed the chance to leap into second place as Spanish striker Ángel Alarcón scored two superb goals for Utrecht to lift Anthony Correia’s team to 11th place.

Julian Brandt and Jorthy Mokio both scored twice as Ajax won 5-2 in Groningen in a match that saw both goalkeepers save penalties.

A double by Anthony Descotte looked to have earned Fortuna Sittard the points at NEC until Willum Thór Willumsson popped up with an injury-time header to snatch a draw for the struggling Nijmegen club.

World.title: Poland breaks up international criminal group accused of laundering €77 million
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland says it has broken up an international criminal group responsible for laundering an estimated 337 million zloty (€77 million) by using currency exchange offices to illegally process money obtained from internet scams. Nine suspects – eight Ukrainians and one Belarusian – have been detained in a series of raids, which also resulted in the seizure of gold and cash worth over 1 million zloty. Służby rozbiły międzynarodową grupę zajmującą się praniem pieniędzy z oszustw inwestycyjnych i kryptowalut. Zatrzymano 9 osób, a skala transakcji przekroczyła 337 mln zł. Zabezpieczono złoto i gotówkę wartą ponad 1 mln zł. @Straz_Graniczna @PolicjaCBZC @ABW_GOV_PL pic.twitter.com/g2NQoqaPvP — Marcin Kierwiński (@MKierwinski) October 19, 2026 The accused – four women and five men aged between 26 and 53 – were arrested in Łódź, Warsaw and Małopolska province, announced Krzysztof Kopania, spokesman for the Łódź regional prosecutor’s office, which is leading the investigation. The detainees are four female cashiers, three men running the exchange offices, and two couriers used to transport money. All have been charged with participating in an organised criminal group and money laundering. They could face up to 15 years in prison if convicted. Prosecutors say that the gang, which operated in the cities of Warsaw, Lublin, Wrocław, Katowice and Gdańsk, collected money that had been obtained through internet fraud and transported it to cryptocurrency exchanges. It was then processed without complying with anti-money laundering procedures. Proceeds were then transferred to bank accounts, sent abroad by car, or concealed in fictitious purchases of gold. Most money was ultimately invested in cryptocurrencies. “The scale of the operation was enormous,” said Kopania. “It is estimated that between February 2025 and July 2026, members of the group took steps to conceal the origins of approximately 337 million zloty.” The ringleader was a 34-year-old Ukrainian national who made the key decisions and oversaw the domestic and international channelling of funds obtained from illegal sources, according to the Internal Security Agency (ABW) and border guard, which were also involved in the operation. Seven of the accused have been placed in pre-trial detention for three (or in one case two) months, while two have been bailed and ordered not to leave Poland. World.title: Lithuania says Ukrainian drone that struck car entered its airspace from Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. This article has been updated to include a statement from Poland’s defence ministry issued on Monday afternoon. Lithuania says there is “no doubt” that a Ukrainian drone which exploded on its territory on Sunday, hitting a moving car, entered its airspace from Poland. However, Poland has so far said that there is no confirmation of an object crossing the border. Meanwhile, Ukraine has apologised for the incident, saying that Russian electronic warfare had diverted the drone’s path during an operation against military targets in Russia. Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine is spilling over onto the Eastern flank of NATO and EU. This morning, NATO fighter jets stationed at Šiauliai Air Base scrambled once again after an unidentified object entered Lithuanian airspace. What appears to be a drone exploded… — Gitanas Nausėda (@GitanasNauseda) October 18, 2026 On Sunday morning, Lithuania confirmed that a drone had entered its airspace and exploded, causing damage to a moving vehicle. NATO jets were scrambled in response to the incursion but were not able to visually identify the object. President Gitanas Nausėda said that the incident was further evidence that “Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine is spilling over onto the Eastern flank of NATO and [the] EU”. Meanwhile, Lithuanian defence minister Robertas Kaunas revealed that preliminary information indicated the drone had entered from Polish airspace. “I have already contacted the Polish defence minister and asked Poland to join the investigation so that we can look into this incident together,” said Kaunas, quoted by broadcaster LRT. However, a spokesman for Poland’s defence ministry, Janusz Sejmej, told the Polish Press Agency (PAP) on Sunday that “there is no confirmation [from our radar systems] of [an object] crossing the border from Poland to Lithuania”. Polsat, a leading Polish broadcaster, cited unnamed sources at Poland’s defence ministry saying that they believed the drone in fact took off from within Lithuanian territory, around 30 kilometres from the Polish border, and then flew deep into the country. In response, Deividas Matulionis, an advisor to the Lithuanian president, told the Baltic News Service (BNS) on Monday that “I can say very unequivocally we have credible evidence that the drone crossed the Polish border”. Later, the country’s prime minister, Mindaugas Sinkevičius, said that “there is no doubt that it entered…from the Polish side”. He also confirmed that the evidence indicates the drone “is of Ukrainian origin”. We regret the incident that occurred this morning in Lithuanian airspace, which may have resulted from Russian electronic warfare diverting drones during an operation against legitimate military targets in Russia. We apologise for any disruption, risks, and concern this may have… — Heorhii Tykhyi (@SpoxUkraineMFA) October 18, 2026 Those remarks followed a statement on Sunday afternoon from Heorhii Tykhyi, the spokesman for Ukraine’s foreign ministry, who appeared to confirm that the drone was Ukrainian. “We regret the incident that occurred this morning in Lithuanian airspace, which may have resulted from Russian electronic warfare diverting drones during an operation against legitimate military targets in Russia,” wrote Tykhyi. “We apologise for any disruption, risks, and concern this may have caused.” The spokesman said that Ukraine would “share all relevant information with our Lithuanian partners to establish the full circumstances of the incident”. However, he gave no further information on what type of drone was involved, where it was launched from, and what its target was. Lithuania borders Belarus, an ally of Russia, and the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, as well as Poland and Latvia. In March and May this year, a number of Ukrainian drones aimed at targets in Russia entered the airspaces of NATO members Lithuania, Latvia, Estonia and Finland, likely due to Russian electronic jamming. On Monday afternoon, Poland’s defence ministry issued a statement “strongly refuting” media reports suggesting that sources within the ministry had identified the drone as having taken off within Lithuania itself. It added that the ministry, in cooperation with its Lithuanian partners, was still “conducting a detailed analysis” of what had taken place. Poland has condemned an attack by masked Israeli settlers on a delegation of European diplomats – including Polish ones – that was visiting the West Bank. It called for a “decisive response from the Israeli authorities”, saying that the incident is “further evidence of the settler violence that the Palestinian population in the West Bank faces on a daily basis”. The attack has likewise been condemned by France and Belgium, whose nationals were also in the delegation, and the European Union, as well as by the Israeli foreign minister. Masked Israeli settlers attacked European diplomats, a French mayor and Palestinians in the occupied West Bank, prompting European condemnation. The violence comes amid unprecedented settler pogroms during the olive harvest. pic.twitter.com/wsP6edL62y — Al Jazeera English (@AJEnglish) October 18, 2026 On Saturday, the delegation – which included members from France, Belgium and Poland as well as representatives of the Catholic church – visited the mostly Christian Palestinian village of Taybeh near Ramallah in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. They had come to assess the situation following regular recent attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians trying to harvest olives on their own land. During the visit, the delegation came under attack, with parts of the incident caught on camera. France’s foreign minister, Jean-Noël Barrot, reported that Bernard Baudoux, mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, had been “violently assaulted” during the incident. He demanded that Israel arrest the perpetrators and “urgently put an end to these criminal acts of violence”. Late on Saturday afternoon, the spokesman for Poland’s foreign ministry, Maciej Wewiór, issued a statement confirming that the attack had taken place and that the delegation had included an unspecified number of Polish diplomats, who he said had not been harmed. “We express our deep outrage and strongly condemn this incident,” added Wewiór. “Poland consistently opposes violence by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank. Attacks on representatives of the diplomatic corps are absolutely unacceptable.” The spokesman said that Poland now “expects urgent and detailed explanations from the Israeli authorities” and for the perpetrators of the attack to be identified and held accountable. “We also expect effective measures to prevent similar incidents in the future.” ❗Potwierdzamy, że na Zachodnim Brzegu Jordanu doszło do ataku na konwój, w którym znajdowali się przedstawiciele korpusu dyplomatycznego, w tym polscy dyplomaci. The incident “is further evidence of the settler violence that the Palestinian population in the West Bank faces on a daily basis”, they added, calling for a “decisive response from the Israeli authorities”. The attack was also “strongly condemned” on Sunday by the European Union’s diplomatic service, which said that it “expects full accountability as well as effective measures to prevent continued acts of violence and violent harassment against Palestinians”. The IDF strongly condemns the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters. Police forces and forensic investigators from the Judea and Samaria District are entering the area accompanied by… — Israel Defense Forces (@IDF) October 17, 2026 The incident involving the diplomatic group came a day after around 80 Israeli settlers had attacked Palestinians harvesting olives, with Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine among those injured. Levine told the Committee to Protect Journalists, an American non-profit organisation, that she had been pushed to the ground by a group of masked settlers, who “were kicking me for I think at least 10 minutes”. In May, Poland issued a five-year entry ban on Israeli national security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir for his treatment of detained activists, including Polish citizens, from a flotilla seeking to reach Gaza. World.title: Poland moves to allow more municipalities to charge tourist fee
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Many more municipalities in Poland will be allowed to charge a daily fee for tourists and other overnight visitors after a change to the law dropping environmental requirements for levying such charges. Kraków, which received 8.7 million overnight tourists last year, had in particular been pushing for the change. However, Poland as a whole has seen a recent boom in visitor numbers, recording the EU’s second-fastest growth in the number of nights in tourist accommodation last year. #Krakow #opłataturystyczna #ustawa 🚨🔥Z OSTATNIEJ CHWILI! 🔥🚨 📢 Prezydent RP podpisał nowelizację przepisów dotyczących podatków i opłat lokalnych, PIT oraz PCC. 🏨 Najważniejsze zmiany dla branży turystycznej dotyczą opłaty miejscowej i uzdrowiskowej. 🗓️ Od 2027 r. za jej… pic.twitter.com/9ATvENvNol — Kraków (@krakow_pl) October 15, 2026 Until now, a “visitor’s fee” could be levied by municipalities with beneficial climatic features, “scenic qualities” and the capacity to accommodate people visiting to benefit from these attributes, as well as localities in areas with the status of a “spa protection area”. In practice, this largely applied to seaside and mountain resorts. Kraków did charge a visitor’s fee between 2004 and 2015, but was subsequently unable to do so due to a toughening of environmental requirements. The city has long suffered from bad air pollution, though it has taken significant steps to tackle the issue. Now, under new legislation proposed by the government earlier this year and signed into law by President Karol Nawrocki this week, the requirement for beneficial climatic features has been scrapped, meaning many more places will be able to charge the visitor’s fee. From 1 January, municipalities with scenic qualities will be able to charge visitors up to 5 zloty (€1.14) for each night they stay in hotels, guesthouses and short-term rental accommodation for up to one month, a rise on the current maximum of 3.46 zloty. Additionally, whereas previously only people visiting for the purposes of tourism had to pay, the fee now applies to all visits, including for work or health purposes, reports broadcaster TVN. People with significant disabilities, children with certified disabilities and their carers will be exempt from the fee. In another change, fees will be collected directly by accommodation providers, who will be required to maintain detailed records, reports the Infor news service. Passing fees on in a timely manner will entitle providers to receive at least 10% of the money they collect. Poland saw the EU's second-fastest growth in tourism in 2025, behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta https://t.co/WVkRbHtU7o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 19, 2026 In 2024, Kraków appealed to the government to be allowed to charge tourists a fee, noting that “overtourism leads to tensions and social discontent”, as the “local community suffers” and “residents increasingly feel like tourists in their own city”. With its UNESCO-listed Old Town, Wawel royal castle, and former Jewish district of Kazimierz, Kraków is regularly named as one of Europe’s best tourist destinations. Last year, a record 16.25 million people visited the city, of whom 8.7 million stayed overnight. While that is a boon to the local economy, it also often causes tensions with residents, who complain about noise and disruption. In 2024, the city created the new position of “night mayor”, whose role is to reconcile the needs of tourists, businesses and residents. Poland’s government has approved legislation that would allow local communities to ban short-term rentals of the type offered through services such as Airbnb. Such accommodation has boomed in recent years, often prompting a backlash from local residents https://t.co/8MRfRWTDxd — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 3, 2026 Following this week’s change to the law, Kraków city hall confirmed that it would now again be able to collect a visitor’s fee “if the statutory conditions are satisfied and the municipal council adopts an appropriate resolution”. The city’s recently elected new mayor, Łukasz Gibała, who will be sworn in next week, said before Sunday’s election that he was in favour of a tourist tax of at least 20 zloty per night, four times the new maximum. “In western European cities there are rates of that size and higher,” Gibała said, quoted by financial news service Money.pl. “Maintaining the city in the face of the influx of tourists is costly. In Kraków, private business owners profit from tourism, whilst the city and its residents foot the bill.” Poland as a whole has also experienced a boom in tourism. Last year, the country recorded the European Union’s second-largest growth in the number of nights spent in tourist accommodation. Its increase of 7% was behind only the Mediterranean island state of Malta (9.9%). World.title: Poland drops proposal to criminalise providing help to illegal migrants following outcry
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s interior ministry has withdrawn a proposal to make it a criminal offence, punishable by up to three years in prison, to provide support to migrants who are in the country illegally. The idea had prompted criticism from human rights groups and even opposition from within the government. The interior ministry said the amendment had been intended to clamp down on migrant smuggling. But activists feared it would criminalise humanitarian aid, such as that provided to migrants who have irregularly crossed the border from Belarus. Za udzielenie bezinteresownej pomocy migrantom nie będzie groziła kara do trzech lat więzienia. Po burzy, którą wywołała publikacja „Rzeczpospolitej” i po sprzeciwie resortu rodziny, MSWiA wycofuje się z pomysłu „karania za podanie posiłku”.https://t.co/Q0N52IMRVn — Rzeczpospolita (@rzeczpospolita) October 15, 2026 Under current Polish law, anyone who facilitates the illegal stay of a person in Poland in exchange for financial or personal benefit can be jailed for up to five years. However, this week, the interior ministry proposed an amendment that would also have penalised anyone who knowingly “enabled or facilitated” the illegal stay of someone in Poland, even if not for financial or personal benefit. The offence would have been punishable by up to three years in prison. “Currently, this behaviour is not criminalised, creating a loophole for those who exploit such situations and, under the pretext of helping migrants, aid them in their illegal stay, thus serving as a springboard for further illegal migration,” wrote deputy interior minister Czesław Mroczek, quoted by the Rzeczpospolita daily. That immediately prompted concern that the law could be used against volunteers and residents of border areas who provide aid – such as food, water, medical treatment, clothing or shelter – to migrants who have crossed illegally from Belarus. Since 2021, tens of thousands of people, mainly from Asia and Africa, have tried to cross that border with the encouragement and support of the Belarusian authorities. They have sometimes used violence against Polish border officers. Poland and the EU accuse Belarus of “weaponising” migration as part of the “hybrid warfare” being waged by Russia and its allies against European countries. They have implemented tough border protection measures to prevent crossings and facilitate “pushbacks” of those who cross. However, many human rights and aid organisations argue that the migrants – over 100 of whom have died around the border since 2021 – are often victims of this process and need humanitarian support. Two dead bodies found in the river on Poland's border with Belarus likely belong to migrants from a group seen being pushed into the water by Belarusian officers as part of efforts to encourage irregular crossings into the EU, says a Polish minister https://t.co/xsnPd6FeO3 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 16, 2025 In response to the interior ministry’s proposal, 61 organisations, including Amnesty International, the Helsinki Foundation for Human Rights and the Auschwitz-Birkenau Foundation, signed a joint statement condemning the plans, which they said “violate international standards binding Poland”. The organisations warned that the proposed wording could expose medical staff treating migrants, lawyers providing legal assistance, facilities working with children, and organisations supporting victims of human trafficking to criminal liability. “This measure is not aimed at smugglers, but rather at activists or residents of border areas who provide humanitarian aid to foreign nationals who have crossed the border illegally and are present in Poland,” attorney Radosław Baszuk told the Rzeczpospolita daily. Baszuk previously represented five Polish activists who were prosecuted for providing food, clothing and shelter to a group of Middle Eastern migrants who had entered Poland from Belarus in 2022. A group of five activists have been found not guilty of enabling the illegal presence in Poland of Middle Eastern migrants whom they provided aid to after they had irregularly crossed the border from Belarus. Prosecutors had been seeking prison sentences https://t.co/RpfhVWL4hY — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 8, 2025 They were acquitted last year, with the ruling made final in March this year after an appeal. But Baszuk told Rzeczpospolita that, under the interior ministry’s proposed amendment to the relevant law, his clients could been convicted. On Wednesday, Poland’s commissioner for human rights, Sylwia Gregorczyk-Abram, also wrote to the justice ministry to “express concern” that the proposed changes “could lead to criminal liability for charitable or humanitarian activities undertaken towards individuals whose residence status has not yet been regulated”. Even a member of the government, the minister for family, labour and social policy, Agnieszka Dziemianowicz-Bąk, expressed her “firm opposition” to the plans on social media. She is from The Left (Lewica), one of the junior partners in Poland’s ruling coalition. ‼️ Ciepły posiłek, nocleg, potrzebne leki – za to wolontariusz ma trafić do więzienia nawet na 3 lata? 😡 Nie ma zgody Lewicy na kryminalizowanie pomocy humanitarnej! Ministra Agnieszka Dziemianowicz-Bąk zwróciła się do ministra Waldemara Żurka ze stanowczym sprzeciwem wobec… pic.twitter.com/QskUfJmgsu — Lewica (@__Lewica) October 14, 2026 In response to the growing criticism, the interior ministry announced on Friday that it was withdrawing the proposal, saying it decided to do so “to eliminate any doubts and prevent the misinterpretation of regulations”. “From the beginning, the ministry’s sole objective has been to tighten the system and target the organisers of this practice [of migrant smuggling],” said the ministry, quoted by Rzeczpospolita. “Legal provisions must effectively protect the state’s borders against organised crime, while simultaneously fully safeguarding humanitarian values ​and life-saving activities.” The number of attempted illegal crossings by migrants from Belarus to Poland fell from 15,500 in the first half of 2025 to 235 this year – a drop of over 98% Poland also now claims a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally https://t.co/RFZkd7CeIk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 20, 2026 Both the former Polish government and the current one, which took power in December 2023, have regularly faced criticism from human rights groups over their response to the migration crisis on the Belarus border. Earlier this year, the previous human rights commissioner, Marcin Wiącek, expressed concern over a ban on asylum claims introduced by the government in March 2025. He noted that the measures had been described as a temporary solution, but have remained in place ever since. The government, however, argues that its measures have been effective in preventing the illegal trafficking of migrants. Its data show that attempted border crossings from Belarus fell from around 15,500 in the first half of last year to less than 250 in the same period this year – a drop of over 98%. It also now claims to have a 100% success rate in apprehending migrants who manage to cross illegally. World.title: Heads of Polish and Ukrainian national remembrance institutes hold first meeting since 2018
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Senior delegations from Poland and Ukraine’s state institutes of national remembrance have held talks in the Ukrainian city of Lviv, marking the first time the heads of the two organisations have met in eight years. The meeting, at which the two sides discussed issues including exhumations of World War Two victims and possible joint research projects, comes as Poland and Ukraine seek reconciliation over historical issues that have regularly caused tensions between two otherwise close allies. 📢 14 października 2026 r. we Lwowie delegacja Instytutu Pamięci Narodowej spotkała się z przedstawicielami ukraińskiego Instytutu Pamięci Narodowej. Było to pierwsze bezpośrednie, robocze spotkanie szefów tych instytucji od 2018 r. ➡️ Stronie polskiej przewodniczył kierujący… pic.twitter.com/qHpZwLeCEa — Instytut Pamięci Narodowej (@ipngovpl) October 14, 2026 News of the meeting was announced on social media by Poland’s Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), which noted that it was “the first direct, working meeting between the heads of these institutions since 2018”. The IPN is currently headed by its deputy president, Karol Polejowski, because Poland’s parliament has been unable to agree on a permanent new president. The Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance (UINR) is led by Oleksandr Alfyorov. “The first topic of discussion,” according to the IPN, was the planned reburial of 115 Polish soldiers recently exhumed in Lviv, where they died in 1939 defending the city (then part of Poland and known as Lwów) during the Nazi-German and Soviet invasions. Polish and Ukrainian researchers have exhumed the remains of 115 Polish soldiers who died in 1939 defending Lviv – now in Ukraine but then part of Poland and known as Lwów – during the invasions by Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union at the start of WWII https://t.co/yQNeq2D54E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 2, 2026 Their exhumation resulted from a diplomatic breakthrough last year between Warsaw and Kyiv that saw Ukraine lift a moratorium on exhumations that had been in place since 2017 in protest at the dismantling in Poland of a monument to the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA). Ukraine has also allowed the exhumation on its territory of Polish victims of the Volhynia massacres, which were led by the UPA. Poland likewise recently granted permission for Ukraine to search for Ukrainian victims of a massacre led by the Polish Home Army in the village of Łasków (Laskiv in Ukrainian). At this week’s meeting, the UINR gave an update on its work in Łasków, where it has uncovered the remains of 30 people. The Ukrainian Institute of National Remembrance has found 30 human remains in a village in Poland where Polish partisans killed Ukrainian civilians in WW2 It thanked Poland for permission to search the site, calling it a step towards "true reconciliation" https://t.co/BeeEtl6gCa — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 15, 2026 The IPN and UINR also discussed planned exhumation work in the now-depopulated village of Huta Pieniacka (Huta Peniatska in Ukrainian), where the local Polish population was massacred in 1944 by a Nazi SS regiment mainly made up of Ukrainians. There was also “willingness on both sides to restore cooperation in the field of historical scientific research”, said the IPN. “The possibility of undertaking joint educational initiatives was also discussed.” The two sides also agreed to hold another meeting in Warsaw, though no date has been set. This week’s meeting comes after a period of tension over historical issues between not only Poland and Ukraine more broadly, but also the two countries’ remembrance institutes. In February this year, the IPN criticised Alfyorov over an interview in which he initially called the Volhynia massacres “one of Poland’s state myths”, before later appearing to correct himself and saying it was “not a myth, but one of the key elements of the Polish grand narrative”. By contrast, “for most Ukrainians, this is just a local episode of history”, added Alfyorov. Referring to Poland’s recognition of the massacres as a genocide – a term Ukraine rejects – he asked if Polish massacres of around 28,000 Ukrainians during the war should also be called a genocide. In response, the IPN called Alfyorov’s remarks “outrageous” and declared that the Volhynia massacres were “not an ‘episode’, but rather one of the largest genocides against civilians in 20th-century Europe”. It also condemned Ukraine for honouring figures associated with the massacres. The UINR, for its part, criticised a law proposed by Poland’s president, Karol Nawrocki (a former head of the IPN), that would criminalise the promotion of ideologies associated with World War Two Ukrainian nationalist groups. Ukraine has criticised a law proposed by Poland's president that would criminalise promotion of historical Ukrainian nationalist ideologies, equating them with Nazism and communism It warns of "retaliatory measures" if the bill is passed https://t.co/TaX2Vj5z8v — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 2, 2025 In another sign of reconciliation, in May the UINR and Poland’s Mieroszewski Centre held a historical congress in Warsaw, bringing together more than 100 historians “to discuss complex issues of the shared past and explore common approaches to their interpretation”, in the words of the Ukrainian foreign ministry. However, that same month, President Volodymyr Zelensky prompted a diplomatic crisis by approving the naming of a Ukrainian military unit after the “heroes of the UPA”. That prompted Nawrocki to strip Zelensky of Poland’s highest honour, the Order of the White Eagle. Since then, both sides have made efforts to reach a diplomatic solution, including a pledge by Zelensky to “grant a substantial number of permits for search and exhumation work”. World.title: Ukraine finds remains of 30 people in search for victims of massacre by Polish WWII partisans
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work!
