World.title: 1,200-year-old archaeological site discovered Iraq’s Babil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The central Iraqi province of Babil announced on Sunday that an exciting archaeological site has been discovered.

Located in the al-Qasim district in the southern part of the province, the remains are believed to date back to the Abbasid era, a period of immense cultural, scientific, and architectural prosperity throughout Iraq.

The Governor of Babil, Ali al-Jamali, conducted an official site visit to examine the structural features, evaluate its historical context, and lay out administrative frameworks to safeguard the artifacts under strict national archaeological laws.

Local officials stressed that this discovery goes much beyond the previous statistics. Professional excavations and investigations are likely to provide additional details about ancient life centuries ago.

Officials are investigating legal alternatives for securely developing the area into a significant tourist destination, raising Babil’s global historical prominence.

The recent announcement follows the discovery of a large ancient city in Basra, dating back 1,200 years, as well as the uncovering of hundreds of ancient Islamic and Hellenistic artifacts revealed by rain at the Borsippa site, both occurring in 2025. This adds to a remarkable series of historical discoveries in Iraq.

The newly discovered archaeological site in Babil’s al-Qasim district provides a crucial physical link to the vast networks that powered the Islamic Golden Age. During the Abbasid era, Iraq was the undisputed geopolitical and economic center of the Islamic world.

World.title: Iraq increases oil exports to 3.4 million barrels per day
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Oil Basim Khudair said on Monday that the export rate during October has risen to 3.4 million barrels per day through three routes, including the Strait of Hormuz.

Iraq’s crude oil export in October surpassed 3.4 million barrels per day through the Strait of Hormuz, the Turkish port of Ceyhan, and the Syrian port of Baniyas, according to Khudair.

Despite the military conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, the Iraqi Ministry of Oil—through the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO)—has managed to maintain an average export rate of three million barrels per day over the past nine months, according to the oil minister.

However, since the beginning of October, the export rate has risen to over 3.4 million barrels per day, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The Ministry of Oil is trying to boost export capacity, which will provide financial revenue for the state. Khudair noted that developing export capacity will allow the government to carry out its tasks and secure the required funds for different governmental expenditures.

Khudair noted that crude oil exports are directed to European and Asian markets, as well as the American market.

Eco Iraq revealed on Saturday that oil production during September reached its highest daily average since the beginning of 2026, at 4.39 million barrels per day.

Iraq’s oil output stayed at normal levels in January and February, averaging more than 4.1 million barrels per day, before falling drastically in March as a result of the war in the region.

Iraq’s average daily oil output was 4.09 million barrels in January and 4.14 million barrels in February before falling to 1.9 million barrels in March and 1.63 million in April.

In May, the country’s oil production fell to 1.4 million barrels per day before rising to 1.52 million in June.

The improvement in oil output continued until the third quarter of the year. According to figures from OPEC, average output increased to 2.9 million barrels per day in July, 3.74 million barrels per day in August, and 4.39 million barrels per day in September.

World.title: Iraq, World Bank discuss financing strategic projects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Finance Minister Faleh Sari and World Bank Group Vice President for the Middle East and North Africa Ousmane Dione discussed on Thursday financing strategic projects and support for economic reforms in Iraq.

The meeting took place on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank Group, held in Bangkok, Thailand, according to a statement released by the Finance Ministry.

Sari stressed the World Bank’s role in Iraq’s economic and financial transformation. He outlined the country’s desire to use the World Bank’s expertise and financial contributions to carry out significant projects in the energy, education, transportation, and digital transformation sectors.

The step aims to promote sustainable development and improve the efficiency of public services in Iraq, according to Sari.

Dione praised the collaboration with the Iraqi Finance Ministry, indicating that it has efficiently arranged its operational and communication mechanisms with the World Bank.

The World Bank official highlighted that the efforts of the Iraqi government pave the way for additional initiatives to support the country’s economic and financial goals in the upcoming period.

Sari reaffirmed last week Iraq’s commitment to continuing economic and financial reforms, diversifying revenue sources, and strengthening the role of the private sector.

According to Sari, these measures aim to bolster economic stability and enhance the country’s capacity to deal with regional challenges.

Sari noted that the government is addressing the economic consequences of the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz by reprioritizing expenditures, increasing non-oil revenues, and maintaining the state’s essential obligations while pursuing structural reforms.

“Iraq Vision 2050” represents a strategic plan for reducing dependency on oil, broadening production, empowering the private sector, and achieving inclusive and sustainable economic growth, according to Sari.

The minister noted that the reform package includes enhancing public financial management, automating customs and tax operations, boosting the business and investment climate, upgrading the banking sector, and increasing electronic payment systems.

According to Sari, the partnership with the IMF and the World Bank Group supports the economic and financial reform program.

World.title: Chinese oilfield service firm markets Iraq’s oil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – China-based Anton Oilfield Services Group has sold its first Iraqi crude oil shipment as part of a new supply deal with the State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO).

According to Reuters, the unique arrangement with one of a few Chinese independent oil corporations expanding their activities in Iraq enables Baghdad to access cash to pay service suppliers.

Iraq is attempting to bolster oil exports impacted by the military conflict in the Middle East. In the past few months, greater discounts have enticed traders and refiners, leading to a resurgence in its oil shipments.

The Chinese firm said in a statement on Saturday that the agreement intends to improve Basra Oil Company’s (BOC) crude oil sales and cash flow, provide channels for engineering and services, and expedite payment collection for Anton and partners.

An official in the oil sector indicated that Anton struck an agreement with SOMO to market undetermined amounts of Iraqi crude oil, mostly from the Majnoon oilfield managed by BOC.

In late September, Anton marketed one million barrels of Basra Heavy crude to a trading company.

Anton mentioned that the agreement with SOMO allows it to sell oil from the Dhufriya oilfield in eastern Iraq, where it received a license in 2024 to develop the field.

World.title: Iraq inaugurates first satellite ground station
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Minister of Communications Mustafa Sanad inaugurated on Sunday Iraq’s first satellite ground station in Baghdad, a step aiming to bolster digital sovereignty and develop the country’s telecommunications infrastructure.

In a speech he delivered during the inauguration ceremony, Sanad said that Iraq’s acquisition of a satellite would be impossible without a ground station.

The new facility will serve as a cornerstone for the country’s upcoming national space program, with future expansions planned to establish additional ground stations across other Iraqi provinces depending on population density and administrative assessment.

The station also acts as a complete technological hub that includes a satellite communication gateway, a localized data center, and an internet exchange point.

Developed in partnership with the technology group Commercis, the station links incoming satellite communications directly into Iraq’s expanding domestic fiber-optic terrestrial network.

Iraq previously relied on international infrastructure located outside its borders to route satellite traffic. The government is now actively urging ministries, private companies, and security agencies to migrate their traffic to this local gateway to secure sensitive data.

The station is part of a broader economic vision to transform Iraq into a regional data corridor. By leveraging its geographic location, Iraq aims to serve as a high-speed data transit bridge connecting networks across Asia, Africa, and Europe.

The station provides high-speed enterprise internet, secure government communications, live television feeds, and commercial satellite broadcasting.

World.title: Competing narratives emerge over blast at PMF security compound in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Two days after a powerful blast ripped through a Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) security headquarters in eastern Baghdad, an investigative report published by Al Mada newspaper and monithas revealed sharp contradictions surrounding the incident, presenting four competing narratives ranging from a targeted foreign strike to sabotage and munitions mismanagement.

The explosion struck at approximately 6:00 PM on Saturday, October 17, 2026, inside a facility operated by the PMF Security Directorate located along Sadr Al-Qanat near the Saad Al-Watri Hospital.

While the PMF’s official communique attributed the incident to an internal fire that detonated obsolete, deteriorated munitions—resulting in minor injuries to five personnel—field sources cited by Al Mada report over twenty injuries among PMF security personnel and unidentified associates. Strict security cordons accompanied the medical evacuation via PMF ambulances, fueling speculation regarding the potential presence of Iranian technical personnel at the site.

The circumstances have ignited debate over the operational nature of the facility. As an intelligence and security installation, the complex is not designated to warehouse expired ordnance. Security sources cited in the report claimed that newly arrived military consignments from Iran had been transferred into the depot just a week prior to the detonation.

Preliminary forensic findings referenced in the investigation point to the possibility of an incoming projectile initiating the primary blast, though information sharing on the file remains tightly restricted by the PMF Chief of Staff’s office while a specialized investigative committee established by Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi conducts its inquiry.

Four Competing Accounts

World.title: Iraq opens public university admissions for international schools’ graduates
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research announced on Monday, October 19, 2026, that the electronic admissions portal for international school graduates applying to public universities will open within the coming days for the 2026–2027 academic year.

According to a ministerial press release obtained by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), admissions processing will be managed through the centralized digital application platform Qaddim.

Eligible candidates graduating from accredited international curricula within Iraq will access the admissions system using their standardized examination sequence number and confidential verification credentials issued directly by their respective school administrations.

The ministry advised prospective students and guardians to monitor its official web portal and recognized digital channels for forthcoming regulatory guidelines, grade-weighting criteria, and precise application submission schedules.

The upcoming portal launch represents an institutional mechanism to integrate international school diploma holders into national university admissions channels alongside graduates of the standard ministerial secondary baccalaureate examinations.

World.title: US dollar edges up to 169,500 IQD in Baghdad and provincial exchanges
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged upward across parallel retail and wholesale counters in Baghdad and major commercial hubs on Monday, October 19, 2026.

The capital recorded an increase of 500 dinars per $100 compared to prior trading sessions, while regional desks in Erbil and Basra registered fractional gains of 50 dinars per $100.

In Baghdad, licensed exchange shops and retail desks posted dollar cash selling quotes at 169,500 dinars per $100 against purchase bids of 168,500 dinars, reflecting persistent upward pressure in parallel liquidity channels.

In Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan Region, counters listed selling rates at 168,550 dinars per $100 with purchase transactions accepted at 168,000 dinars. Across the southern port province of Basra, foreign exchange desks closed the morning session at a selling price of 168,750 dinars per $100 against buying offers of 168,250 dinars.

The current parallel figures sustain a pronounced gap above the official statutory cash rate mandated by the Central Bank of Iraq, which remains benchmarked at 152,000 dinars per $100.

This continuous premium highlights elevated demand for physical banknotes among local commercial importers navigating foreign trade settlements outside the central electronic clearance window.

World.title: 'State-sponsored terrorism': Mamata Banerjee demands release of CJP's Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister

on Monday accused the government of perpetrating âstate-sponsored terrorismâ and âpolice-sponsored atrocitiesâ as she demanded the release of Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka.

The CJP duos judicial custody was extended by two days in a case linked to the alleged trespassing at Jantar Mantar in Delhi.

In a post on X, Banerjee alleged that the authorities were deliberately extending the duo's custody and accused those in power of using a âdangerous virusâ to attack democracy. She also condemned the alleged treatment of young protesters, invoking India's freedom struggle to argue that people would continue to resist what she described as attacks on democratic rights.

âI can understand the desperate motive to extend the custody of Ashutosh and Saurav. This is a dangerous virus being used on a daily basis to attack democracy. Stop torturing the boys and girls of Gen Z. Those in power today, will not be in power tomorrow,â she wrote.

âFrom Kolkata to Delhi to Mumbai - throughout the country, atrocities have reached unprecedented levels,â Banerjee added.

Drawing a parallel with the struggle against British colonial rule, the former chief minister said those who fought for India's independence had also faced atrocities but continued their fight with conviction.





âWhen our forefathers stood up to colonial rulers, they too had to face atrocities and yet they fought with conviction and valor. Let me say it clearly: this is state-sponsored terrorism. These are police-sponsored atrocities. These cannot sustain for long,â she wrote.

World.title: 400-plus Indian-origin scholars, alumni from 27 countries warn against ‘anarchy’
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Days after competing groups of Harvard-linked Indians took opposing positions on protests against the Election Commission, more than 400 Indian-origin students, researchers and alumni associated with universities across 27 countries have issued a statement warning against efforts to erode public trust in constitutional institutions and attempts to replace democratic debate with street confrontation.

Titled âSpare India from Anarchyâ, the statement carries 402 names, including individuals linked to Harvard, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), Oxford, Cambridge, Stanford, Princeton, Yale and Columbia universities, as well as the London School of Economics, National University of Singapore and University of Toronto.

The signatories allege that âa frenzy of election denialâ and a preference for âstreet over Sansadâ have taken hold in some quarters.

They argue that unfavourable election results are being used to question electoral procedures, adverse court rulings to cast doubts on judicial independence and even the armed forces are being drawn into partisan debate.

âAn unconscionable and devious plan of sowing seeds of doubt in Indian democracy has been hatched,â the statement claims, accusing unspecified groups of turning matters before courts into campaigns on the streets.





The intervention follows a public disagreement among Harvard affiliates over the October 10 protests in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. A group of around 100 Harvard-linked signatories criticised alleged police excesses and detentions, while 44 others subsequently warned against attacks on the credibility of constitutional institutions.

The latest appeal widens that dispute beyond Harvard, though it does not name the Election Commission, the SIR exercise or the Delhi protests explicitly.

Invoking BR Ambedkarâs warning about the âgrammar of anarchyâ, the statement says dissent remains essential to democracy but should not become a cover for undermining its institutions. It calls for resolving differences through âdebate, discussion, dialogue and dissentâ within the constitutional framework.

World.content:
Manipur CM condemns âkilling of innocent civiliansâ as security forces launch combing operation

Combing operation launched, helicopters deployed

NDA MLAs condemn killings

Fresh violence follows deadly clash in Thoubal

Manipur chief minister Y Khemchand Singh on Monday condemned the killing of three civilians by suspected militants in the border area of Imphal East and Kangpokpi districts and directed officials to strengthen security in vulnerable areas of the state.The three victims were among a group of Meitei villagers collecting firewood in a forest when unidentified gunmen opened fire on them, officials said.Three others were injured and three people were reported missing.The attack triggered protests in Imphal, where demonstrators placed two bodies outside the chief minister's residence. Police fired tear gas shells to disperse the protesters.Singh chaired a security review meeting attended by home minister Govindas Konthoujam, chief secretary Rajeev Singh Thakur, security advisor Kuldiep Singh, director general of police Mukesh Singh and senior officers from the Army, Assam Rifles, CRPF, BSF and other security agencies.An official statement said the meeting reviewed the state's overall security situation and discussed the previous day's incident in Thoubal district and the latest attack in Imphal East.The chief minister âstrongly condemned the killing of innocent civilians by armed miscreants at Nongshum in Imphal East districtâ, the statement said.Security forces launched a combing operation in the Sunurok hills of Kangpokpi district following the attack, deploying sniffer dogs and drones to search the area.Helicopters were also being used for surveillance, news agency ANI reported.Additional director general of police (law and order) Lhari Dorjee Lhatoo said unidentified militants opened fire at around 9.40 am on a group of villagers cutting and transporting firewood near Sunurok hills under Sagolmang police station.âThree individuals died in the incident while three more sustained injuries and they are now under medical care,â Lhatoo said.A joint team comprising police, CRPF, CoBRA, Assam Rifles and BSF personnel was conducting the operation, he added. Mobile checkposts had also been established, while security agencies were closely monitoring the situation.âPolice, in close coordination with CRPF, BSF, Army, Assam Rifles and other sister security agencies, is working continuously to maintain law and order, and to prevent further escalation,â Lhatoo said.He assured the public that strict action would be taken against those responsible and appealed to people to exercise restraint.Singh later visited the injured at a private hospital and assured them that the state government would cover their medical expenses.The chief minister subsequently chaired a meeting of National Democratic Alliance (NDA) legislators at the chief minister's Secretariat.In a social media post, Singh said the legislators had unanimously condemned the killings and demanded the immediate arrest of those responsible.âThe legislators unanimously condemned the killings of three civilians in the strongest terms. They demanded that police and security forces apprehend the perpetrators of the crime immediately,â he said.Protests also erupted at Khwairamband Ima market in Imphal following the attack, with heavy security deployed in the area.The killings came a day after violence in Manipur's Thoubal district left one person dead and several others injured in clashes between two communities.The confrontation reportedly took place during a musical programme at Cherapur in Khangabok.District authorities imposed prohibitory orders in the affected areas, restricting residents from leaving their homes. A few houses and vehicles were also set on fire.The deceased was identified as Laishram Rakesh Singh, who was reportedly struck by a stone during the clashes. Villagers subsequently blocked National Highway 2, demanding justice and action against those involved in his death.In a separate social media post, Singh said he had met representatives of a Joint Action Committee formed over Rakesh's killing.The committee submitted a memorandum raising concerns about the case, and the chief minister assured its members that their demands would be examined and appropriate action taken under the law.

World.title: 'Feeling strong?' Abhijeet Dipke targets PM Modi after Das & Ranka's judicial custody extended, shares photo
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday after the judicial custody of

and Ashutosh Ranka was extended by two more days, accusing the government of using state machinery to intimidate young protesters.

In a video shared on social media, Dipke questioned the Prime Minister's leadership and praised Das and Ranka for remaining defiant despite spending five days in judicial custody.

"You must be feeling very strong keeping a 26-year-old Saurav Das in jail. You must be feeling very strong beating children on the streets. You must be feeling very strong putting up barricades across Delhi and dragging students on the streets," he said.

Dipke claimed that Das and Ranka had gone to Jantar Mantar to wave the national flag but were sent to judicial custody. He also alleged that their court hearings had been repeatedly postponed. "Is this strength? Hiding behind the police, hiding behind the courts, is this Narendra Modi's strength?" he asked.

"Do you feel like a very powerful Prime Minister by keeping them in jail? You are just a coward," Dipke added.

Then, praising Das for remaining composed despite his detention, Dipke said the young protester had previously admitted that he would struggle to spend even a day in jail.





"After spending five days in jail, the same Saurav Das, who himself thought he would not be able to survive even a single day in jail, walks into court on the fifth day with a smile," he said.

"And even when he learns that his judicial custody has been extended, he is not afraid. That is strength," he added. Dipke had also shared a photo of Das smiling as he appeared in court.



Meanwhile, continuing in his video statement, Dipke also praised Ranka and the families of both protesters for refusing to give in to fear.

Recalling a conversation with Das's mother, he said she had told him, "I know he will be fine. He won't break so easily."

He further accused the government of attempting to silence dissent through arrests and intimidation, insisting that such measures would not deter young protesters. "Mr Modi, I'm sorry to say this, none of us are scared of you. And none of us is going to remain silent," he said.

World.title: Cyber unit flags rise in social media fraud using deepfake videos of PM, ministers to promote fake schemes
World.content:
Deceptive s on Facebook and Instagram impersonate well-known public figures, including the Prime Minister.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit (NCTAU) under the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) has flagged a rise in financial fraud through deceptive s on Facebook and Instagram that impersonate well-known public figures, including the Prime Minister, finance ministers and chief ministers, to promote fake govt schemes.âVictims are asked to pay purported fees or taxes to receive the benefits of these fake schemes. In some cases, s offer fake cashback rewards through scratch-cards or spin-and-win contests, tricking victims into approving UPI collect requests from fraud merchants and transferring money to fraudsters,â the NCTAU warned on Monday.Ads, majorly on meta platforms featuring manipulated/deepfake videos ostensibly show the public figures announcing and promoting a welfare scheme allegedly intended to provide financial assistance to the needy. The s listing phone numbers either offer financial assistance under a purported welfare scheme or cashback/rewards through scratch-card or spin-and-win offers.Victims are either directed to a phone number/WhatsApp chat or redirected to a fraudulent website through the  in order to claim the funds/benefits of the purported scheme. In many instances, victims receive calls from international numbers, largely Pakistan-based (+92 numbers), claiming that they have been randomly selected to receive the alleged funds.Victims are redirected to a website and are coerced to make repeated payments under the pretext of taxes, processing fees, registration charges, verification fees or other administrative expenses in order to receive the funds and benefits.Victims make multiple payments and suffer substantial cumulative financial losses. In some instances, the victims are redirected to a payment app and induced to enter their transaction PIN on the pretext of receiving the prize money. The transaction, however, results in money being debited from the victimâs account and gets transferred to the perpetrator.NCTAU has asked users to check details of welfare schemes on the official website of the concerned department, before acting on social media s. They have been asked to verify the purpose and recipient of any fee or payment requested in connection with a welfare benefit, as well as identities of the persons claiming to represent the govt, through official channels.âBefore approving a UPI collect request or entering a UPI PIN, check the transaction detailsâ¦ A UPI PIN is used to authorise payments, not to receive money,â cautioned NCTAU.

World.title: 'Smiles on their faces, spirits unbroken': Dipke's first reaction after court extends judicial custody of Das, Ranka
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday shared a picture of group leaders Ashutosh Ranka and

after a court

their judicial custody by two days.

"Ashu and Saurav's first crime was waving the Tiranga at Jantar Mantar. Their second crime? Refusing to back down. Even after five days in jail, they walked into court with smiles on their faces, their spirits unbroken," Dipke wrote on X, sharing a photo of Ranka and Das being brought to court.

The duo was taken into custody on October 13 after they and some CJP supporters entered Jantar Mantar, a day after Delhi Police denotified the venue as the capital's designated protest site and identified three alternative venues for demonstrations in the city.

NEW DELHI: India on Monday issued an advisory for its citizens residing in Italy after protests over the rising cost of living broke out into violent clashes in Milan.In a social media post on X, Indian embassy in Italy advised Indian nationals to exercise caution and avoid crowded areas and locations where protests are taking place."There were protests and demonstrations last week in some Italian cities," the embassy said."We advise Indian nationals to exercise caution, avoid crowded areas & locations where protests are taking place and follow local news about such events," it added.It also issued emergency helpline numbers for its embassy in Rome and the consulate general of India in Milan."In case of any emergency, Indian nationals can contact: Embassy of India, Rome: +39 331 614 2085 , Consulate General of India, Milan: +39 3881647527," it said.This comes after more than 5,000 people gathered in Milan over the weekend.Police deployed tear gas and water cannons after protesters threw paving stones, bins and chairs at officers.Meanwhile, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is set to hold an emergency security meeting on Monday. World.content:
Union home minister Amit Shah will pay homage to the police martyrs by laying a wreath at the memorial, besides addressing the event.

NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah will on Wednesday mark the Police Commemoration Day, observed on October 21 every year, by paying homage to the police martyrs at the National Police Memorial.He will also flag off a motorcycle rally of about 90 police riders from Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi)Central Armed Police Forces (CRPF, CISF, BSF, SSB, ITBP and NSG) and some Central Police Organisations (RPF, NDRF and NIA). This is part of a nationwide rally themed on âFight Against Drugsâ, wherein police riders from all states/UTs and Central Forces would reach Ekta Nagar, Gujarat to join the Ekta Parade on Octoberober 31, 2026.The Police Commemoration Day is celebrated in honour of ten valiant policemen who laid down their lives on October 21, 1959, in an ambush laid by heavily armed Chinese troops at Hot Springs, Ladakh. In recognition of the sacrifices made by police personnel and their paramount role in preserving national security and integrity, the Prime Minister dedicated the National Police Memorial (NPM), Chanakyapuri, New Delhi to the nation on Police Commemoration Day 2018.On October 21, an event will be organised at the National Police Memorial, New Delhi, where a joint parade of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Delhi Police would be held. The home minister will preside over the function, to be attended by retired DGs, officers from the police fraternity and other dignitaries.Shah will pay homage to the police martyrs by laying a wreath at the memorial, besides addressing the event.As part of the remembrances, CAPFs/CPOs will organise various commemorative events at NPM from October 22 to 30, which will include visits of family members of martyrs, police band display, motorcycle rallies, Run for Martyrs, blood donation camps, essay/painting competitions for children and display of video films showcasing sacrifice, valour and services of police personnel. Similar programmes will be organised simultaneously by all the police Forces across the country.

World.title: Jaishankar welcomes UAE’s Foreign Minister Al Nahyan in Mumbai
World.content:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar expressed his delight in welcoming UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan at Mumbai airport on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) ahead of their upcoming bilateral talks.

“Delighted to welcome DPM & FM UAE @ABZayed to Mumbai. Look forward to our talks,” said Mr. Jaishankar in his social media post

Delighted to welcome DPM & FM UAE @ABZayed to Mumbai. Look forward to our talks. 🇮🇳 🇦🇪 https://t.co/uZxsao6hBe — Dr. S. Jaishankar (@DrSJaishankar) October 19, 2026

Deputy Prime Minister of the United Arab Emirates Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan landed in Mumbai on Monday (October 19) evening for a two-day visit expected to focus on further enhancing bilateral ties in key areas of trade, energy and defence.

PM Al Nahyan, who is also the UAE's Foreign Minister, will hold wide-ranging talks with External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Tuesday (October 20).

The two Foreign Ministers are also expected to deliberate on the overall situation in West Asia, including the recent attacks on Saudi Arabia.

The leader of the influential Gulf nation was received at the airport by Maharashtra's Skill Development Minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha.

"This high-level visit reflects the close and regular engagement between India and UAE, and will further strengthen our Comprehensive Strategic Partnership," External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on social media.

Mr. Jaiswal said on Friday (October 16, 2026) that the two sides will assess and advance initiatives in energy, trade and investment, fintech, defence, and connectivity.

With inputs from PTI

World.title: West Bank on verge of 'explosion': senior Palestinian official
World.content:
Israeli settler attacks risk setting off an "explosion" in the occupied West Bank, a senior Palestinian leader told AFP, while urging that the response remain peaceful.

Also Read: Israeli settlers burn olive trees, injure journalist in West Bank attack

Jibril Rajoub, the secretary general of the central committee of the Palestinian Authority's ruling Fatah faction, said he called for "peaceful confrontation" as he took part in meetings in Cairo with other Palestinian movements, including Gaza-based rival Hamas, which led the October 7, 2023 attacks against Israel.

"The terrorism carried out by the army and settlers, under the supervision of the Israeli government... is a prelude to a coming reaction and explosion," Mr. Rajoub told AFP in Cairo.

But he said that a "peaceful, nonviolent struggle is a necessity and a strategic choice for all Palestinians".

"Bloodshed is no longer an acceptable option," he said, calling for "peaceful confrontation with the occupation, despite the crimes it commits".

Settlers have carried out daily physical attacks, thefts and other attacks against Palestinians, with the violence intensifying in the run-up to the October 27 elections, in which Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, governing with the fiercely pro-settlement far-right, is seeking a new mandate.

Violence has picked up as extremist settlers seek to stop the Palestinian olive harvest, an annual season with cultural resonance for the community.

More than 500,000 Israelis live in West Bank settlements, which are considered illegal under international law, surrounded by around three million Palestinians.

The talks in Cairo came after Palestinian leader Mahmoud Abbas, who has ruled since 2005, delayed elections slated to start next month until September 2027.

Mr. Rajoub said the talks called for "unified political representation" with the principle of a "single authority" and "only one legitimate armed force".

Hamas took over Gaza in 2007, dividing the two Palestinian territories. Israel has vowed to obliterate Hamas after the October 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day in Israel's history. The Hamas attack resulted in 1,221 deaths.

At least 1,125 Palestinians have died in the West Bank since October 2023, mostly by the Israeli military, according to an AFP tally based on Palestinian Health Ministry figures.

Settler attacks have killed 23 Palestinians in that timeframe, according to the United Nations.

Palestinian attacks have killed at least 49 Israelis in the same period, according to Israeli figures.

In Gaza, the Israeli offensive has killed 74,459 Palestinians since October 2023, according to figures from the Health Ministry run under Hamas. The United Nations generally considers the figures reliable.

World.title: Sudan drone attacks kill three children in Khartoum, dozens of civilians in Kordofan
World.content:
A rare drone attack on Sudan’s capital killed three children Monday (October 19, 2026), a rights group said, as both sides in the country’s war step up airstrikes that have killed dozens of civilians in the Kordofan region in recent days.

Also Read: More than 300 children killed or injured in Sudan war in 6 months, UNICEF says

The strike, which the group blamed on Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces, killed children aged two, four and six in Imtidad Nasser, a neighbourhood east of Khartoum’s airport. The RSF has been at war with the Sudanese military for more than three years.

Sayed Mustafa, a resident of the area, told The Associated Press he saw a drone flying toward the airport and heard anti-aircraft fire engage it.

“Shortly after, the drone went down, and we heard an explosion near the airport,” Mr. Mustafa said.

Emergency Lawyers, a group that tracks violence against civilians in Sudan’s war, condemned the attack, calling it a humanitarian tragedy and a “serious violation” that requires investigation and accountability.

There was no immediate comment from the RSF.

According to the group, the Sudanese military struck West Kordofan province with drones in a separate attack over the weekend, bombing a market in al-Muglad on Saturday (October 17) and striking the Al-Dabab area, also in West Kordofan, on Sunday, killing dozens of civilians, including women and children. It called the attacks violations of international humanitarian law.

Sudan’s war began in April 2023, when simmering tensions between the military and the RSF exploded into open fighting in Khartoum and spread across the country.

The conflict has killed at least 59,000 people, according to conflict monitor ACLED, though aid groups say the true toll is likely higher.

About 13 million people have been displaced from their homes, according to U.N. figures, creating what aid groups call the world’s largest humanitarian crisis.

Across Sudan, 33.7 million people, including 17.3 million children, urgently need aid this year. An estimated 825,000 children face severe acute malnutrition, according to the U.N.

The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC), a global hunger monitor, warned last week that conflict and drought are worsening food insecurity in Darfur and Kordofan, where two displacement camps recorded malnutrition levels above famine thresholds.

The United States on Friday (October 16) urged the U.N. Security Council to push for a humanitarian truce and expand an arms embargo on Sudan, but China and Russia opposed widening the embargo.

World.title: Naveen Patnaik questions Odisha government’s 'silence' on Andhra's poll notification for disputed Kotia villages
World.content:
BJD president Naveen Patnaik on Monday (October 19, 2026) demanded to know whether the BJP's "dependence" on NDA ally TDP was the reason for the state government's "silence" on Andhra Pradesh issuing a notification for panchayat elections in three villages of Kotia in Koraput district.

The decades-old dispute involves both Odisha and Andhra Pradesh claiming their right over 21 of the 28 villages of Kotia Gram Panchayat. The matter has been pending before the Supreme Court, with a fresh suit filed by Odisha in January 2022 still under consideration.

In the face of the opposition's charge of "double standards" and reneging on Odisha's territorial integrity and pride, state minister Suresh Pujari said the BJP government was prepared to "thwart any provocative attempts" by TDP-ruled Andhra Pradesh.

Mr. Patnaik, who is also the leader of the opposition in the Odisha Assembly, sent a letter to Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, expressing concern over Andhra Pradesh's notification announcing polls in Phagunasineri, Ganjeipadar and Phatusineri villagers of Kotia gram panchayat.

"What happened to the BJP's assurances that Kotia belongs to Odisha? What makes this even more troubling is that the Telugu Desam Party, which governs Andhra Pradesh, is a crucial ally of the BJP-led NDA government at the Centre," the former Chief Minister said.

He asked if "political dependence is the reason for the silence of the BJP government in Odisha and its willingness to compromise with the state's interests and territorial integrity?"

"What were the recommendations of the 16-member high-level Kotia Committee constituted in 2025? What actions have been taken to implement them?” Mr. Patnaik posed the question and pointed out that as Chief Minister, he had fought all along to protect Odisha's territorial integrity.

He reminded the Chief Minister that BJP leaders in Odisha have repeatedly asserted that Kotia belongs to the state and they had raised the "Go Back Andhra" slogan.

Also, before the 2024 elections, the BJP made a promise that a 'double-engine’ government would resolve the Kotia issue once and for all, safeguarding Odisha's territorial integrity and restoring Odia pride, Mr. Patnaik said in the letter to the Chief Minister.

"What happened to those promises? Despite Odisha having a so-called double-engine government, it is deeply concerning that Andhra Pradesh has proceeded to announce elections in Kotia," he said in the letter.

"Will the double-engine government stand firm in safeguarding Odisha's territorial integrity and constitutional rights, or will it once again yield to pressure from the Centre?,” he posed and said that the people of Odisha deserve clear answers and accountability.

Meanwhile, Odisha Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari on Sunday (October 18) had said that the government is fully prepared to "thwart any provocative attempts by the neighbouring state".

"Kotia gram panchayat is an integral part of Odisha and its people are with the state," he had said, adding that the Revenue Divisional Commissioner of the southern division has been asked to take stock of the situation and remain vigilant.

The Koraput district collector has been taking stock of the situation, and both officers have been asked to make sure Kotia doesn't become a part of Andhra Pradesh's election process, the minister said.

Congress Legislature Party Leader Rama Chandra Kadam, who is also an MLA from Koraput district, demanded immediate intervention of the state government. "The Odisha BJP government's double standards on Kotia have allowed Andhra Pradesh to make its claim over the region," he alleged.

The dispute over the Kotia cluster of villages reached the Supreme Court in 1968, which directed both states to maintain the status quo. In 2006, the apex court ruled that such inter-state boundary disputes are best resolved by Parliament under Article 131 of the Constitution.

A fresh original suit filed by Odisha remains under consideration of the top court since January 2022.

World.title: Kuki group announces shutdown of key Manipur highway after attacks on villages
World.content:
A Kuki organisation in Manipur on Sunday (October 18, 2026) announced a “total shutdown” of National Highway 202 for four days to protest the continuing violence and the “absence of a credible security arrangement”.

NH-202, also called the Imphal-Ukhrul road, was a key alternative route when National Highway-2, Manipur’s lifeline, was closed to certain communities after the ethnic conflict between the Kuki-Zo and Meitei people erupted in May 2023. These highways reopened for passenger and goods movement from the second week of August.

The shutdown call by the Working Committee of Kuki Civil Society Organisations (WCKCSO), from Sunday (October 18, 2026) midnight to Thursday (October 22, 2026) midnight, followed a series of attacks on villages near the India-Myanmar border in Manipur’s Kamjong district. At least one person, a Kuki villager, and several others were injured, and at least 15 houses were torched in attacks that continued till Saturday (October 17, 2026) night.

Also Read: One dead, several injured in clashes in Manipur's Thoubal district, prohibitory orders clamped

The WCKCSO accused Naga extremists, specifically the Isak-Muivah faction of the National Socialist Council of Nagalim, of attacking Chassad and other Kuki villages near the Myanmar border. It also said the attacks in Kamjong and Ukhrul districts were carried out near bases or camps of the security forces.

“The governments of Manipur and India must abandon hollow assurances and demonstrate their resolve through decisive, on-ground action before another innocent civilian is killed. All operations must remain lawful and intelligence-led, targeting armed cadres and their operational infrastructure rather than civilians solely on the basis of their community identity,” it said in a statement on Sunday (October 18, 2026).

Blame game

Naga organisations, on the other hand, accused Kuki armed groups, including the Myanmar-based Kuki National Army-Burma, of attacking Naga villages. They said at least three Tangkhul Naga civilians were injured in such an attack at Kamjong, the district headquarters, on Saturday (October 17, 2026).

The injured, identified as T. Chithung, S. Malung and M. Shithung, were admitted to a local hospital.

Meanwhile, the Manipur government replaced Tholu Rocky with Jay Barange as the Superintendent of Police of Kamjong district. In an order on Sunday (October 18, 2026), the government transferred Mr. Rocky to the Manipur Police Training Centre in Imphal East district.

The Manipur Naga Youth Organisation condemned the State authorities for transferring Mr. Rocky, allegedly at the insistence of Kuki MLA Kimneo Hangsing. The organisation alleged that Ms. Hangsing urged Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh to transfer Mr. Rocky as he was a Naga, while “turning a blind eye” to Kuki police personnel allegedly involved in the May 13 Konsakhul (Kangpokpi district) kidnapping and killings.

“The Nagas have long endured the State administration’s law and order failure in the hope of an early return of peace and normalcy, but the present government appears (to be) appeasing only the troublemakers,” the organisation said.

World.title: Kolkata Metro services disrupted for around 1 hour due to technical glitch
World.content:
Kolkata Metro services on the North-South corridor were disrupted for around an hour on Monday (October 19, 2026) evening due to a technical glitch, officials said.

The disruption came at a time when large numbers of people use the Metro to visit Durga Puja pandals across the city on Maha Ashtami.

The technical problem occurred at Mahanayak Uttam Kumar station in Tollygunge around 5.31 p.m., following which truncated services were run in both directions between Maidan and Dakshineswar stations, they said.

The issue was resolved, and services were restored along the entire stretch of the Blue Line at 6.23 p.m., they added.

World.title: Man City star Guehi says taking the knee has lost impact after opting against anti-racism gesture
World.content:
Manchester City defender Marc Guehi believes the gesture of footballers taking the knee before matches might have lost its impact and wants to see more done in the sport's fight against racism.

Also read: The big blot on the beautiful game | On racism in football

Guehi, who is Black, didn't take the knee prior to kickoff in City's home game against Ipswich in the Premier League on Saturday (October 17, 2026) in the first of two rounds of games dedicated to the competition's “No Room For Racism” campaign.

It isn't the first time Guehi refused to perform the gesture, which was introduced in June 2020 to show support for the Black Lives Matter campaign. Since the start of the 2022-23 season, the Premier League has decided against taking the knee ahead of every match, with players instead invited to do so on certain occasions each season.

Speaking Monday (October 19) at a news conference the day before City's Champions League match against AEK Athens, Guehi said it was “great” that the Premier League's anti-racism campaign was continuing.

“Whether more can be done — more can always be done,” he said. “We have to see how we can move the campaign along.

“I don't think it's necessarily a football issue. I think it's a wider societal issue and football is that beacon of hope to try to get the message out. But whether more can be done, we will try, hopefully with the PFA [English footballers union], with the league.”

Asked whether taking the knee had lost its meaning, Guehi said: “Maybe. I haven't been taking the knee for a while now, to be honest. I'd always clap, just because of what that actually signifies.”

Guehi didn't go into more detail about his reasons for not taking the knee.

Another player not performing the gesture at the weekend was Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who stood while his teammates and opposition players for Manchester United knelt.

“Dom is more or less like, No, I don't go down. I show my respect by standing up, more or less,'” Leeds manager Daniel Farke said after the match, in which Calvert-Lewin scored in a 1-1 draw.

“I think each individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way.”

In 2021, Wilfried Zaha — a Black player who was at Crystal Palace at the time — said he would no longer be taking the knee, describing the gesture as “degrading.”

“I feel like taking a knee is degrading,” Zaha was quoted by The Guardian newspaper as telling the FT Business of Football conference. “Growing up, my parents just let me know that I should just be proud to be black, no matter what, and I just think we should stand tall.

“I think the meaning behind the whole thing is becoming something that we just do now. That's not enough."

Premier League CEO Richard Masters said the current "No Room For Racism" initiative, which comes during the U.K.'s Black History Month, intends to use “the reach of our players to send an important message: we are united in the fight against racism.”

World.title: Donald Trump rallies on Republican turf as midterm fears mount
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump heads to Kansas on Monday (October 19, 2026) to open a seven-state campaign blitz through territory he carried in 2024, as dismal polls and unexpectedly tight races in Republican strongholds stoke fears of sweeping Democratic gains in November’s midterms.

With 15 days until the November 3 vote, Mr. Trump’s rally on the outskirts of Wichita aims to shore up Senator Roger Marshall, who is locked in a dead heat with a Methodist megachurch pastor.

Mr. Trump won Kansas by 16 percentage points just two years ago, and the state has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932.

Yet analysts now rate it a “toss-up,” and a key fundraising group for Republican senators has diverted money from North Carolina to defend a seat it once took for granted.

The University of Virginia’s Center for Politics said it hesitated before moving deeply conservative Kansas into “toss-up” category -- its most competitive -- but was swayed by signs that a “full-on Republican rescue operation appears underway for Marshall.”

Control of Congress may hinge on such races, with Republicans holding slender majorities in both chambers, and Democrats needing a net gain of just four seats to capture the Senate.

Soaring costs

Over the coming six days, Mr. Trump will follow Kansas with rallies in the Carolinas, Iowa, Florida, Georgia and Michigan. All seven states backed him in 2024, though his margins in Michigan, Georgia and North Carolina were narrow.

The schedule suggests the aim is less to win over undecided voters than to fire up loyal supporters, many of whom stay home when he is not on the ballot.

Two stops, North Carolina and Iowa, are damage control in Republican-held seats, and many national party officials have all but written off North Carolina.

Elsewhere, the party is on the offensive, targeting a Democratic-held seat in Michigan, though it has struggled to make headway in Georgia.

Vice President J.D. Vance is campaigning separately in North Carolina, in Ohio and in Nebraska, where the sitting Republican senator is fending off a strong challenge from an independent.

A Washington Post-ABC News-Ipsos survey published on Sunday (October 18) put Mr. Trump’s approval rating at 33%, the lowest of either of his terms in that poll, with 66% disapproving. An NBC News poll released the same day had him at 34%.

Asked which party they would back for Congress, likely voters favored Democrats by eight points in the Post-ABC poll, and registered voters by 10 points in NBC’s.

The figures point to a possible Democratic wave, although national polls do not translate neatly into seats, particularly after partisan redistricting, and they can miss by several points in either direction.

Headwinds

The economy has become a heavy liability for a president who promised to bring prices down.

Fuel costs have soared since the United States went to war with Iran and tariffs have added to the strain on consumers, especially farmers in agricultural states such as Iowa and Kansas.

Even immigration, still Mr. Trump’s best-rated issue, is drawing a backlash, with 56% in the Post-ABC poll saying his deportation campaign has gone too far.

Democrats are turning that discontent into campaign cash. Third-quarter filings showed their Senate candidates far outraising Republicans in Ohio, Iowa and other key races.

Just over nine million votes have already been cast nationwide, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab.

In Texas, where early voting began on Monday (October 19), Democrat James Talarico raised about $64 million, a record quarter for a Senate candidate, and more than triple Republican Ken Paxton’s $18 million.

In House races, at least 47 Republican incumbents were outraised by Democratic or independent challengers, according to Punchbowl News.

Republicans are relying on outside groups to close the gap, bankrolled in part by Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, who has given some $366 million this election cycle, including $158 million to Paxton.

In the face of the multiple headwinds facing Republicans, Senator James Lankford refused to accept on Sunday (October 18) that a bad election night was inevitable.

“Only God knows what actually will happen,” the Oklahoma conservative told NBC. “Elections are about who actually shows up and votes.”

World.title: Govt slashes petrol price by Rs5.16 per litre, high-speed diesel rate by Rs7.69
World.content:
The government on Monday cut the price of petrol by Rs5.16 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.69.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs381.14 per litre while HSD will cost Rs389.27 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 20 (Tuesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: CDF Munir, new Saudi envoy express satisfaction at progress made under Makkah defence pact: ISPR
World.content:
The new Saudi envoy in Pakistan, Dr Rajeh Tami Albugamy, met with Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on Monday, with both sides expressing satisfaction over the progress made under the trilateral Makkah defence agreement, according to the military’s media wing.

Albugamy assumed his diplomatic responsibilities in Islamabad last Thursday, reaffirming the commitment to strengthening the strategic and fraternal ties between the two countries.

Inter-Service Public Relations (ISPR) said in a statement on Monday that the ambassador called on CDF Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi. According to the statement, matters of mutual interest and regional security dynamics were discussed.

“Both the dignitaries expressed satisfaction over the progress made under the framework of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement and underscored the importance of strengthening defence collaboration, institutional linkages and strategic coordination,” the statement read.

CDF Munir congratulated the ambassador on his appointment and expressed confidence that his tenure would further strengthen the longstanding fraternal ties between Islamabad and Riyadh, which are “rooted in shared faith, mutual trust and strategic partnership”.

Last week, Albugamy met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.

PM Shehbaz reaffirmed Pakistan’s support for Saudi Arabia in safeguarding its “sovereignty, security and territorial integrity” amid a recent escalation in Houthi attacks during their meeting.

DPM Dar, meanwhile, underscored longstanding fraternal and strategic ties between Islamabad and Riyadh when he met Albugamy. He also reaffirmed Islamabad and Riyadh’s “shared commitment to further strengthen bilateral cooperation for mutual progress and prosperity”.

Islamabad and Riyadh have signed two defence pacts aimed at collective deterrence, the Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement between the two and the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance that also includes Turkiye.

Earlier this month, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye convened an emergency meeting under the Makkah alliance and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom.

While the statement did not specifically name any threat, the development came against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

The Makkah defence pact , signed on Aug 7, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empower its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

In an interview aired on Sunday, the military’s spokesman said Pakistan is providing “whatever support is needed” to defend Saudi Arabia amid attacks by Yemen’s Houthi rebels against the kingdom.

World.title: Senate approves bill seeking blue passports for ex-lawmakers with incomplete term
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Senate on Monday passed a bill that sought to allow former lawmakers to have blue passports even if they had not served a full term in the National Assembly (NA) or Senate.

In the same sitting, the House withdrew a bill seeking to allow the issuance of blue passports to dependent children under the age of 28 of ex-members of Parliament.

Official blue passports are issued to key constitutional, government and judicial office holders, senior bureaucrats and their eligible dependents, allowing them visa-free entry to 55 countries, including 22 European countries.

The bills pertaining to the blue passport were moved by Senator Abdul Qadir today.

Of them, the House passed the amendment inserting a new Section 3-A in the Passports Act, 1974, which states that “a retired parliamentarian who has taken oath as a Member of the National Assembly (MNA) or the Senate, whether for a full term or for the remainder of the term of another member, shall, on such terms and conditions as may be prescribed, be entitled to retain and use the gratis official (blue) passport issued to him or her after ceasing to hold office”.

The amendment also covers lawmakers who leave office before completing five years as an MNA or six years as a senator.

At present, blue passports are issued to those ex-parliamentarians who remained a member of either House for at least one term, according to the Passport Rules 2021.

The statement of objects and reasons of the bill approved by the Senate states that the amendment “brings parity with the privileges available to other high-ranking officials and ensures uniform treatment of persons who have served the state at the highest level”.

The bill has yet to be passed by the NA.

The second bill, which sought to amend Section 12 of the Members of Parliament (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974 to provide that “an ex-member, the spouse of the ex-member and the dependent children of the ex-member below the age of 28 years shall be entitled to a gratis official (blue) passport”, was withdrawn after opposition by treasury members in the Senate.

In July, the bill had been approved by the relevant Senate committee, with the government drawing backlash. After criticism of the bill, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry had assured that measures would be taken to ensure that the travel document was used for “only official duties” abroad and issued for a limited time in most cases.

Speaking on blue passports in the Senate, Chaudhry said the number of these official passports issued in the country had been reduced from 75,000 to 45,000 after European countries and Canada raised reservations. Around 30,000 unnecessary and inactive blue passports had been cancelled, he said.

“Security and dignity of passport is a matter of the dignity of people of Pakistan,” he remarked, noting that Pakistan also had agreements with other countries regarding blue and red passports.

He said the government had no issue with parliamentarians themselves getting blue passports but had concerns over extending the facility to their families, explaining that a large number of blue passports resulted in other countries hesitating to offer visa-free access.

He added that a bill would soon be moved to withdraw the blue passport facility available for the children of retired bureaucrats.

Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar emphasised that blue passports should be regulated as they are meant for official business.

“Let children make their own careers; respect is not built through blue passports,” he said.

He also called for ending the six-year service requirement for Senate members to obtain official passports, saying the rules should be the same for members of the Senate and the NA.

NA members became eligible for official passports after taking the oath, while senators had to complete their six-year term, he said, adding that a senator who resigned a few months before completing their term could lose eligibility for the passport.

PML-N Senator Abid Sher Ali strongly criticised the requirement of a no-objection certificate (NOC) from the interior ministry for the issuance of blue passports to parliamentarians, saying it did not exist earlier.

“Are we dacoits or terrorists that we need NOCs?” he said, terming the requirement a breach of privilege. He announced that he would move a privilege motion in this regard.

‘Assault on people’s mandate’

The Senate also witnessed a debate between the opposition and the treasury over the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Leader of the Opposition in the Senate Allama Raja Nasir Abbas termed the move an “assault on the people’s mandate”.

“You robbed the people’s votes. Your own minister said the system has collapsed,” he said, referring to comments made by Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi about the governance system in the country requiring a reset.

Speaking at the Pakistan Economic Summit in July, the interior minister had said the current “system” of governance had “collapsed”, and was fundamentally incapable of resolving the country’s problems.

The opposition leader said what happened in KP was “sheer oppression” and could have been avoided.

He also urged the government not to push people to the wall, saying, “You snatched the mandate from Bengalis and they separated. You have still not learned.”

Abbas also sought a briefing on Yemen, noting that Parliament in 2015 had passed a resolution not to be part of the conflict in the Middle Eastern country. He said he had written to the prime minister and foreign minister asking them to mediate, instead of becoming part of the conflict.

“This is a sensitive issue. Countries are economically devastated and we are going to be part of another war,” he said.

In response, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said that emergency and governor’s rule were imposed in KP via a presidential order under Articles 233 and 234 of the Constitution, and were ratified by the Senate and National Assembly.

“All steps have been taken in the interest of peace, stability and national interest,” he said.

Additional input from APP

World.title: In NA, Achakzai demands to know Sohail Afridi’s whereabouts
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly (NA) Mehmood Khan Achakzai on Monday demanded on the floor of the House that details about Sohail Afridi’s whereabouts be shared.

Afridi, who has become non-functional as the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister, has not been seen since the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in his province on Oct 11. His whereabouts remained unknown on the day governor’s rule was imposed and federal minister said a day later that he and some of his cabinet members are in preventative custody.

The PTI has also alleged the detention and arrests of several of its other members, including lawmakers and ministers.

“Afridi and six to seven other MNAs of the opposition party are missing since the proclamation of emergency and governor’s rule in KP. At least we and their families should know where they are,” Achakzai said, after he reached the NA some time after the session began.

Deputy Speaker Syed Ghulam Mustafa Shah was presiding over the proceedings and was asked by Achakzai to give him the floor.

Continuing his criticism of governor’s rule, Achakzai said, “You have attacked the assembly of a province”. He called for the issuance of production orders for missing MNAs.

The chief whip of the opposition in the NA, MNA Amir Dogar, also submitted an adjournment motion in the House, seeking production orders for six “missing” PTI MNAs: Amjad Ali Khan (NA-02), Junaid Akbar (NA-09), Fazal Muhammad Khan (NA-25), Zubair Khan (NA-42), Haji Imtiaz Ahmad Choudhry (NA-68) and Nasim Ali Shah (NA-39).

The adjournment motion referred to Rule 109, read with Rule 110, of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly, 2007. The motion termed the reported detention of Afridi, Swati, and the six MNAs “a matter of definite and urgent public importance”.

The motion said the reported detention of elected representatives holding constitutional and parliamentary offices raised serious concerns regarding the functioning of democratic institutions, the representation of the people, and the protection of the rights and privileges of elected representatives under the Constitution and applicable laws.

“This is a serious matter that warrants immediate discussion on the floor of the house,” the motion stated, requesting that the regular business of the House be adjourned to discuss the matter urgently.

It also requested the House to deliberate on the circumstances surrounding the said detentions and consider “appropriate measures” in accordance with the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly, 2007.

The NA proceedings began at 5pm, with federal ministers absent other members in low attendance. Consequently, PPP MNA Agha Rafiullah criticised the government for what he described as a lack of interest in legislation.

“You see all the front rows are empty, and not a single federal minister has turned up,” he said.

Dogar supported Rafiullah’s criticism, saying, “Rafiullah sahib, that is what we have been saying for the last three years.”

Later, Dogar pointed out the lack of quorum, and owing to the low attendance of MNAs, the deputy speaker stopped the proceedings to allow some more time for the House to be put in order.

At least 65 members are required to put the House in order or meet the quorum.

Eventually, the quorum was found complete after two counts and the proceedings resumed.

The proceedings have been adjourned until Tuesday morning.

World.title: 'We never gave up': Naqvi highlights Pakistan's peace efforts in US-Iran war at Qatar forum
World.content:
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi on Monday highlighted Pakistan’s mediation efforts between the United States and Iran, affirming that Islamabad “never gave up”.

He made the remarks while addressing the 8th Global Security Forum being held in Qatar’s capital, Doha. Convened under the title “The Future of Alliances“, the forum brings together high-ranking officials and dignitaries from over 100 nations, according to Qatar News Agency.

“The last few months have been very difficult for our region. The conflict involving Iran and the United States created serious risks not only for the Middle East, but for the entire world,” Naqvi noted.

He added that at such a critical time, Pakistan chose the path of peace and made “every possible effort to reduce tensions”.

Naqvi, who has been involved in Islamabad’s peace efforts and has made several trips to Iran since the war began, said: “There were moments when the situation was extremely tense, but we never gave up.

“We continued talking, listening and working to build trust. And I can tell you from my experience: peace is not achieved in one meeting; it requires patience, trust and continuous efforts.”

He particularly highlighted the “remarkable role” of Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir in Pakistan’s efforts to reduce tensions.

CDF Munir, accompanied by Naqvi, had visited Iran in August “as part of Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability”. The interior minister last made a visit to Iran in September, with Tehran describing the trip as part of bilateral engagements.

Speaking at the Doha forum, Naqvi recalled the June 18 signing of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Iran and the US. The 14-point MoU , which Pakistan signed as a mediator, provided a framework for ending the war that began with US-Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28.

The interior minister recalled that the MoU was followed by the Lake Lucerne Summit in Switzerland, organised by mediators Pakistan and Qatar.

“There, I saw something I will never forget,” he said, adding that Qatar’s Prime Minister Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and CDF Munir worked for “more than 16 hours without a single break”.

“No cameras, no announcements; only two men who refused to let the talks fail,” Naqvi remarked, emphasising that the only aim of the two mediating countries was to “stop further conflict and to save innocent lives”.

The minister praised Qatar’s peace efforts, noting it had “done so much”. “In the diplomacy of our time, when others chose sides, Qatar chose to keep talking. Pakistan has seen this closely because we have worked beside you.”

He stressed that Pakistan has always believed that “dialogue is better than war”.

“Our recent experience has taught us three important lessons: never close the door to dialogue, trust is the most important key for any kind of talk, and thirdly, peace requires sincere efforts from everyone.”

The senator emphasised that no single country could achieve regional peace alone.

“Pakistan is proud of the role it has played in the regional peace efforts,” he said, reaffirming that Islamabad would continue to support dialogue, peace and cooperation.

“We believe that winning peace is far more important than winning a war,” the minister remarked.

He conveyed Pakistan’s message: “We do not want credit for stopping wars. We want a future where wars do not start.”

The war between Washington and Tehran began in February with US-Israeli strikes on Iran , which responded with retaliatory attacks on nearby Gulf countries.

While diplomatic engagements continue, there has been a lack of progress in recent weeks in negotiations to end the war.

After an interim ceasefire collapsed, Iran in September presented its proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz — the key oil trade route that has remained central to the conflict.

The US said it had rejected that proposal, while Iran’s security chief said negotiations have stalled because Washington failed to address all seven conditions for reopening the strait. On Sunday, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran’s offer to the US to reopen the waterway within seven days was still on the table.

Meanwhile, the Middle East is currently facing heightened tensions on another front as Houthi rebels attack Saudi Arabia after a truce in their long-running war with Yemen’s coalition government unravelled in July.

Makkah alliance ‘not for war’

During his address, Naqvi cited the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement signed among Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in August as an example of Islamabad’s commitment to regional security.

“It is a pact for defence, not for war,” he declared, adding that no country could “enjoy lasting peace if its neighbours are facing conflicts”.

The pact , under which the three countries have formed the Makkah Defence Alliance, empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Naqvi also spoke about countering security challenges and called for stronger international cooperation on the matter.

“As Pakistan’s interior minister, I also understand the price of terrorism and insecurity. Pakistan has suffered greatly; thousands of our citizens, soldiers, and policemen have lost their lives. Even today, we continue to fight.”

Describing terrorism as a “common enemy”, he called for “stronger cooperation, better intelligence-sharing and joint efforts to defeat it”.

The senator noted that counterterrorism cooperation was not something Pakistan has only sought, but also provided. He then highlighted the country’s contributions to the United Nations’ peacekeeping missions.

“Our UN police peacekeepers have helped protect civilians, support local police and restore peace in countries affected by conflict. We are proud of their services and sacrifices,” he said.

World.title: Christiane Amanpour to leave CNN after four decades as Ellison era begins
World.content:
CNN’s chief international anchor Christiane Amanpour will leave next year, after 43 years with the network, according to an internal memo seen by Reuters on Monday.

The news channel has recently come under the ownership of Skydance, whose Chief Executive Officer David Ellison has faced criticism over his stewardship of CBS News.

“After thinking carefully for several months … I’ve decided to separate from CNN, my partner of 43 fantastic years,” Amanpour said in a video statement, joking that it was “longer than many marriages”.

She added that her daily show on CNN would conclude at the end of this year, but that she would continue hosting ‘Amanpour’ once a week through to June 2027.

Thanking her TV crew and colleagues, Amanpour highlighted that it was the “teams and the camaraderie we built that counts so much”.

Amanpour, whose first major assignment was covering the first Gulf War, went on to report on conflicts in Bosnia, Rwanda, Afghanistan, Ukraine and Iran.

Skydance, formerly Paramount Skydance, completed its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery earlier this month, bringing CNN and CBS News under one roof.

CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss kept their roles, with both reporting to Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz.

Lawmakers have criticised Ellison for tailoring news coverage at CBS News to favour US President Donald Trump.

World.title: McCullum wary of Pakistan’s home advantage as England prepare for tri-series test
World.content:
England head coach Brendon McCullum has warned his side they will need to adapt quickly to subcontinent conditions to compete against Pakistan and Sri Lanka, as the visitors prepare to face the hosts in the second match of the One-day International tri-series at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Tuesday.

McCullum acknowledged Pakistan’s familiarity with home conditions and the challenge of winning away from home, but said England were eager to test themselves against two strong opponents in a competition that will also serve as preparation for next year’s 50-over World Cup.

“Pakistan’s a very strong side,” McCullum said during a media talk on Monday. “When you come to this part of the world, you have to do things differently. Playing subcontinent teams in subcontinent conditions has its own challenges, but that’s something we’re looking forward to.”

England arrive with momentum after three consecutive ODI series victories in 2026, but the prospect of facing Pakistan on their home ground presents a different examination. The visitors will also have to contend with Sri Lanka, with the top two sides from the double round-robin stage qualifying for the Oct 31 final in Lahore.

McCullum said England wanted to be competitive against any opposition and in all conditions, rather than rely on a fixed approach.

“We don’t have any kind of binary process of how we want to go about playing,” he said. “We want to just make sure that we play what’s in front of us, adapt as quick as we can, and hopefully try and play the best cricket we can to give ourselves a chance.”
